latest.title: Generative AI in Consumer Decision Making: How Algorithmic Recommendations Shape Brand Trust
latest.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
latest.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly moving from the back end of recommendation engines to the consumer-facing interface, where conversational assistants, generated product descriptions and personalised feeds increasingly decide what shoppers see, compare and buy. While the literature on algorithm aversion and algorithm appreciation explains when consumers accept algorithmic advice, little is known about how such advice reshapes trust in the brand that deploys it. This paper develops and specifies a multi-level, testable framework in which four attributes of a GenAI recommendation (perceived personalisation, perceived accuracy and relevance, transparency and explainability, and disclosure of the AI source) influence brand trust through two opposing appraisal pathways: perceived algorithmic competence and fairness, which build trust, and perceived manipulation and privacy concern, which erode it. Brand trust in turn drives purchase intention and loyalty, with AI literacy and task type (utilitarian versus hedonic) as boundary conditions. Nine hypotheses are derived from trust theory, the persuasion knowledge model and the human–automation literature, and a dynamic trust-calibration loop is proposed in which each decision cycle updates the trust baseline used in the next. A two-study empirical design is specified, comprising a PLS-SEM survey and a 3 × 2 × 2 online experiment, and a Monte Carlo power analysis shows that a survey of about 300 respondents gives at least 95% power for the main hypothesised paths, while a 600-participant experiment gives about 92% power for medium-small effects of disclosure. latest.title: The Influence of Social Media Marketing and Brand Awareness on Purchase Decisions for Decoration Services at Catasa.id In South Tangerang
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of Social Media Marketing and Brand Awareness on purchase decisions for decoration services through Instagram @Catasa.id, both partially and simultaneously. The research used a quantitative associative approach. Data were collected through questionnaires from 106 respondents who knew or had interacted with @Catasa.id. The data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, simple and multiple linear regression, correlation, coefficient of determination, t-test, and F-test with IBM SPSS Statistics 27. The results show that Social Media Marketing has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (t = 8.361; p < 0.001), while Brand Awareness has a positive but insignificant effect (t = 0.925; p = 0.357). Simultaneously, Social Media Marketing and Brand Awareness have a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (F = 70.849; p < 0.001). The coefficient of determination is R² = 0.579, indicating that 57.9% of the variation in purchase decisions is explained jointly by the two independent variables.

latest.title: Transparency that sells: the impact of anti–pre-made dishes attitude disclosure on restaurant patronage intentions
latest.abstract: Introduction Although industrially produced pre-made (PMDs) offer convenience, their use in restaurants may conflict with consumers’ expectations of freshness and culinary craftsmanship. Drawing on signaling theory and expectancy violation theory, this study examines how restaurants’ disclosure of an anti-PMD stance influences patronage dishes through perceived moral authenticity and perceived risk, and whether these effects depend on operational transparency. Methods Four between-subjects scenario experiments were conducted in casual-restaurant contexts involving offline dining and online food delivery. Two single-factor experiments examined the effects of anti-PMD disclosure (presence versus absence), while two 2 × 2 factorial experiments further manipulated operational transparency (closed versus open kitchens). The hypotheses were tested using analysis of variance, bootstrap mediation analysis, and moderated mediation analysis. Results Anti-PMD disclosure increased patronage intention and perceived moral authenticity while reducing perceived food-related risk. Perceived moral authenticity and perceived risk mediated the relationship between disclosure and patronage intention. Operational transparency moderated these relationships: disclosure significantly influenced patronage intention and both mediators in closed-kitchen settings, whereas these effects were not significant in open-kitchen settings. The indirect effects through both mediators were also significant in closed-kitchen settings but not in open-kitchen settings. Discussion These findings clarify how food-preparation information and operational transparency jointly shape the psychological evaluations underlying consumers’ food-provider choice intentions. latest.title: Towards Sufficiency in Consumer Electronics? Consumers’ Perceptions of Longevity Strategies for Postponing Product Replacement
latest.abstract: The circular economy highlights the need to slow resource use by making products last longer. Although various longevity strategies have been proposed, it remains unclear whether consumers perceive these strategies as effective. This paper draws on literature on lifetime extension strategies and behavioural theories to investigate the extent to which consumers perceive these strategies as effective in postponing replacement. A survey of 617 consumers examined the perceived effectiveness of 13 product lifetime extension strategies across four product categories using ANOVAs. Durability and reliability emerged as the strategies perceived to be most effective. Preventing functional problems during product use is particularly important for postponing product replacement, as such problems appear to be prominent triggers for replacement. However, consumers remain unconvinced about the effectiveness of most other strategies. Correlational analyses revealed that satisfaction with lifetimes is negatively correlated with perceived strategy effectiveness, suggesting that consumers are less likely to search for lifetime-extending strategies as they do not see lifetime as a concern. These findings underscore the need for design/policy interventions to strengthen durability and enhance awareness of lifetime-extending strategies.

latest.title: Strategi Rebranding Bakpia Djava (Repositioning, Redesign, Relaunching) Dalam Mempertahankan Daya Saing Produk Oleh-Oleh Tradisional
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini menganalisis strategi rebranding Bakpia Djava dan kontribusinya dalam mempertahankan daya saing sebagai produk oleh-oleh tradisional Yogyakarta. Menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan wawancara mendalam terhadap Head Marketing dan Konsultan F&B Bakpia Djava, penelitian ini mengkaji fenomena rebranding yang dilakukan pada Juni 2025. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa rebranding didorong oleh tekanan persaingan pasar dan perubahan perilaku konsumen generasi muda di era digital. Implementasi mencakup perubahan logo menjadi lebih humanis, pergantian tagline dari "Resep Tradisional Tempo Doeloe" menjadi "Cita Rasa Tempo Doeloe", serta peluncuran tiga kategori kemasan berdasarkan strata sosial konsumen. Dampak rebranding terlihat pada peningkatan kunjungan, omset penjualan, dan penguatan keunggulan merek melalui strategi pembuktian kualitas produk. Keunikan strategi Bakpia Djava terletak pada penerapan kolaborasi kompetitif dengan kompetitor dan manajemen transisi visual yang mempertahankan logo lama untuk menjaga loyalitas pelanggan setia. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa rebranding yang memadukan pembaruan identitas visual dengan pelestarian nilai tradisional dan strategi kolaboratif efektif dalam mempertahankan daya saing produk oleh-oleh tradisional di era digital

latest.title: Examining the role of digital promotion, referral, and CRM in shaping decisions to enroll in RPL programs
latest.venue: Jurnal Ilmiah Bisnis dan Ekonomi Asia
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of digital promotion, referral, and customer relationship management (CRM) on study decisions in the Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) program at Institut Teknologi dan Bisnis ASIA Malang. A quantitative approach was employed to analyze the partial and simultaneous effects of the independent variables on prospective students’ decisions to choose the RPL program. Data were collected through questionnaires distributed to respondents associated with the RPL program and analyzed using appropriate statistical techniques. The results indicate that digital promotion has a positive and significant effect on study decisions, suggesting that accessible digital information, engaging promotional content, and clear communication can strengthen prospective students’ interest and confidence. Referral also has a positive and significant effect, indicating that recommendations from alumni, current students, family members, and colleagues can enhance trust in the RPL program. Furthermore, CRM has a positive and significant effect on study decisions, particularly through effective information services, prompt communication, consultation accessibility, and responsiveness to prospective students’ needs. These findings highlight the importance of integrating digital promotion, referral strategies, and relationship-based services to strengthen enrollment decisions in RPL programs.

latest.title: Building Trust for Second-Hand Purchase on P2P Resale Platforms: Interactive Effect of Seller-Generated Content and Relationship Norms
latest.abstract: Second-hand consumption on peer-to-peer (P2P) online platforms, as a form of extended product use, is often associated with circular economy initiatives. Yet consumer participation in these markets remains constrained by uncertainty and a lack of trust in sellers. While seller-generated content (SGC) can help build consumer trust, the specific psychological mechanisms through which different SGC types promote second-hand purchase intention remain underexplored. Drawing on relationship norms theory and signaling theory, this study differentiates competence-based trust from benevolence-based trust and explores how the interplay between SGC types and relationship norms facilitates consumers’ second-hand purchase intention via distinct trust pathways. Through three experiments, we demonstrate that seller-generated content (informational vs. emotional) and relationship norms (exchange vs. communal) interact to influence consumers’ second-hand purchase intention. Specifically, informational seller-generated content is more effective under exchange relationship norms in fostering competence-based trust and promoting purchase intention, whereas emotional seller-generated content is more effective under communal relationship norms in strengthening benevolence-based trust and driving purchase intention. These findings contribute to research on trust formation and consumer decision-making in P2P resale markets and offer practical implications for designing norm-congruent seller communication on second-hand platforms.

latest.title: Balancing budgets and emotions: The dual influence of economic and psychological factors on furniture purchase decisions during relocation
latest.abstract: Furniture purchasing is a high-involvement consumer decision, particularly during relocation, when consumers must navigate both financial and psychological considerations. Despite extensive research on consumer behaviour, limited attention has been given to how these factors jointly shape furniture purchase decisions during relocation, particularly in the Malaysian context. This exploratory study employed a quantitative research design to examine the influence of economic and psychological factors on furniture purchase decisions before relocation. Data were collected from 218 adult consumers through a structured online questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The findings show that both economic and psychological factors significantly influence consumer purchase decisions, with psychological factors emerging as the stronger predictor. This suggests that, alongside financial considerations, consumers place considerable importance on comfort, personal preferences, lifestyle compatibility, and adjustment to their new living environment. The findings extend the application of the Theory of Reasoned Action and the Theory of Planned Behaviour to relocation-related consumer behaviour and contribute to a better understanding of high-involvement purchasing during significant life transitions. Practically, the findings suggest that furniture retailers and marketers should combine affordability and flexible purchasing options with strategies that address consumers’ psychological and lifestyle needs.

latest.title: Examining the role of artificial intelligence and social media marketing activities through the brand resonance model
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractIn an era where digital technologies are rapidly transforming consumer behavior, e-commerce platforms have emerged as primary channels for purchasing goods. This shift has prompted organizations to adapt their marketing strategies to increasingly competitive digital environments, particularly by applying artificial intelligence and social media to build consumer relationships and strengthen customer-based brand equity. This study aims to examine the effects of Artificial Intelligence Marketing Activities (AIMA) and Social Media Marketing Activities (SMMA) on brand resonance, using Keller’s brand resonance model as the main theoretical framework. Data were collected through an online survey from 210 respondents in Thailand and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that both AIMA and SMMA have significant positive effects on brand salience, brand performance, and brand imagery. These constructs subsequently influence brand judgments and feelings, ultimately leading to brand resonance. The findings extend the application of the brand resonance model to the digital marketing context, contribute to a deeper understanding of how AI-driven and social media marketing can be effectively managed on digital platforms, and provide practical implications for developing marketing strategies aimed at strengthening brand equity.AcknowledgementsThe authors would like to thank all participants for their contribution to this study.

latest.title: Which review cues matter most? Perceived authenticity as the dominant predictor of purchase intention toward Indonesian local fashion brands
latest.abstract: In digital fashion markets, consumers navigate a complex landscape of online reviews, although the cues they prioritize when evaluating local brands remain poorly understood. Grounded in signalling theory and the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM), this study develops a multi-cue framework examining how review content quality, review source credibility, perceived review authenticity, and emotional tone collectively predict purchase intention toward local fashion brands. Drawing on survey data from Generation Z consumers in Indonesia analyzed through PLS-SEM, the findings reveal a signal hierarchy: perceived review authenticity consistently emerges as the dominant evaluative cue, outweighing informational and credibility-based signals alike. This pattern suggests that consumers in identity-driven consumption contexts prioritize legitimacy verification above argument evaluation, a finding that departs from prior ELM-based review research in which argument quality typically dominates. Theoretically, the study contributes to signalling theory by suggesting that signal effectiveness depends on imitation cost relative to the prevailing manipulation environment and identifies a scope condition for ELM in contexts where message authenticity cannot be presumed. Practically, local fashion brands are advised to cultivate authentic consumer narratives rather than optimizing review volume or aggregate ratings.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kredibilitas Influencer Dan Kualitas Konten Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian Produk Somethinc Pada Generasi Z Di Kota Bandung
latest.abstract: Perkembangan industri skincare di Indonesia tidak terlepas dari perubahan perilaku konsumen dalam mencari dan mengevaluasi informasi produk melalui influencer dan konten media sosial. Meskipun demikian, bukti empiris mengenai pengaruh kedua faktor tersebut terhadap keputusan pembelian produk skincare lokal, khususnya pada Generasi Z, masih terbatas. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh kredibilitas influencer dan kualitas konten terhadap keputusan pembelian produk Somethinc pada Generasi Z di Kota Bandung. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain asosiatif. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 126 responden yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Data dianalisis menggunakan analisis regresi linear berganda dengan bantuan IBM SPSS Statistics Versi 27. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kredibilitas influencer (β = 0,568; p < 0,05) dan kualitas konten (β = 0,356; p < 0,05) berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian. Secara simultan, kedua variabel juga berpengaruh signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian (F = 186,847; p < 0,05) dengan koefisien determinasi sebesar 0,752, yang menunjukkan bahwa 75,2% variasi keputusan pembelian dapat dijelaskan oleh kedua variabel tersebut. Temuan penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kredibilitas influencer merupakan faktor yang lebih dominan dibandingkan kualitas konten dalam memengaruhi keputusan pembelian. Penelitian ini memperkuat penerapan Source Credibility Theory dalam konteks pemasaran digital serta memberikan bukti empiris bahwa pemilihan influencer yang kredibel dan penyajian konten yang berkualitas merupakan strategi yang efektif dalam meningkatkan keputusan pembelian produk Somethinc pada Generasi Z di Kota Bandung

latest.title: Attention Economy and Marketing Mechanisms: A Comparison of Low- and High-Involvement Products
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: In the era of the attention economy, consumer attention has become an increasingly scarce and valuable marketing resource. With the rapid development of digital platforms and algorithmic recommendation technologies, the way firms acquire and utilize consumer attention has undergone significant changes. This paper uses a conceptual analysis examines how attention-based marketing mechanisms differ across products with different levels of consumer involvement. By integrating insights from attention-based marketing theory and consumer decision-making literature, this paper analyzes two distinct pathways through which attention is transformed into purchase behavior: low-involvement products primarily rely on attention repetition and mental availability to stimulate purchasing, while high-involvement products require deeper information processing and trust formation after attention is captured. The study further discusses how firms can allocate attention resources effectively by adopting broad attention strategies for low-involvement products and deep attention strategies for high-involvement products in the digital marketing environment. This paper contributes to a better understanding of attention allocation in marketing and provides both theoretical and practical implications for firms seeking to improve marketing effectiveness in the attention economy.

latest.title: Children’s responses to influencer advertising: examining the impact of advertising disclosure and content type
latest.abstract: Kidfluencers have become an increasingly familiar feature of children’s online viewing, raising concerns about how children process persuasive content embedded in entertainment. Drawing on the Elaboration Likelihood Model and advertising literacy, this study examines the effects of advertising disclosure and content type on children’s purchase intention, as well as the moderating role of advertising literacy. A quasi-experimental study using a 2 (disclosure vs. non-disclosure) × 3 (content type: rational, interactional, transactional) design was conducted with children aged 8–12 years using manipulated kidfluencer videos. Data were analyzed using two-way analysis of variance and moderation analysis. The results indicate that advertising disclosure had a significant effect on purchase intention. Children exposed to disclosed content reported higher purchase intention than those exposed to non-disclosed content. Content type and the interaction between disclosure and content type were not statistically significant. Advertising literacy also significantly moderated the effect of advertising disclosure on purchase intention, such that the positive effect of disclosure weakened as advertising literacy increased. These findings point to the importance of considering both disclosure practices and children’s advertising literacy when investigating responses to influencer advertising and suggest that advertising disclosure does not necessarily reduce children’s purchase intention.

latest.title: Exploring How to Optimize Enterprise Marketing Strategies in the Digital Age
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies and the proliferation of new media platforms are fundamentally transforming the retail landscape and reshaping consumer decision-making processes. In this evolving environment, conventional, mass-oriented marketing approaches are increasingly inadequate for sustaining competitive advantage in digital markets—evidenced by persistently low customer acquisition efficiency and diminishing brand resonance. This paper systematically examines enterprise-level digital marketing strategies through a dual-method approach: comprehensive literature review and in-depth case analysis. It first maps the current state of the digital marketing ecosystem, then identifies and analyzes critical implementation barriers—including organizational silos, data fragmentation, and capability gaps—that hinder effective digital marketing adoption, further clarifies the core strategic advantages of digital marketing (e.g., real-time responsiveness, audience precision, and iterative optimization) and its tangible business value, and finally proposes forward-looking, actionable recommendations aligned with emerging industry trajectories. Empirical findings indicate that sustainable marketing transformation hinges on three interdependent pillars: seamless cross-channel integration, granular data-driven operationalization, and audience-centric content innovation. These insights provide a rigorous, practice-oriented framework to guide traditional enterprises in navigating their digital marketing transformation.

latest.title: Achieving sustainable development goals through digital supply chains: The interplay between green innovation, AI adoption, and consumer preferences
latest.abstract: The research investigates the impacts of AI adoption, green innovation, consumer preferences, and infrastructure on SDG-aligned supply chain performance in the Malaysian pharmaceutical industry. Additionally, the research examines the mediating role of trust in these relationships. Resource-Based View theory and the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework are the theoretical basis of this research. A quantitative research design was utilized to collect data from 325 pharmaceutical employees in Penang, Malaysia, by conducting a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale. Data were analyzed with SPSS for Descriptive Statistics and SmartPLS for Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that all direct relationships are significant, with green innovation, AI adoption, infrastructure, and consumer preferences having positive impacts on SDG-aligned supply chain performance. Additionally, trust proves to mediate these relationships and emerges as the strongest predictor of sustainable supply chain performance. The findings add to the literature by integrating the Resource-Based View and TOE, placing green innovation and AI as strategic assets of competitive advantage. Regarding the practical insights, it is recommended that companies invest in AI-powered sustainability analytics, jointly design green products with customers, create SDG 9-based key performance indicators, and focus on building trust based on open stakeholder relations, thus creating green supply chain management initiatives. Nevertheless, the study is limited by aspects such as its cross-sectional design and a focus on the region, so future longitudinal and multi-industry studies can increase the extent of generalizability and prove causality.

latest.title: AI features and social influence affect Gen Z purchase intention and behavior through trust in an extended SOR model
latest.abstract: Driven by digital transformation in the global retail sector, this study investigates the psychological and behavioral mechanisms underlying Generation Z college students’ AI-assisted shopping experiences. It examines how four stimuli—AI algorithm transparency, user-friendliness, internet word of mouth (IWOM), and trust propensity—influence consumer trust and purchase intention, alongside the moderating effects of privacy concern and information collection behavior. Drawing on an extended Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, the research empirically validates the proposed framework using 979 valid online survey responses analyzed via SPSS 32. Results reveal that the four antecedents exert significantly positive effects on both consumer trust and purchase intention, with trust serving as a significant mediator between these antecedents and purchase intention. Additionally, information collection behavior positively moderates the relationship between IWOM and consumer trust, while privacy concern negatively moderates the relationship between AI algorithm transparency and consumer trust. This study offers novel theoretical insights into Gen Z’s AI shopping behaviors and provides practical implications: retailers should enhance AI algorithm transparency, optimize user interfaces, cultivate positive IWOM, and strengthen privacy protection to foster Gen Z’s trust and facilitate purchase conversion.

latest.title: Cognitive bias across generations: The influence of online reviews on consumer decision-making in E-commerce
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: This study examines whether purchase intentions in response to online review scenarios differ across generational cohorts. Survey data were collected from 1028 Czech online panellists grouped into Baby Boomers, Generation X, Generation Y (Millennials), and Generation Z. Participants evaluated ten fictitious reviews developed around anchoring, attribute emphasis, framing, recency, and hindsight-related cues. Kruskal–Wallis tests yielded nominally significant cohort differences for positive anchoring, design-focused attribute emphasis, positive framing, and the older-review scenario. All four omnibus effect sizes were very small (η 2 H = 0.005–0.009). Holm-adjusted Dunn comparisons identified differences between Baby Boomers and Generations Y and Z for positive anchoring, between Baby Boomers and Generation Z for design-focused attribute emphasis, and between Baby Boomers and Generation Y for the older-review scenario. No pairwise comparison for positive framing remained significant after adjustment. These findings suggest that cohort membership alone provides limited information about responses to the scenarios and does not justify generation-specific review-interface strategies. The attribute-emphasis scenarios vary substantive product information and therefore do not isolate a priming mechanism. More generally, the Czech quota sample, hypothetical purchase-intention measures, and confounded stimuli restrict generalisability and causal interpretation. The study provides exploratory descriptive evidence rather than a basis for inferring stable generational differences in susceptibility to cognitive bias.

latest.title: Marketing innovation capability, market knowledge capability, and digital marketing capability on marketing performance: The mediating role of religiocentric relational advantage
latest.abstract: This study investigates the influence of marketing innovation capability (MIC), digital marketing capability (DMC), and market knowledge capability (MKC) on marketing performance (MP), with religiocentric relational advantage (RRA) as a mediating variable. Data were collected through questionnaires with 305 leaders or owners of Muslim fashion SMEs in Indonesia. The data were processed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). These findings show that marketing innovation capability, digital marketing capability, and market knowledge capability directly influence both religiocentric relational advantage and marketing performance. Furthermore, religiocentric relational advantage also directly influences marketing performance. Religiocentric relational advantage mediates the relationship between marketing innovation capability and marketing performance. Religiocentric relational advantage also mediates the relationship between digital marketing capability and marketing performance, and between market knowledge capability and marketing performance.

latest.title: The evolution and future directions of AI in digital marketing within the banking sector
latest.abstract: The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) is changing digital marketing in the banking sector. The need to engage with consumers in a personalized, dynamic, and automated way has become a pressing requirement now that institutions that were formerly traditional, product-oriented are shifting to dynamic, customer-centric approaches. Although the field is growing rapidly in terms of technology, extensive syntheses of the new field are still in their early stages. Therefore, this study seeks to develop a systematic synthesis on the development, modern trends, and themes of AI use in digital marketing in the banking sector. Using a PRISMA-compliant systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis, a strict search was conducted in the Scopus and Web of Science databases, which returned 107 articles. After meeting the inclusion criteria, a final sample of 47 peer-reviewed journal articles, conference papers, book chapters, and review articles was selected for detailed assessment. The discussion reveals a big shift towards data-based, advanced marketing strategies. Besides, the bibliometric synthesis identifies major thematic groups that are currently prevalent in the academic world. These clusters include customer engagement, machine-learning-based customer segmentation and predictive analytics, automation and service personalization via chatbots, and advanced applications leveraging deep learning and recommendation systems. By leveraging these technologies together, banking institutions can provide more personalized communications, anticipate consumer behavior, and operate more efficiently. latest.title: Secondary Market Premiums and Impulse Buying in Concert Ticketing: The Role of Scarcity, FOMO and Institutional Regulation
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: The secondary market premium of concert tickets represents a structurally embedded flaw in live entertainment markets, and it can strongly influence consumers' impulse purchasing. With Jay Chou's "Carnival" tour as a real-world example, this article combines the perspective of scarcity theory and fear of loss (FOMO) to analyze the impact of secondary market premium on consumers' impulsive purchases. Some findings indicate that secondary market premiums enhance ticket allocation efficiency, reinforce fan-community cohesion, and incentivize organizers to expand supply. However, these premiums also generate systemic risks, including irrational overpayment, algorithmic scalping monopolies, and regulatory lag, which collectively undermine market fairness and consumer welfare. To tackle these real-world difficulties, this article uses strategies such as technical counter-control and improvement of the real-name system, price limit, and transparency in the secondary market, enhancement of the regulatory framework, and industry self-discipline. The study also reveals the double-edged effect of secondary market premiums, which helps the performance ticket market to grow sustainably and consistently.

latest.title: Decision pathways in mobile-app shopping: a Throughput Model study of online consumers
latest.abstract: Purpose Mobile shopping environments increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to personalise recommendations, curate product information and support purchase decisions. Yet, existing consumer decision-making models maintain a linear, stage-based logic that fails to capture how AI-enabled interfaces compress, extend or reconfigure the pathways consumers actually follow. This study aims to use the Throughput Model (TPM) to conceptualise and empirically validate distinct algorithmic decision pathways through which perception, information search and evaluative judgement interact to shape purchase intentions in mobile-app shopping contexts. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from Gen Z consumers with recent mobile-app shopping experience. The study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and mediation analysis to test the TPM and estimate one-step, two-step and three-step decision pathways in AI-enabled mobile commerce. Findings Perception, information search and judgement each exert significant effects within the model, with judgement emerging as the central integrative mechanism linking upstream inputs to purchase intention. These results demonstrate that AI-enabled mobile interfaces simultaneously support impulsive, efficiency-driven and deliberative decision architectures. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study provides the first empirical operationalisation of the TPM in mobile-app commerce, reconceptualising purchase decisions as coexisting algorithmic pathways rather than a single sequential route. It offers marketers a diagnostic framework for segmenting consumers by decision architecture and designing adaptive AI-enabled shopping experiences accordingly.

latest.title: Drivers of sustainable fashion purchase in India: a moderated value framework
latest.abstract: Purpose Although sustainable fashion research has extensively examined either consumer attitudes or purchase intentions, limited studies have explicitly distinguished between the cognitive foundation of attitude and the situationally driven nature of intention within the eco-fashion context. Furthermore, the interactive role of psychological traits such as altruism and mindfulness, along with economic considerations like willingness to pay a premium, in moderating the attitude–intention relationship remains underexplored, particularly in emerging markets such as India. This study aims to address these gaps by developing and empirically validating an integrated framework that captures both individual and contextual drivers of eco-fashion purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a comprehensive mixed-methods design informed by grounded theory principles, this study explores the underlying factors that shape the phenomenon. Qualitative data from interviews and FGD enabled themes to emerge inductively, while quantitative survey data validated and extended these insights. Statistical analyses examined relationships among variables, and hypotheses were tested using SEM to ensure robustness of the conceptual model. Findings Environmental consciousness, social influence and marketing stimuli considerably shape eco-fashion attitude and purchase intention, while attitude mediates these relationships. Altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay strengthen the relationship between attitude and purchase intention. Originality/value The study proposes a moderated value framework that explains sustainable fashion purchase more dynamically by treating altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay as moderators in the Indian context.

latest.title: Tác động của nỗi lo sợ bỏ lỡ và hiệu ứng đám đông đến hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng của người tiêu dùng trẻ trong mua sắm livestream: bằng chứng từ ngành thời trang Việt Nam
latest.venue: The University of Danang - Journal of Science and Technology
latest.abstract: Trong lĩnh vực livestream thời trang tại Việt Nam, hành vi ra quyết định mua của nhóm khách hàng trẻ chịu ảnh hưởng bởi các tín hiệu xã hội, đặc biệt là cảm giác sợ bỏ lỡ và xu hướng hành động theo đám đông. Dựa trên khung Kích thích – Chủ thể – Phản hồi (S-O-R), nghiên cứu kiểm định tác động của nỗi lo sợ bỏ lỡ (FoMO) và hiệu ứng đám đông đến hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng, đồng thời phân tích vai trò trung gian của trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy mua sắm bốc đồng. Dữ liệu 308 người tiêu dùng trẻ đã tham gia mua sắm livestream thời trang được phân tích bằng PLS-SEM. Kết quả cho thấy, FoMO và hiệu ứng đám đông đều ảnh hưởng tích cực đến trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy mua sắm bốc đồng và hành vi mua bốc đồng. Trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng đóng vai trò trung gian một phần. Nghiên cứu góp phần cung cấp thêm bằng chứng thực nghiệm trong livestream commerce ngành thời trang tại Việt Nam và gợi ý hàm ý quản trị cho doanh nghiệp.

latest.title: Modeling Circularwashing Risk in Renewable Energy Adoption: A Structural Equation Approach for Sustainable Consumption
latest.abstract: Abstract Circularwashing limits eco-friendly consumption by overstating, confusing, or inadequately proving the circular properties of products. While regular greenwashing makes ambiguous claims about the environmental characteristics, circularwashing takes advantage of the complicated nature of resource loops and the quality of the supply chain, causing significant market friction and high information asymmetry. Hence, an unexpected change in information distorts price signals, weakens customer trust, and jeopardizes market transparency by creating a lemon market for real circular goods. The present research presents the idea of circularwashing risk and provides a model to analyze the effect of false claims on the customers’ skepticism, decision-making risk perception, institutional trust, penalties for unreasonable behavior, and post-decision actions. The model is based on the Signaling Theory and the Stimulus Organism Response theory and is verified with the help of the survey data collected from 607 digital consumers in Colombia using the method of Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Model (PLS SEM). The measurement properties were assessed through composite reliability, average variance extracted, and heterotrait monotrait discriminant criteria and bootstrap resampling. The findings imply that misleading environmental claims correlate with consumer skepticism, which has a positive relationship with perceived decision risks and the erosion of institutional trust. Moreover, the effects of perceived decision risk and erosion of institutional trust on behavioral penalty are considerable. Structural chains indicate that the relationship between decision risk and erosion of trust serves as two mediating channels. Lastly, the Circularwashing Risk Propagation Model s

latest.title: Green or Greenwashed? Eco-Anxiety and Teen Consumer Choice
latest.venue: Critical Debates in Humanities Science and Global Justice
latest.abstract: Prior research has found that environmental anxiety is becoming prominent among teenagers and can increase their green purchasing intentions. To appeal to growing consumer interest, many companies use greenwashing, a deceptive environmental marketing tactic to appeal to interested consumers but keep their product costs low by avoiding actual eco-friendly production. This tricks worried consumers into believing they are purchasing eco-friendly products when they are not. A survey was conducted to see if there was correlation between how teens analyzed and selected between eco-friendly versus greenwashed product advertisements and their measured eco-anxiety levels. The survey showed low eco-anxiety levels had no association with product selections, medium eco-anxiety levels had notable association with greenwashed selections, and high eco-anxiety levels had notable association with eco-friendly selections. The association between moderate eco-anxiety and greenwashed selections highlights why greenwashing poses an issue to teens who want to make green purchases. However, it is unlikely that the study’s results are highly generalized to a larger population, and the survey should be replicated on a larger scale for better results.

latest.title: NEURO-EMOTIONAL ADVERTISING AND SUBCONSCIOUS CONSUMER DECISION-MAKING IN THE FAST-MOVING CONSUMER GOODS SECTOR IN SOUTH-WEST NIGERIA.
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This study examines how five dimensions of neuro-emotional advertising (emotional appeal, sensory stimuli, neurological engagement, message framing, and brand personality projection) relate to subconscious consumer decision-making among fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) consumers in South-West Nigeria. A cross-sectional survey was conducted in Lagos, Ogun, and Oyo States using a structured five-point Likert questionnaire distributed to FMCG consumers. Of the 384 questionnaires administered, we analysed 208 usable responses (54.2%) using Pearson correlation and multiple regression in SPSS. All five dimensions correlated positively with subconscious consumer decision-making (r = 0.246 to 0.506, p < 0.01). In the regression model (R² = 0.527; adjusted R² = 0.519; F(5, 202) = 65.29, p < 0.001), all five dimensions were positive and statistically significant predictors. Brand personality projection had the largest standardised coefficient (β = 0.345), followed by emotional appeal (β = 0.306), sensory stimuli (β = 0.292), message framing (β = 0.214) and neurological engagement (β = 0.116). The results suggest that FMCG advertising works through several complementary routes at once, and that projecting a distinctive, trustworthy brand personality is the strongest single correlate of automatic, emotion-driven purchase tendencies in this market. Because the outcome and predictors are self-reported and the design is cross-sectional, the findings describe associations, not causal effects, and should be followed by experimental and neurophysiological work

latest.title: Does the Right Package Color Brew Better Feelings About the Product? Emotional Congruence, Perceived Fit, and Brand Affect in Coffee Packaging
latest.venue: Journal of Applied Business and Economics
latest.abstract: Packaging color is a powerful brand signal that shapes perceptions and purchase behavior, yet managers select packaging colors based on convention or aesthetic preference rather than congruence with a category's emotional objectives. Drawing on color-in-context theory, schema congruity, and sensory marketing, this study explores whether matching package color to a product category’s emotional meaning improves brand affect. In a coffee packaging study, red packaging produced higher brand affect than blue packaging, and perceived package-category fit mediated the effect. The findings translate color theory into an applied decision framework for packaging audits, portfolio management, retail and digital merchandising, and global expansion.

latest.title: The Effects of Digital Entrepreneurship, Digital Literacy, and Digital Platforms on Gen Z Purchase Decisions
latest.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies has fundamentally transformed the competitive landscape of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). To remain competitive, MSMEs are increasingly required to strengthen their digital entrepreneurial capabilities, improve consumers' digital literacy, and optimize the use of digital platforms. This study examines the effects of digital entrepreneurship, digital literacy, and digital platforms on Generation Z purchase decisions as a strategy for strengthening MSME competitiveness in the era of artificial intelligence. The study employed a quantitative approach involving 175 Generation Z consumers of a local culinary MSME in Bogor, Indonesia. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings demonstrate that digital entrepreneurship has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (β = 0.336, t = 4.040, p < 0.001). Digital literacy also positively and significantly influences purchase decisions (β = 0.205, t = 2.009, p = 0.045), while digital platforms show a positive and significant effect (β = 0.296, t = 3.180, p = 0.001). The model explains 55.8% of the variance in Generation Z purchase decisions. These findings highlight the importance of integrating entrepreneurial digital capabilities, consumer digital literacy, and effective digital platform utilization to enhance MSME competitiveness. In the era of artificial intelligence, these capabilities provide an important foundation for MSMEs to improve market engagement, strengthen consumer decision-making, and sustain their competitiveness in an increasingly technology-driven business environment.

latest.title: Understanding the Mediating Role of Purchase Intention in Personality-Driven Sustainable Consumption Behaviour
latest.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Sustainable consumption has gained increasing attention due to growing environmental concerns and the need to encourage responsible consumer behaviour. Despite greater awareness of sustainability issues, many consumers continue to exhibit a gap between favourable sustainability perceptions and actual purchasing behaviour. This study examines the influence of personality traits and perceived behavioural control on sustainable consumption behaviour, with particular attention to the mediating role of purchase intention. Drawing on personality-based and intention-driven behavioural perspectives, the study investigates the effects of openness to experience, conscientiousness, and perceived behavioural control on consumers’ sustainable purchasing decisions. A quantitative research design was employed, and data were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). The findings reveal that purchase intention is the strongest predictor of sustainable consumption behaviour. Conscientiousness significantly influences both purchase intention and sustainable consumption behaviour, while openness to experience demonstrates an indirect effect through purchase intention but does not directly predict behaviour. Perceived behavioural control significantly affects purchase intention and sustainable consumption behaviour, highlighting the importance of consumers’ perceived capability to engage in sustainable purchasing practices. The mediation analysis confirms that purchase intention serves as a critical mechanism linking personality traits with sustainable consumption behaviour. These findings contribute to the growing literature on personality-driven consumer behaviour by demonstrating that personality traits influence sustainable purchasing through differen

latest.title: Integrating Conventional and Islamic Economic Perspectives into Financial Literacy Education: A Comparative Analysis of Consumption, Saving, and Investment Theories
latest.abstract: This study compares consumption, saving, and investment theories in conventional and Islamic economics and develops their implications for financial literacy education and economics teaching. Using a qualitative descriptive-comparative literature review, it examines Keynesian consumption theory, life-cycle and permanent-income approaches, saving–investment coordination, national-income equilibrium, and Islamic principles of moderation, lawful transactions, social responsibility, and maqasid al-shariah. The comparative synthesis identifies complementary learning dimensions: conceptual understanding of economic relationships, analytical interpretation of macroeconomic models, ethical evaluation of financial choices, and contextual application to household budgeting and investment decisions. A proposed pedagogical framework connects comparative theory, scenario-based discussion, numerical exercises, and reflective assessment. The study argues that macroeconomic identities remain analytically applicable across economic perspectives, while Islamic economics contributes explicit normative criteria for financial decision-making. These findings are conceptual curriculum implications, not measured improvements in students’ literacy or behavior. The article contributes an interdisciplinary foundation for designing financial literacy lessons that integrate economic reasoning and ethical reflection in secondary and higher education.

latest.title: How does a disaster change consumers' belief systems and retail expenditure?
latest.venue: Family and Consumer Sciences Research Journal
latest.abstract: Abstract Theory of awe suggests that awe elicited by disasters can affect both consumers' belief systems, such as new ecological paradigm (NEP), and their behavioral patterns. In this vein, this research examined how a disaster experience was associated with consumers' NEP endorsement and shopping motivations. It also profiled consumers based on expenditure changes across product categories, comparing pandemic experiences, NEP, shopping motivations, and demographic characteristics. Analysis of responses from 259 U.S. consumers confirmed the NEP as a central mechanism linked to consumption changes and identified four consumer typologies with unique profiles, offering insights for retailers to predict consumer behaviors during future disasters.

latest.title: A Study on Consumer Buying Behaviour in the Cosmetic Industry in India
latest.abstract: Abstract This paper explores buyer behaviour in the Indian cosmetic market, considering the demographic, psychological, socio-cultural, and digital influencing factors. As the market is growing fast and getting more digital, it has become critical to comprehend the changing consumer motivations. The literature review chapter critically looks at the literature review on the consumer buying behaviour of the cosmetic industry in India, and analyses the demographic, psychological, cultural, and digital factors influencing consumer buying behaviour. The secondary results indicate that cosmetic purchasing behaviour in India is multidimensional and the interplay of socio-economic, psychological assessment, cultural identity, and digital influence. Income and value perception influence brand choice, and specialised categories, green and halal cosmetics, depend on environmental concern and religiosity. The purchase and repurchase intention are strongly based on perceived quality and brand trust. Further, online marketing and social media activate decision-making processes faster by influencing attitudes, improving access to information and strengthening social validation.

latest.title: The Artificial Intelligence and Social Media Marketing Performance: Evidence on Personalization and Predictive Analytics from Pakistan’s Consumer Products Industry
latest.abstract: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) affects social media marketing in Pakistan’s consumer products industry, focusing on both its opportunities and its challenges. It uses a mixed-method design that combines 20 in-depth interviews with a structured questionnaire completed by 150 marketing professionals in firms that use AI. Multiple regression analyses show that AI-enabled personalized content and predictive analytics are significant positive predictors of ROI, customer engagement, and conversion rates, and together explain 43% to 50% of the variance in these outcomes. Personalized content is most strongly associated with ROI, while predictive analytics is most strongly associated with conversion rates. The interviews point to three main opportunities: enhanced personalization, greater efficiency and cost savings, and better data-driven decisions. They also point to three main challenges: high implementation costs, data privacy and security concerns, and a shortage of AI skills. The findings highlight the importance of strong data protection, transparency, and staff training for maintaining consumer trust and complying with regulations. The study offers practical recommendations for using AI responsibly in social media marketing. Because the data are cross-sectional, self-reported, and drawn from one industry in one country, the results show associations rather than cause and effect.

latest.title: Beyond Price: Understanding the Interplay Between Perceived Value, Customer Satisfaction, and Purchase Intention Among Generation Z Consumers
latest.abstract: Understanding the factors that shape Generation Z's purchase intention is increasingly important in the fast-food industry, where price perceptions and customer experiences play critical roles in consumer decision-making. Although previous studies have examined the relationships between price, customer satisfaction, and purchase intention, further investigation is needed to clarify the mediating role of customer satisfaction in the relationship between price perception and purchase intention, particularly among Generation Z consumers in the fast-food sector. Therefore, this study examines the direct effect of price perception on purchase intention, the effect of customer satisfaction on purchase intention, the effect of price perception on customer satisfaction, and customer satisfaction's mediating role in the relationship between price perception and purchase intention. A quantitative explanatory research design was employed using primary data collected through questionnaires distributed to 100 Generation Z consumers of Mie Gacoan. The sample size was determined using the Lemeshow formula. This study contributes to consumer behavior literature by clarifying the mediating mechanism through which customer satisfaction connects price perceptions with Generation Z's purchase intention in the fast-food context. Practically, the findings offer insights into fast-food businesses to develop competitive pricing strategies while maintaining customer satisfaction to strengthen purchase intention among younger consumers.

latest.title: Impact of restaurant robot service consumption values on their consequences: the moderating effects of perceived risk and human–robot interaction quality
latest.venue: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Insights
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examined the effects of consumption values on customers' behavioral intentions toward robot service restaurants, based on the theory of consumption values and the value attitude behavior model. It also analyzed the moderating effects of perceived risk and human–robot interaction quality. Design/methodology/approach The study collected data from 756 customers who experienced robot services in restaurants. A structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis with a multi-group approach was used to test relationships. Findings The results showed that functional, human-like capability, social, emotional and epistemic values significantly predicted attitudes toward robot services, while price, safety and privacy did not. Most consumption values also influenced perceived brand equity, which strongly affected all outcomes including customers' intention to pay more, loyalty, intention to recommend and participation in value co-creation. Perceived risk and human–robot interaction quality partially influenced relationships in the structural model. Research limitations/implications This study has contributed to the literature on consumption value theory by incorporating a new construct – human-like capability – and emphasizing price value and safety and privacy values in the context of robot-provided restaurant services. However, future studies could examine robotic consumption values across a broader range of robot-assisted hospitality and tourism sectors. Practical implications This study provided valuable insights for restaurant managers by identifying robot service consumption values that significantly influence customers' behavioral intentions. Additionally, it demonstrates that service robots enhance service providers' performance through improved service efficie

latest.title: Too little, too much, or just right? How AI recommendation information volume shapes trust and consumer behavior
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) shopping assistants explain why a product is selected, yet the appropriate defaults remain unclear. We define recommendation information volume as the amount of nonredundant, product-relevant information and compare five ordered explanation packages. Study 1 identifies an inverted-U response in a randomized Chinese mobile-retail experiment. Study S1 compares identical messages attributed to an AI assistant or a human salesperson, with separate source-neutral measurement validation. Study 2 reports conditional positive indirect associations through perceived usefulness, trust in AI, and decision comfort, and conditional negative indirect associations through information overload and algorithmic over-justification. Same-session estimates do not establish causal mediation. Its product-version comparison combines complexity, functionality, and safety considerations. Study 3 provides behavioral evidence across 51,248 recommendation impressions and service outcomes for 5000 distinct users. Moderate packages perform best within the tested sets. Bounded information processing explains the benefit–burden trade-off; persuasion knowledge suggests that disproportionate justification depends on expectations of selective versus comprehensive advice, across AI and human sources. Because amount, diagnostic priority, and content composition vary jointly, the experiments identify assigned-package effects, not pure quantity effects. The findings support category-specific testing of default explanations without establishing an exclusively algorithmic mechanism.

latest.title: UNDERSTANDING GEN-Z’S ATTITUDE TOWARDS PENANG’S LOCAL FOOD: THE ROLE OF EMOTIONAL, PRESTIGE, AND QUALITY-VALUES
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: Penang’s local food creates an important element of the state’s cultural identity and serves as a key driver of tourism attractiveness. As Generation Z (Gen-Z) increasingly becomes a prominent consumer group in both the food and travel industries, understanding their perceptions and engagement with local food experiences has become increasingly important for sustaining culinary tourism and preserving cultural heritage. This study aims to examine the factors that contribute to Gen-Z’s attitude towards Penang’s local food by focusing on three variables which is emotional value, prestige value and quality value. A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was employed, utilizing a self-administered questionnaire distributed to 431 Gen-Z respondents aged 18-29 years in Malaysia who had prior experience consuming Penang's local food. Convenience sampling was used, and data were analyzed using Pearson correlation and multiple regression analyses. Results indicated that all three variables significantly influence Gen-Z’s attitudes with prestige value emerging as the strongest predicator, followed by quality and emotional value. These findings suggest that social recognition, sensory satisfaction and emotional connections play an essential role in shaping young consumers’ perception of local food. The study provides useful insights for tourism authorities, local food businesses, and cultural stakeholders to develop more effective strategies in preserving Penang’s culinary heritage while aligning with the preferences of the younger generation in a rapidly digitalized and globalized food culture.

latest.title: Analyzing Consumer Loyalty to Ultra‐Fast Fashion: An Integrative Analysis Based on the Stimulus‐Organism‐Response Model
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The ultra‐fast fashion industry generates massive online sales, partly because of its ability to attract the custom of Generation Z (Gen Z). Given that this generational cohort typically has low brand loyalty, this paper examines how the dimensions of the stimulus‐organism‐response (S‐O‐R) model explain Gen Z's loyalty to the ultra‐fast fashion industry. For this purpose, the analysis presented in this paper relies on both a linear and an evolutionary view of the S‐O‐R model. Based on data from 208 questionnaires completed by consumers of ultra‐fast fashion, two analytical phases were conducted: (1) partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) and (2) qualitative comparative analysis (QCA). The results of the first phase suggest that consumer sustainability consciousness is associated with brand loyalty directly and under mediation, whereas social media peer communication is associated with brand loyalty only under mediation by brand equity. The second phase shows the relevance of brand equity in explaining both high and low brand loyalty. The configurations explaining high brand loyalty or low brand loyalty show that the relationship of each outcome with consumer sustainability consciousness and social media peer communications reflects psychological mechanisms that allow consumers to overcome the cognitive dissonance between their attitudes and behavior.

latest.title: Customer Engagement and Lead Conversion in Automotive Retail
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: This exploratory research paper examines customer engagement and lead conversion at a private Škoda dealership in Pune, India. The study draws on a confirmed aggregate activity summary of 52 walk-in customers observed during a three-month internship, together with an anonymised 24-record enquiry extract. Of the 52 walk-ins, 45 completed a test drive, six booked within the internship period, and three additional bookings were known to occur later. The enquiry extract shows interest concentrated in the Slavia and Kylaq models, although the extract is not a complete cohort and cannot represent the dealership or market as a whole. Field observations from both authors inform a process-level interpretation of needs discovery, product explanation, test-drive coordination, and follow-up. The analysis is descriptive: it does not estimate causal effects, compare dealerships, or attribute booking outcomes to a single intervention. The findings suggest that a dealership should treat the test drive as an intermediate engagement stage and maintain a consent-aware, structured follow-up process that distinguishes in-period bookings from later conversions. The paper contributes a carefully bounded practitioner account of how customer-journey concepts can be applied to automotive retail while preserving the limits of a small, private operational dataset. Keywords: automotive retail; customer engagement; lead conversion; customer journey; exploratory research paper; Pune

latest.title: Retail Sales Promotion and Consumer Conversion of Wellness-Oriented Food Products: An Exploratory Field Study of Nutrica at Sai Bazar, Mamurdi
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study examines how point-of-sale promotion and need-based personal selling are used to engage shoppers and support purchase conversion for Nutrica wellness-oriented food products at Sai Bazar, Mamurdi. It focuses on the practical selling process, customer questions and objections, and the role of product knowledge in retail interactions. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopts an exploratory, descriptive single-site case-study design based on a two-month sales internship conducted from 1 June to 31 July 2026. Evidence comprises the trainee’s field observations, customer-facing selling activities, an internship activity diary and a summary of outlet-level records supplied in the source report. No structured questionnaire, probability sample or controlled experiment was reported. Findings: The field account indicates that concise, customer-centred communication, active listening, product familiarity and responses tailored to specific objections were central to the selling process. The source report records 247 customer interactions and 192 conversions. If these counts use consistent definitions and refer to the same observation period, the implied descriptive conversion ratio is 77.7%; this should be treated as provisional because the underlying transaction-level records and operational definitions were not included. The report also lists 1,014 L as units sold, but the measure requires clarification because the promoted portfolio included oils, honey and peanut butter. Practical implications: Retail promoters may benefit from short question-led scripts, approved product-information sheets, systematic objection logs and consistent recording of approaches, meaningful conversations, transactions and SKU-level quantities. hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings.
