latest.title: Factors associated with anxiety among college students: a combined analysis using regression and fsQCA
latest.abstract: Background This study explores the associations of information overload (IO), perceived involution (PI), psychological richness (PR), and meaning in life (MIL) with anxiety among college students. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 1,325 college students. A demographic questionnaire, the IO scale, the PI scale, the PR scale, and the MIL scale served as the measurement tools. Spearman correlation analysis was applied to examine the bivariate associations among variables. Linear mixed models and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) were adopted to investigate the interrelationships between IO, PI, PR, MIL, and anxiety. Results The linear mixed model results indicated that IO had positive indirect associations with anxiety via both MIL and PR. PI showed a positive direct association with anxiety but negative indirect associations through MIL and PR. The fsQCA results further revealed that no single antecedent condition was necessary for anxiety. One high-anxiety configuration was dominated by the core conditions of high IO and high PI, along with the absence of PR and MIL. Conclusion College students’ anxiety is associated with both external stressors and internal psychological resources. These preliminary findings may inform future longitudinal and intervention studies.

latest.title: From emotional comfort to relational investment in generative AI companionship: evidence from SEM and fsQCA
latest.abstract: With the rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (AI), chatbots are evolving from instrumental assistants into emotionally responsive companions. This study develops a low-friction relational process model to examine the relationships linking generative AI companionship with emotional relief and positive social investment. AI emotional responsiveness, non-judgemental interaction, and memory-based continuity were conceptualized as interaction conditions, while perceived being understood, deep self-disclosure, and synthetic attachment were specified as psychological mechanisms. Structural equation modeling (SEM), bootstrap mediation analysis, moderation analysis, and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) were employed to analyse 765 valid responses from generative AI chatbot users. The SEM results show that non-judgemental interaction exhibits the most consistent pattern of associations with perceived being understood, deep self-disclosure, synthetic attachment, emotional relief, and positive social investment. Perceived being understood and synthetic attachment show relatively stable mediating patterns, whereas deep self-disclosure is significantly associated with emotional relief but shows a less consistent association with positive social investment. Perceived AI safety and self-disclosure habit play differentiated moderating roles. The fsQCA findings reveal three configurations for high emotional relief and four configurations for high positive social investment, complementing the SEM results. This study provides a systematic account of generative AI companionship and offers implications for safer and relationship-oriented AI design.

latest.title: Generative AI in Consumer Decision Making: How Algorithmic Recommendations Shape Brand Trust
latest.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
latest.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly moving from the back end of recommendation engines to the consumer-facing interface, where conversational assistants, generated product descriptions and personalised feeds increasingly decide what shoppers see, compare and buy. While the literature on algorithm aversion and algorithm appreciation explains when consumers accept algorithmic advice, little is known about how such advice reshapes trust in the brand that deploys it. This paper develops and specifies a multi-level, testable framework in which four attributes of a GenAI recommendation (perceived personalisation, perceived accuracy and relevance, transparency and explainability, and disclosure of the AI source) influence brand trust through two opposing appraisal pathways: perceived algorithmic competence and fairness, which build trust, and perceived manipulation and privacy concern, which erode it. Brand trust in turn drives purchase intention and loyalty, with AI literacy and task type (utilitarian versus hedonic) as boundary conditions. Nine hypotheses are derived from trust theory, the persuasion knowledge model and the human–automation literature, and a dynamic trust-calibration loop is proposed in which each decision cycle updates the trust baseline used in the next. A two-study empirical design is specified, comprising a PLS-SEM survey and a 3 × 2 × 2 online experiment, and a Monte Carlo power analysis shows that a survey of about 300 respondents gives at least 95% power for the main hypothesised paths, while a 600-participant experiment gives about 92% power for medium-small effects of disclosure. The paper contributes a brand-level, trust-centred account of GenAI recommendations, identifies transparency as the lever that most plausibly converts alg

latest.title: Buy Now, Pay Later: An AI and Machine Learning-Based Analysis of Its Influence on Youth Spending Behaviour and Financial Decision-Making
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of digital financial technologies has increased the adoption of Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) services, particularly among young consumers. BNPL offers flexible payment options and convenient access to short-term credit, but it also raises concerns regarding impulsive purchasing, excessive spending, financial literacy, and responsible financial decision making. This research aims to analyze the influence of BNPL services on youth spending behaviour and financial decision making through Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques. The study focuses on young consumers aged 18 30 years and examines key factors such as BNPL usage frequency, purchasing patterns, financial awareness, affordability, and perceived financial risk. Primary data is collected through a structured questionnaire, while secondary data is obtained from existing research literature and financial reports. The proposed methodology involves data preprocessing, exploratory data analysis, and the application of machine learning algorithms to identify behavioural patterns and predict spending-related risks. The study seeks to investigate the relationship between BNPL usage and financial behaviour while exploring the potential of AI driven predictive analytics to support responsible financial decisions. The research is expected to contribute to a better understanding of BNPL-related financial behaviour among youth and demonstrate the potential of machine learning in promoting financial awareness and informed decision-making.

latest.title: Cooperative entrepreneurship education in the care sector
latest.abstract: Population aging, dependency, and demand for long-term care call for improvements in employment quality and greater social and labor inclusion of women in situations of vulnerability. This article systematizes a cooperative entrepreneurship education pathway for establishing, joining, or managing worker cooperatives in the home help service sector. It was designed within EDIMET, Decent Employment for Migrant Women in the Cross-Border Area (0531_EDIMET_3_E), funded by Interreg Spain–Portugal (POCTEP) 2021–2027, and connects decent work with the prevention of labor exploitation. The pathway integrates the legal framework and literature on the social economy, cooperatives, entrepreneurship, vulnerability, care, and inclusion. It combines personal, relational, cooperative, entrepreneurial, technical and organizational, legal and administrative, and digital and management competencies; modules on cooperative design and management, home help, accreditation, and support; and active learning methods, projects, simulations, tutoring, and continuous assessment. A curriculum design is presented with potential for adaptation by training providers, public administrations, and social economy organizations. Its contribution lies in connecting the recognition of competencies, group support, the professionalization of care, and the prevention of exploitation. Design validation, feasibility, acceptability, learning outcomes, and social and employment effects require subsequent evaluation

latest.title: Strengthening an Edu-Tourism Village Ecosystem through Integrated Production, Digitalization, and Appropriate Technology in Parakanjaya Village : Towards a Sustainable Smart Economy
latest.venue: International Journal of Research in Community Service
latest.abstract: Parakanjaya Village in Kemang District, Bogor Regency has strong potential in batik-based creative industries, village-owned enterprises (BUMDes), rural water services, and the Setu Salabenda environmental asset. The first-year empowerment program addressed constraints in production capacity, product quality, financial records, digital marketing, water-service efficiency, poultry productivity, and village information. A service-learning and civic-engagement approach covered five stages: outreach, training, technology adoption, mentoring and evaluation, and sustainability strengthening. Key interventions included batik screen-printing technology transfer; GARLaTik and the Batik Generative Algorithm for motif development; dyeing quality-control standards; WhatsApp-based Simple Finance; digital marketing; a portable cage for 400 chickens; solar-powered jet pumps; and an improved village website. Baseline data showed batik production of about 35 pieces per month, egg output of 20 kg per day, PAMDes electricity costs of IDR 1.2 million per month, and water service for about 200 households. First-year targets were at least 50% higher batik capacity, 30% higher sales, 40% higher egg output, 30% lower electricity costs, and regular website updates. The program positions technology as an empowerment tool integrated with institutional capacity, local wisdom, and the village economy to advance a sustainable smart edu-tourism economy.

latest.title: CEO environmental communication, speech acts, and firm value
latest.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
latest.abstract: Abstract Signaling theory predicts that communication, such as by CEOs, might complement observable environmental engagement by a firm, by reducing information asymmetry. Yet it remains unclear whether firms with stronger environmental engagement communicate more about these efforts and the potential implications for firm value. To analyze 14,523 firm-quarter earnings call Q&A sessions held by 364 publicly listed firms between 2007 and 2022, the current research measures CEO communication about firm environmental engagement and the communicative intent behind such communication by combining MSCI Environmental Pillar Scores, Compustat data, and a fine-tuned DeBERTa model. Firms with stronger environmental engagement communicate less, rather than more, about their efforts during earnings call Q&A sessions. Yet CEO communication about firm environmental engagement can be positively associated with firm value, depending on the communicative intent the CEO indicates, such that assertive and directive speech maintain this positive association, but expressive and commissive speech acts are negatively associated with firm value.

latest.title: Questionnaire Item Budgets and Incremental Predictive Value for Self-Reported AI-Enabled Consumer Service Use: Temporal Evidence from a Korean Panel
latest.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
latest.abstract: We examined whether additional questionnaire items improve prediction of self-reported artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled consumer service use. Models were developed with 1565 Korean panel respondents who hesitated to shop online because their activity might be recorded. They were evaluated on 1520 such respondents one wave later. Item sets were selected under limits of 0–30 additional items, with or without prior use. All four original models using every candidate item had higher log loss (prediction error; lower is better) than their benchmarks: for ridge regression with prior use, 0.69961 versus 0.66062 for a benchmark based on prior use alone. Three models remained worse after adjustment for multiple comparisons, and no original budget policy established improvement. A single expected-benefit item gave favorable estimates, but its added value remained uncertain. Collapsing regional categories and retuning made demographic estimates slightly favorable; stronger regularization was associated with smaller excess losses, and random forests had favorable estimates. The full panel also included respondents outside the hesitation-defined group. Gains in that broader panel remained uncertain among people absent from model development. These findings concern particular fitted specifications. How information is encoded and regularized may matter as much as whether it is collected.

latest.title: Analysis of Consumer Perception of Minimalist Packaging Design as a Marketing Communication Strategy in Digital Business
latest.abstract: The development of digital business is encouraging companies to utilize packaging design as a marketing communication strategy that can attract young consumers through visual displays on digital media. Minimalist packaging design has become a widely used trend because it is considered to create a modern, simple, and professional impression. This study aims to determine consumer perceptions of minimalist packaging design as a marketing communication strategy in digital businesses and analyze the influence of visual communication elements on the appeal of young consumers. The study used a quantitative approach with descriptive methods. Data collection was conducted by distributing questionnaires to 100 young consumer respondents aged 17–30 who actively use digital platforms such as Shopee, TikTok Shop, and Instagram Shopping. Data analysis used IBM SPSS Statistics through validity and reliability tests and descriptive percentage analysis. The results show that minimalist packaging design has a very good perception with an average score of 87%. The study's conclusions confirm that minimalist packaging design is effective as a visual-based marketing communication strategy in the digital business era.

latest.title: The Impact of Insurance Partnerships on Customer Trust and Social Protection at Pegadaian
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of insurance collaboration on customer trust in Pegadaian. The research background arises from the relatively low insurance penetration in Indonesia compared to the ASEAN average, alongside the increasing number of Pegadaian customers utilizing insurance-integrated services. The research method employed is a quantitative approach using a survey of 150 Pegadaian customers who have used products with insurance protection. The research instrument is a Likert-scale questionnaire, tested for validity and reliability using Pearson Product Moment and Cronbach’s Alpha. The results indicate that the instrument is valid and reliable, with Cronbach’s Alpha values exceeding 0.80. Simple linear regression analysis produced a regression coefficient of 0.684 with a significance level of 0.000, meaning that insurance collaboration has a positive and significant effect on customer trust. The coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.468 shows that insurance collaboration explains 46.8% of the variation in customer trust, while the remaining 53.2% is influenced by other factors such as institutional reputation, personal experience, and external conditions. This study concludes that insurance collaboration is a crucial strategy in building customer trust in Pegadaian and provides academic contributions to the development of trust theory and relationship marketing in the context of non-bank financial institutions.

latest.title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Water Security in Western Rajasthan: A Study of Selected Renewable Energy Companies
latest.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF INNOVATIONS & RESEARCH ANALYSIS
latest.abstract: The western parts of Rajasthan experience water scarcity owing to the arid nature of the climate and low amount of rainfall in the area. As such, the CSR programs of renewable energy companies have immense importance in conserving the water resources as well as uplifting the rural population. This research analyzes the water-based CSR initiatives of Suzlon Energy Limited and Adani Green Energy Limited (AGEL) in western Rajasthan. Using the descriptive research methodology, the paper is based only on corporate annual reports and any other available corporate public reports. The analysis is conducted by classifying and examining company's interventions in pond construction, desilting, and construction of water infrastructure. It is found that both the companies have carried out many water projects; however, type of activities and places have varied in different financial years. Furthermore, it is found that there is a serious lack of information in the corporation's reports, especially about the number of beneficiaries and project viability in the long run. It is concluded that the water projects by CSR programs have great potential to increase water security of rural areas provided they are monitored constantly.

latest.title: how ai going to change the beauty industry in 2027
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in beauty product discovery, virtual try-on, photo editing, marketing, product research, retail and professional services. This report synthesizes publicly available evidence published through 11 November 2026 to assess how those developments may change the beauty industry in 2027. It distinguishes the core beauty market from AI software revenue and separates verified historical results from scenario-based projections. The review draws on industry market studies, public company filings, official product documentation, regulatory guidance and selected academic research. Major findings indicate meaningful commercial adoption of generative imaging, virtual beauty tools and AI-assisted marketing, alongside persistent measurement gaps concerning causal sales impact, consumer welfare and model quality across skin tones. The report examines cosmetic versus medical claims, facial-image privacy, advertising transparency, body-image research, algorithmic fairness, potential impacts on beauty professionals and scientific product development. Three qualitative 2027 scenarios are proposed: selective normalization, accelerated integration and adoption constrained by trust, costs or regulation. The report concludes with a practical measurement framework for brands, retailers, application developers and researchers. This is a structured desk review, not a systematic review, original market survey, independently benchmarked product comparison or peer-reviewed journal article. Findings should be interpreted within the definitions, dates and limitations stated in the report. Editorial source note (not part of the abstract): First-party product examples in the report include the AI Beauty Styling tool directory, Face Beauty Analysis, AI Skin

latest.title: Novelty or eeriness? Investigating consumer responses to AI-generated product images through expectancy violation theory
latest.venue: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on Expectancy Violation Theory, this study examines how product image creator identity (AI vs. human) influences purchase intentions and the underlying psychological mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach Three online experiments examined consumers' attitudes toward AI-generated product images and purchase intentions toward the featured products, assessed how these evaluations deviated from expectations associated with human-created images, and identified conditions under which artificial intelligence (AI) imagery was more or less effective in shaping consumer responses. Data were analyzed in Statistical Package for the Social Sciences using Multivariate Analysis of Variance and Multivariate Analysis of Covariance, with serial and moderated mediation analyses conducted using the PROCESS macro. Findings Consumers consistently prefer human-created product images and perceive them as more novel, whereas AI-generated images evoke greater eeriness. Perceived novelty, eeriness, positive and negative expectancy violations, and attitudes mediate the relationship between image creator identity and purchase intention. Product type serves as a boundary condition, with AI-generated images evaluated more favorably for search products than for experience products. Originality/value This research identifies positive and negative expectancy violations as central psychological mechanisms shaping consumer responses to AI-generated product images. By highlighting product type as a boundary condition, it helps reconcile mixed findings in the AI-generated marketing literature and provides actionable guidance for the strategic use of AI-generated product imagery.

latest.title: Structural insights into the effects of generative AI-empowered social media marketing on customer-brand engagement and purchase behaviors: evidence from China's platform economy
latest.abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of generative artificial intelligence-empowered social media marketing activities in enhancing customer purchase intentions through the mediating roles of brand equity and relationship equity within China’s platform economy. As generative artificial intelligence increasingly transforms digital interactions between brands and consumers, understanding its influence on customer engagement and purchasing behavior has become increasingly important. Data were collected from 620 Chinese consumers and analyzed using structural equation modeling to examine the relationships among generative artificial intelligence-empowered social media marketing activities, customer–brand engagement, brand equity, relationship equity, and purchase intention. The findings reveal that generative artificial intelligence-empowered social media marketing activities exert significant positive effects on customer–brand engagement, purchase intention, brand equity, and relationship equity. Brand equity significantly enhances both customer–brand engagement and purchase intention, confirming its important role in converting artificial intelligence-enabled social media marketing efforts into favorable consumer outcomes. Relationship equity significantly influences purchase intention but does not significantly affect customer–brand engagement. Furthermore, customer–brand engagement does not significantly influence purchase intention. The mediation results indicate that brand equity significantly mediates the effects of generative artificial intelligence-empowered social media marketing activities on both customer–brand engagement and purchase intention. In contrast, relationship equity mediates only the relationship between generative artificial intelligence-empowered

latest.title: Transparency that sells: the impact of anti–pre-made dishes attitude disclosure on restaurant patronage intentions
latest.abstract: Introduction Although industrially produced pre-made (PMDs) offer convenience, their use in restaurants may conflict with consumers’ expectations of freshness and culinary craftsmanship. Drawing on signaling theory and expectancy violation theory, this study examines how restaurants’ disclosure of an anti-PMD stance influences patronage dishes through perceived moral authenticity and perceived risk, and whether these effects depend on operational transparency. Methods Four between-subjects scenario experiments were conducted in casual-restaurant contexts involving offline dining and online food delivery. Two single-factor experiments examined the effects of anti-PMD disclosure (presence versus absence), while two 2 × 2 factorial experiments further manipulated operational transparency (closed versus open kitchens). The hypotheses were tested using analysis of variance, bootstrap mediation analysis, and moderated mediation analysis. Results Anti-PMD disclosure increased patronage intention and perceived moral authenticity while reducing perceived food-related risk. Perceived moral authenticity and perceived risk mediated the relationship between disclosure and patronage intention. Operational transparency moderated these relationships: disclosure significantly influenced patronage intention and both mediators in closed-kitchen settings, whereas these effects were not significant in open-kitchen settings. The indirect effects through both mediators were also significant in closed-kitchen settings but not in open-kitchen settings. Discussion These findings clarify how food-preparation information and operational transparency jointly shape the psychological evaluations underlying consumers’ food-provider choice intentions. They extend research on PMDs and restaurant authent

latest.title: Strategi Rebranding Bakpia Djava (Repositioning, Redesign, Relaunching) Dalam Mempertahankan Daya Saing Produk Oleh-Oleh Tradisional
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini menganalisis strategi rebranding Bakpia Djava dan kontribusinya dalam mempertahankan daya saing sebagai produk oleh-oleh tradisional Yogyakarta. Menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif dengan wawancara mendalam terhadap Head Marketing dan Konsultan F&B Bakpia Djava, penelitian ini mengkaji fenomena rebranding yang dilakukan pada Juni 2025. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa rebranding didorong oleh tekanan persaingan pasar dan perubahan perilaku konsumen generasi muda di era digital. Implementasi mencakup perubahan logo menjadi lebih humanis, pergantian tagline dari "Resep Tradisional Tempo Doeloe" menjadi "Cita Rasa Tempo Doeloe", serta peluncuran tiga kategori kemasan berdasarkan strata sosial konsumen. Dampak rebranding terlihat pada peningkatan kunjungan, omset penjualan, dan penguatan keunggulan merek melalui strategi pembuktian kualitas produk. Keunikan strategi Bakpia Djava terletak pada penerapan kolaborasi kompetitif dengan kompetitor dan manajemen transisi visual yang mempertahankan logo lama untuk menjaga loyalitas pelanggan setia. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa rebranding yang memadukan pembaruan identitas visual dengan pelestarian nilai tradisional dan strategi kolaboratif efektif dalam mempertahankan daya saing produk oleh-oleh tradisional di era digital

latest.title: Personality without a person: measuring personality in generative AI
latest.abstract: Personality describes relatively stable styles of thinking, feeling, and acting when interacting with the physical and social environment. The stability and reliability of these individual styles plays an important role in our daily lives as we team with various individuals at work and home. Generative AI agents (LLMs) are new additions to our lives, quickly assuming roles that might otherwise have been given to humans though there is little known about the stability and reliability of LLM “thinking” styles or actions. We have been investigating whether LLMs can be thought of as having personality out of the box along with the creation and measurement of AI agents with distinct and reliable personalities. In this study four LLMs were assessed with both self-report and newer gamified behavioral measures of personality under an Out-of-the-Box condition and with three prompt-based personas. Contrary to previous studies, LLMs showed very high test-retest reliability. Personality scores varied predictably following persona prompting, while agreement between assessment types varied across models and persona conditions.

latest.title: Value Orientations, Product-Specific Considerations, and Conditional Consumer Acceptance of Refrigerators Containing Recycled Materials in Poland
latest.abstract: Abstract The transition toward a circular economy requires not only technological and regulatory changes but also consumer acceptance of products incorporating recycled materials. While previous research has extensively examined pro-environmental consumption, comparatively less attention has been paid to high-involvement durable goods, where purchase decisions are infrequent and involve substantial financial and functional considerations. This study explores how consumers evaluate refrigerators containing recycled insulation by examining the interplay between personal value orientations, product-specific considerations, overall product evaluation, and conditional purchase consideration. The study draws on two qualitative focus group interviews conducted in Poland with 14 participants representing two age cohorts. The transcripts were analysed using thematic analysis combining deductive and inductive coding. The findings show that biospheric, altruistic, egoistic, and hedonic value orientations coexist in consumers’ reasoning, while their relative relevance varies with the purchase context. Product-specific considerations, including price, quality, durability and reliability, energy efficiency, functionality and usability, design and aesthetics, and credible product information formed an important complementary dimension of product evaluation. Recycled insulation was not evaluated as inherently positive; rather, participants’ evaluations were qualified by the perceived credibility of environmental benefits and expectations concerning product performance. Purchase consideration was likewise strongly conditional, particularly on price comparability, durability, reliability, and transparent environmental information. The study contributes to sustainable consumption and circ

latest.title: Artificial Intelligence as a Strategic Marketing Capability: An Integrated Framework for Firms in Developing Economies
latest.abstract: Purpose: Research on artificial intelligence (AI) in marketing is fragmented across applications and theories, and rests largely on evidence from developed economies.This paper conceptualises AI as a firm-level marketing capability and explains how, and under what conditions, it improves marketing performance, with particular attention to developing economies.Design/methodology/approach: The paper adopts a conceptual, theory-synthesis design.It integrates the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities theory, the marketing capabilities perspective, and relationship marketing and customer equity theory, and develops a framework with nine testable propositions.Findings: AI capability is proposed to improve marketing performance indirectly, by strengthening marketing capabilities, which in turn create customer value.Because AI technologies are increasingly bought as standardised services, advantage is argued to come less from the technologies themselves than from the complementary resources and dynamic capabilities with which they are bundled.Ethical AI governance and human-AI collaboration condition whether AI-enabled marketing creates customer value, while the institutional voids common in developing economies weaken the conversion of AI capability into marketing capability. Research limitations/implications:The propositions await empirical testing, preferably with longitudinal, multi-source and cross-country designs.Practical implications: Managers should invest in data, skills, governance and human-AI routines alongside AI tools.Policymakers should address digital infrastructure, data protection enforcement and the AI capability of small and medium-sized enterprises.

latest.title: From capability to sustainability: The role of innovation, collaboration, and knowledge management in the sustainability performance of SMEs in the food industry
latest.abstract: Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are pivotal to national growth and development; nonetheless, sustaining long-term performance remains particularly challenging in resource-constrained and rapidly evolving market environments. For SMEs in developing countries, the need to balance environmental and social obligations with competitiveness adds to the burden. Building on these considerations, this study examines the impact of innovation, collaboration, and knowledge management on the sustainability performance of SMEs in the food industry in Central Java, Indonesia. Drawing on the Resource-Based View (RBV) and Dynamic Capability Theory (DCT), the study proposes an integrated framework conceptualizing sustainability performance as an outcome of interrelated organizational capabilities. A quantitative research method was employed, and data were collected from 375 owners and managers of SMEs. Prior to hypothesis testing using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM), the data underwent preliminary data analysis, including data screening, missing values analysis, outliers, normality assessment, common method variance (CMV), and non-response bias. The findings indicate that collaboration and knowledge management have positive and statistically significant effects on sustainability performance, whereas innovation does not exhibit a significant effect. Innovation and collaboration explain 41.2% of the variance in knowledge management, while the three capabilities collectively account for 28.3% of the variance in sustainability performance. Theoretically, the study extends the RBV by demonstrating that sustainability requires not only valuable resources but also the DCT to adapt and reconfigure them under changing conditions. The integration of innovation, c

latest.title: Human factors shaping engagement with a digital treatment platform among individuals with lived experience of addiction
latest.abstract: Introduction Substance use disorders (SUDs) are highly prevalent, yet access to care remains limited. Digital interventions have been investigated as a means to expand treatment access, but individuals routinely disengage from them. We evaluated the acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, and usability of a digital platform being tested as part of a collaborative care management-based intervention for SUD treatment in under-resourced areas to identify human factors influencing feasibility, usability, and accessibility. Methods Participants were adults with lived experience of addiction and related treatment. They engaged with the digital treatment platform for one week, then completed semi-structured interviews exploring their experience, followed by the Acceptability of Intervention Measure, Intervention Appropriateness Measure, Feasibility of Intervention Measure, and System Usability Scale. Template-based rapid analysis identified themes. Results 18 individuals ( n = 12 females) completed all assessments. Heavy text, lack of customization, and inconsistent notifications hindered usability. Participants felt assigned goals should match an individual's circumstances and resources available to them to support utilization. Participants desired personalization, integration with existing recovery supports, and features that encouraged routine use. Acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility had respective means of 3.4 (95%CI = 3.0-3.9), 3.3 (95%CI = 2.8-3.9), and 3.4 (95%CI = 2.8-4.0) on 5-point scales with a neutral midpoint of 3. Usability scores approached the commonly used benchmark of 68 (mean=67.6, SD = 15.0). Discussion Digital interventions suffer from heavy disengagement. These findings suggest that digital interventions should fit the end-user's needs an

latest.title: Service Quality Assessment and Improvement Prioritization at the PT. Swabina Gatra Savings and Loan Cooperative Using SERVQUAL and IPA
latest.abstract: This study aims to evaluate service quality and determine improvement priorities at the Savings and Loan Cooperative of PT Swabina Gatra by integrating Service Quality (SERVQUAL) and Importance Performance Analysis (IPA). Unlike previous studies that primarily confirm the existence of service gaps, the novelty of this research lies in its methodological contribution: creating a two-dimensional prioritization framework that combines gap magnitudes with IPA quadrant placements to classify attributes into immediate action, maintenance, or resource reallocation. A descriptive quantitative approach was employed, collecting data from 100 members (exceeding the minimum Slovin sample size of 86) through accidental sampling. The SERVQUAL analysis reveals an overall service quality score of 92.70% with an average gap of -0.30. The responsiveness dimension records the lowest quality (88.37%), while empathy shows the highest (98.32%). The IPA analysis identifies six attributes in Quadrant I (Top Priority), including TA1, TA2, TA3, RE2, RS1, and RS2. Among these, RS2 (staff promptness in responding to member inquiries and complaints) emerges as the most critical finding, exhibiting the largest SERVQUAL gap (-0.600). Practically, this finding directs management to implement specific corrective actions, such as a digital complaint tracking system and a 24-hour Service Level Agreement (SLA) for RS2, alongside targeted improvements for the other five attributes. It is important to note that this study is limited to a descriptive design; it identifies perceived service quality gaps and priorities but does not directly test whether these improvements will enhance member satisfaction or loyalty

latest.title: Sports Betting and Regulatory Governance in Nigeria: Consumer Protection, Disputed Winnings and Institutional Accountability
latest.abstract: This study examined sports betting and regulatory governance in Nigeria, with particular attention to disputed winnings, consumer protection and institutional accountability. It examined the practices and contractual provisions of sports-betting operators that generated disputes over winnings and assessed how effectively regulatory and consumer-protection institutions addressed such disputes. The study adopted a qualitative research design and relied on secondary data drawn from relevant laws, regulatory documents, operators’ terms and conditions, court cases, official records and credible media reports. Purposively selected cases were analysed thematically, focusing on bet cancellation and voiding, technical and settlement errors, integrity investigations, account restrictions, cash-out, payout limits, regulatory intervention and consumer redress. The findings showed that disputes often arose from the considerable contractual, technological and informational control operators exercised over betting transactions and settlement processes. Although regulatory institutions had formal mechanisms for handling complaints and enforcing regulations, their effectiveness in resolving disputes remained uneven. While some interventions resulted in payment and restoration of accounts, other cases lacked clearly documented independent determinations or meaningful redress. The study recommended that operators provide clearer reasons, applicable rules and supporting evidence for decisions affecting winnings, while regulators strengthen independent dispute-resolution mechanisms, coordinate the handling of cross-jurisdictional complaints and regularly publish information on complaints, determinations, sanctions and redress outcomes. These measures would strengthen consumer protection and

latest.title: Artificial intelligence readiness and perceived e-invoicing regulatory compliance: The mediating role of e-invoicing capability in Malaysian SMEs
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) readiness has become increasingly salient for organisations operating in digitally administered regulatory environments. Nevertheless, scant research has examined how organisational readiness for AI translates into capabilities that support digital compliance activities. This study aimed to empirically test the effects of Artificial Intelligence Readiness (AIR) on Perceived e-Invoicing Regulatory Compliance (PEIRC) of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) operating in Malaysia and examine the mediating role of e-Invoicing Capability (EIC). Conceptually bridging the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capability Theory, the authors develop a resource–capability–compliance framework that explains how technological, human, data, and managerial resources are translated into perceived regulatory compliance. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was administered to collect primary data from SMEs across Malaysia’s major economic hubs. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was employed to test the hypothesised relationships. The results reveal that AIR is positively associated with EIC (β = 0.609; p < 0.001) and PEIRC (β = 0.712; p < 0.001). EIC is also positively associated with PEIRC (β = 0.187; p = 0.001). EIC partially mediates the relationship between AIR and PEIRC (β = 0.114; p = 0.005). This study contributes to digital transformation literature by providing evidence that perceived regulatory compliance is associated with both AI readiness and domain-specific organisational capability. The study also reinforces the importance of coupling technological preparedness with organisational capability-building efforts amongst firms operating in digitally regulated environments.

latest.title: Linking ethics and CSR with business sustainability as a strategy for achieving the SDGs: A aystematic review from 2016 to 2025
latest.abstract: In sustainability research, the understanding of the links between corporate social responsibility (CSR), business ethics, business sustainability, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is gaining in importance. However, the literature remains fragmented, with these themes being addressed in isolation rather than as interrelated facets of responsible business conduct. This study, therefore, attempts to analyze the role of ethics and CSR in business sustainability and in making the attainment of the SDGs possible. A systematic literature review (SLR) was performed following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) format, including publications published between 2016 and 2025. The review synthesizes significant methods, difficulties, and emerging patterns in the literature and suggests an integrated framework that explains the links among ethics, CSR, business sustainability, and SDG attainment. The report also sets a future research agenda based on these findings to deepen theoretical and empirical understanding of these interrelated areas.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Understanding digital platform ecosystems: A scoping review, integrative framework, and research agenda
latest.abstract: Digital platform ecosystems (DPEs) have become central socio-technical arrangements for digital innovation, industry transformation, and business model renewal. Yet DPE research remains fragmented across studies that examine ecosystem emergence, operation, and impacts separately. Thus, we conduct a scoping review of information systems and related research to clarify what constitutes a DPE and to theorize how DPE dynamics unfold. Synthesizing prior definitions, we identify four constitutive dimensions: a focal digital platform, heterogeneous but interdependent actors, platform-mediated value creation and capture, and governance mechanisms embedded in broader environmental conditions. Synthesizing prior research on the drivers, evolutionary dynamics, and impacts of DPEs, we develop a complex adaptive systems-informed framework that explains DPE dynamics as a recursive, multi-level process. We show how platform structuring and actor enactment generate meso-level relational crystallization, how these relational patterns consolidate into ecosystem structures of power, capabilities, and dependence, and how such structures feed back into subsequent governance and actor behavior under environmental coupling. By recasting DPE dynamics as a set of multi-level mechanisms rather than descriptive labels, our review also identifies a new agenda for future research.

latest.title: A Sequential Process Framework for ESG Activation: Translating Platform Capabilities Into Organizational Performance
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT This study proposes a sequential process through which organizations translate data collected and managed by environmental, social, and governance (ESG) platforms into institutionalized sustainability performance shifting the attention from ESG measurement for reporting to data activation for the organizational strategy. We develop an integrated framework and empirically test it using survey data from 580 corporate entities headquartered in EU‐27 countries and subject to Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD)‐related disclosure obligations. The data are analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM). The empirical results highlight, on the one hand, the ability of the ESG platform to act as a critical technological antecedent capable of significantly driving ESG–management by objectives (MBO) integration ( β = 0.542); and, on the other hand, how the integration of sustainability metrics into performance management systems directly promotes the rigorous alignment of managerial incentive structures ( β = 0.612), while exerting a significant direct effect on overall sustainability performance ( β = 0.276). The paper highlights how it is possible to turn double materiality and regulatory demands into integrated control mechanisms, showing that ESG tracking delivers value only when coupled with data‐driven MBO and ESG‐linked compensation.

latest.title: Trusting GenAI Shopping Assistants: A Trust-Mediated Benefit–Risk Model with AI Literacy: Evidence from Saudi E-Commerce
latest.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
latest.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) shopping assistants can provide personalized shopping guidance while raising concerns about conversational data use. Drawing on privacy calculus, trust theory, and information systems success logic, this study examines a Trust-mediated benefit–risk model using cross-sectional survey data from 295 consumers in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with prior GenAI shopping-assistant experience. Partial least squares structural equation modeling indicates that perceived conversational quality is positively associated with Personalization Value (β = 0.563) and Privacy Concern (β = 0.235). Personalization Value is positively associated with Trust (β = 0.514), while Privacy Concern is negatively associated with Trust (β = −0.122). Trust is strongly associated with Purchase Intention (β = 0.731). The relationship between Privacy Concern and Trust is less negative at higher levels of self-assessed overall AI Literacy (interaction β = 0.144). Additional analyses indicate complementary partial mediation for Personalization Value and indirect-only mediation for Privacy Concern. The findings suggest that valued personalization and Privacy Concern can coexist during AI-assisted shopping, with Trust linking these appraisals to Purchase Intention. AI Literacy is interpreted as a global self-assessment rather than empirically separable competencies. Given the cross-sectional, non-experimental design, all findings reflect associations rather than causal effects.

latest.title: From experience to loyalty: A conceptual framework for building customer–brand relationships in retailing
latest.abstract: Brand loyalty has emerged as a critical factor amid intensifying competition in the retail sector. It serves as a key driver of brand equity, as loyal customers are more likely to engage in repeat purchase behaviour and promote the brand through positive word-of-mouth. Consequently, brand loyalty contributes significantly to customer retention and long-term business profitability. Sustaining brand loyalty has become increasingly challenging, as consumers are exposed to a growing number of competing brands and alternatives. Previous studies have examined the individual effects of retail brand experience (RBE), brand satisfaction, brand trust, and brand love on brand loyalty. However, limited research attention has been given to how these constructs interrelate and jointly influence brand loyalty within the retail context. This conceptual paper has thus developed an integrated framework comprising 11 formal propositions, grounded in the Stimulus–Organism–Response Theory and Expectancy-Disconfirmation Theory. The model conceptualises RBE as the stimulus; brand satisfaction, brand trust, and brand love as the cognitive, relational, and emotional states representing the organism; and brand loyalty as the consumer response, encompassing attitudinal and behavioural aspects. The proposed conceptual model will serve as a foundation for future empirical research and contribute to both academic knowledge and managerial understanding of brand management and consumer behaviour.

latest.title: Less Disclosed, More Minimal: How Soft Launches of Romantic Relationships Promote Minimalist Consumption
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Soft and hard launches of romantic relationships have become increasingly prevalent forms of relationship disclosure in digital environments, yet little is known about whether these forms of disclosure influence subsequent consumer behavior. Across four experiments, we show that soft (vs. hard) relationship disclosures increase consumers' preference for minimalist consumption. We identify preference for subtle self‐presentation as a potential explanatory mechanism underlying this effect: soft relationship disclosures increase preference for subtle self‐presentation, which subsequently enhances preference for minimalist consumption. Relationship privacy orientation moderates this process, such that the indirect effect of soft launch on minimalist consumption via preference for subtle self‐presentation strengthens as relation privacy increases. A marketplace urgency cue also moderates this process, such that the indirect effect holds when the cue is absent but diminishes when it is present. These findings demonstrate how romantic relationship disclosure types influence subsequent marketplace preferences.

latest.title: Ergo-iconic value resonance in heritage tourism: A descriptive survey study of traditional Panggong House of Belitung, Indonesia
latest.abstract: Heritage tourism in Indonesia stands at a pivotal intersection where traditional cultural spaces must serve simultaneously as living archives and competitive tourism destinations. This study explores how ergo-iconic value, understood as the convergence of ergonomic functional design and iconic cultural symbolism embedded in vernacular architecture, resonates with visitor experience at Traditional Panggong House of Belitung, a traditional stilt dwelling indigenous to Bangka Belitung Province, Indonesia. Employing a descriptive narrative approach, data were gathered from 150 domestic and international visitors through a structured questionnaire utilising a five-point Likert scale. Seven constructs are examined: Heritage Tourism, Ergo-Iconic Value, Cultural Authenticity, Destination Branding, Visitor Engagement, Tourist Satisfaction, and Enhancement of Tourism Experience. Descriptive analysis reveals that Ergo-Iconic Value records the highest mean perception score (M = 4.12), followed by Enhancement of Tourism Experience (M = 4.05) and Visitor Engagement (M = 3.98), indicating that visitors hold distinctly positive perceptions of the architectural and experiential qualities of Traditional Panggong House of Belitung. The study proposes a theoretical model linking these constructs through eight directional propositions intended to guide future structural equation modelling research; these propositions are not tested in the present study. Findings carry substantive descriptive implications for heritage destination managers seeking to leverage architectural identity as a marketing asset across the Asia Pacific region.

latest.title: Towards Green Innovation: Impact of Green Entrepreneurial Orientation on Green Product Development with a Mediating Role of Green Creative Behaviour
latest.venue: Open Access Organization and Management Review
latest.abstract: Recently, Green Product Development (GPD) has gained broad acceptance in academia, business, and the research community and has become an important part of a company's growth in the era of environmentalism. This study aimed to explore new dimensions that will improve Green Product Development by exploiting certain important variables such as Green Entrepreneurial Orientation (GEO) and Green Creative Behaviour (GCB). The research framework is based on the Natural Resource-Based View (NRBV) theory to examine the relationships among the GEO, GPD, and GCB constructs. Data were obtained from a sample of employees working in manufacturing SMEs (ISO 14001 certified), using a structured survey questionnaire. The results confirmed that GEO significantly influences GPD both directly and through the GCB, thereby validating the role of creative behaviour as a mediator. Model fit indices demonstrated strong reliability and validity, ensuring robustness of the findings. The outcomes provide empirical evidence that GEO-driven practices foster innovative green product initiatives, reinforcing the strategic importance of creativity in sustainable entrepreneurship. The results provide a substantial theoretical contribution to current literature. This study will help researchers to understand the variation in GEO and GPD from different aspects. The proposed study also suggests new insights for SMEs to reinforce green entrepreneurial orientation practices as part of their firm's strategies to attain a highly competitive advantage.

latest.title: Analysis of the Effectiveness of Upskilling Programs in Improving Agent Performance to Face Market Dynamics
latest.abstract: The rapidly evolving sales environment requires sales agents to continuously enhance their competencies to respond effectively to changing market demands. However, the effectiveness of upskilling programs in improving job performance remains insufficiently understood, particularly from the perspectives of sales agents themselves. This study aimed to examine the implementation of upskilling programs for sales agents, explore their experiences in applying newly acquired skills during customer interactions, and identify the facilitating factors and barriers influencing the transfer of training to workplace practices amid changing market conditions. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, with data collected through semi-structured interviews, observations of sales activities, and document analysis involving sales agents and supervisors. The findings revealed that formal training enhanced agents' conceptual understanding of products and sales procedures, while informal knowledge sharing among colleagues reinforced their practical competencies. Nevertheless, the transfer of acquired knowledge and skills into consistent workplace behaviors was not automatic but depended on opportunities for practical application, the quality of supervisory feedback, peer support, and the alignment of training content with actual customer needs and sales situations. Operational constraints, including demanding sales targets and administrative workloads, further limited agents' opportunities to apply newly acquired skills. The study concluded that the effectiveness of upskilling programs should be evaluated through a multidimensional framework encompassing training content relevance, participant comprehension, opportunities for practical application, organizational and peer support, an

latest.title: Examining the role of artificial intelligence and social media marketing activities through the brand resonance model
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractIn an era where digital technologies are rapidly transforming consumer behavior, e-commerce platforms have emerged as primary channels for purchasing goods. This shift has prompted organizations to adapt their marketing strategies to increasingly competitive digital environments, particularly by applying artificial intelligence and social media to build consumer relationships and strengthen customer-based brand equity. This study aims to examine the effects of Artificial Intelligence Marketing Activities (AIMA) and Social Media Marketing Activities (SMMA) on brand resonance, using Keller’s brand resonance model as the main theoretical framework. Data were collected through an online survey from 210 respondents in Thailand and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that both AIMA and SMMA have significant positive effects on brand salience, brand performance, and brand imagery. These constructs subsequently influence brand judgments and feelings, ultimately leading to brand resonance. The findings extend the application of the brand resonance model to the digital marketing context, contribute to a deeper understanding of how AI-driven and social media marketing can be effectively managed on digital platforms, and provide practical implications for developing marketing strategies aimed at strengthening brand equity.AcknowledgementsThe authors would like to thank all participants for their contribution to this study.

latest.title: Which review cues matter most? Perceived authenticity as the dominant predictor of purchase intention toward Indonesian local fashion brands
latest.abstract: In digital fashion markets, consumers navigate a complex landscape of online reviews, although the cues they prioritize when evaluating local brands remain poorly understood. Grounded in signalling theory and the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM), this study develops a multi-cue framework examining how review content quality, review source credibility, perceived review authenticity, and emotional tone collectively predict purchase intention toward local fashion brands. Drawing on survey data from Generation Z consumers in Indonesia analyzed through PLS-SEM, the findings reveal a signal hierarchy: perceived review authenticity consistently emerges as the dominant evaluative cue, outweighing informational and credibility-based signals alike. This pattern suggests that consumers in identity-driven consumption contexts prioritize legitimacy verification above argument evaluation, a finding that departs from prior ELM-based review research in which argument quality typically dominates. Theoretically, the study contributes to signalling theory by suggesting that signal effectiveness depends on imitation cost relative to the prevailing manipulation environment and identifies a scope condition for ELM in contexts where message authenticity cannot be presumed. Practically, local fashion brands are advised to cultivate authentic consumer narratives rather than optimizing review volume or aggregate ratings.

latest.title: Do Sustainable Agricultural Technologies Induce Greenwashing? Evidence From Agricultural Firms in Emerging Markets
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Sustainable agricultural technologies provide an important pathway for emerging economies to achieve the coordinated development of environmental protection and food security. However, due to the lag in the realization of technological benefits, agricultural firms may rely on impression management to convey green commitments during the early stages of technology adoption, thereby engaging in greenwashing behaviors. Therefore, whether sustainable agricultural technologies can truly improve environmental performance remains an important question. Based on impression management theory and legitimacy theory, this study examines the impact of sustainable agricultural technologies on corporate greenwashing behaviors and their boundary conditions using a sample of representative agricultural firms from the largest emerging economy and firm‐level panel data from 2011 to 2024. The results show that sustainable agricultural technologies have a significant inverted U‐shaped relationship with greenwashing behaviors, with impression management providing an important behavioral explanation for this relationship. Furthermore, agricultural supply chain characteristics significantly influence this inverted U‐shaped relationship, with factors such as inventory turnover, cooperation stability, and information transparency constituting important boundary conditions for the impact of sustainable agricultural technologies on greenwashing behaviors. Finally, legitimacy pressures arising from food security policies, ecological legitimacy requirements, and innovation‐oriented expectations in emerging markets serve as important contextual factors influencing the inverted U‐shaped relationship between sustainable agricultural technologies and greenwashing.

latest.title: Pengaruh Personalisasi Rekomendasi Produk Terhadap Perilaku Pembelian Konsumen Dengan Trust Sebagai Variabel Mediasi Pada Pengguna Shopee
latest.abstract: Product recommendation personalization helps e-commerce platform users find products that match their needs and preferences. This study examines the effect of Product Recommendation Personalization on Trust, the effect of Trust on Purchase Behavior, and the mediating role of Trust among Shopee users based on the Stimulus–Organism–Response (S-O-R) framework. A quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design was employed. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using purposive sampling, resulting in 111 eligible respondents, comprising 72.07% male and 27.93% female respondents aged 14–69 years. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4 with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. The results indicate that Product Recommendation Personalization has a positive and significant effect on Trust (β = 0.696; p < 0.001). Trust also has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Behavior (β = 0.719; p < 0.001). The indirect effect of Product Recommendation Personalization on Purchase Behavior through Trust is also significant (β = 0.501; p < 0.001), confirming the mediating role of Trust. These findings support the S-O-R mechanism and highlight the importance of recommendation relevance and user trust in supporting online purchasing behavior.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
hot.abstract: Abstract Chatbots are now able to engage in sophisticated conversations with consumers in the domain of relationships, providing a potential coping solution to widescale societal loneliness. Behavioral research provides little insight into whether these applications (apps) are effective at alleviating loneliness. We address this question by focusing on “artificial intelligence (AI) companions”: apps designed to provide consumers with synthetic interaction partners. Study 1 examines user reviews of AI companion apps and finds correlational evidence suggesting that these apps help alleviate loneliness. Study 2 finds that AI companions successfully alleviate loneliness on par only with interacting with another person and more than other activities such as watching YouTube videos. Moreover, consumers underestimate the degree to which AI companions improve their loneliness. Study 3 uses a longitudinal design and finds that an AI companion consistently provides momentary reductions in loneliness after use over the course of a week. Study 4 provides evidence that both the chatbots’ performance and, especially, whether it makes users feel heard, explain reductions in loneliness. Study 5 provides an additional robustness check for the loneliness-alleviating benefits of AI companions and shows that self-disclosure and distraction alone do not explain AI companions’ effectiveness.

hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Abstract Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
Factors of Customer Loyalty and Retention in the Digital Environment
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Customer loyalty and retention are crucial for digital platforms, yet systematic studies integrating technological innovation and loyalty strategies remain scarce. This study addresses this gap by conducting a bibliometric analysis of key factors influencing customer retention in the digital environment. Our research employs a quantitative bibliometric approach using the Biblioshiny and Bibliometrix tools (RStudio 2022.02), analyzing 300 scientific articles from the Web of Science database (2021–2024). This study applies bibliometric techniques such as descriptive metrics, bibliographic coupling, co-citation, and scientific collaboration mapping to identify trends and thematic clusters. Our findings indicate that emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data, significantly impact customer experience, trust, and engagement. Personalization and digital innovation emerge as fundamental drivers of customer retention, offering strategic insights for companies aiming to strengthen competitiveness in the global digital market.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Impact of digital transformation on SME’s marketing performance: role of social media and market turbulence
hot.abstract: Despite the rising relevance of digital transformation, there is still a knowledge vacuum due to limited literature available on digital transformation. This study aims to examine the impact of digital transformation on the marketing performance of small and medium enterprises.
