latest.title: Analisis Kredibilitas Konten Instagram Terhadap Kepercayaan Calon Jamaah Milenial dalam Perumusan Strategi Konten (Studi Kasus PT An-Nahl Umrah dan Haji)
latest.abstract: Increasing number of Umrah and Hajj pilgrims, where the tight competition among travel agencies in the digital era, and the rise of travel agency fraud cases through social media have created a crisis in the level of trust of prospective pilgrims, especially millennials as active Instagram users. This study aims to analyze the influence of the credibility of Instagram content on the trust of prospective millennial pilgrims in order to provide content strategy recommendations for PT An-Nahl Umrah and Hajj. This study uses a quantitative approach with a survey method. The sampling technique in this study use purposive sampling with 75 respondents. Data were collected through a Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using validity, reliability, classical assumptions and multiple linear regression through the SPSS 26 program. The analysis shows that simultaneously, the three indicators have significant influence on trust, with an F value of 34.193, and partially only the trustworthiness indicator has a dominant influence on trust of β = 0.598, while expertise and attractiveness partially do not have a significant influence on trust. From the results of this study it can be concluded that transparency, honesty and accuracy of information such as testimonial content are the main factors in building trust among prospective millennial pilgrims.

latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan dan Electronic Word of Mouth (eWOM) Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian pada Koka Ramen Express Sudirman
latest.venue: Jurnal Penelitian Ekonomi Manajemen dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: The increasingly competitive culinary industry requires businesses to improve service quality and manage their digital reputation to influence consumer purchasing decisions. This study aims to examine the effects of service quality and Electronic Word of Mouth (eWOM) on purchasing decisions among consumers of Koka Ramen Express Sudirman, both partially and simultaneously. This research employs a quantitative approach with a causal associative design. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using purposive sampling involving 120 respondents who had previously purchased and consumed products at Koka Ramen Express Sudirman. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics 29. The results indicate that service quality has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.207 and a significance level of less than 0.001. Electronic Word of Mouth also has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.184 and a significance level of less than 0.001. Simultaneously, both variables have a significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a coefficient of determination of 63.6%. Service quality is the more dominant factor influencing purchasing decisions compared to eWOM. These findings imply that management should improve employee friendliness, service speed, and restaurant cleanliness while optimizing social media activities and responding professionally to customer reviews to strengthen consumer confidence in making purchasing decisions.

latest.title: Analisis Daya Saing dan Kinerja Ekspor Karet Alam Indonesia dan Thailand di Pasar Korea Selatan
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis dan membandingkan keunggulan komparatif serta posisi spesialisasi perdagangan karet alam (HS 4001) antara Indonesia dan Thailand di pasar Korea Selatan periode 2016–2025. Menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif deskriptif komparatif, data sekunder time-series bersumber dari ITC Trade Map dianalisis dengan metode Revealed Comparative Advantage (RCA), Revealed Symmetric Comparative Advantage (RSCA), dan Trade Specialization Index (TSI). Hasil analisis RSCA menunjukkan bahwa Indonesia (0,84–0,94) dan Thailand (0,93–0,97) secara konsisten memiliki keunggulan komparatif yang sangat kuat (RSCA > 0) di pasar Korea Selatan. Meskipun demikian, daya saing Thailand relatif lebih stabil dibanding Indonesia yang mengalami tren penurunan di paruh akhir pengamatan. Hasil analisis TSI mengonfirmasi bahwa kedua negara bertindak sebagai eksportir bersih (net exporter) utama dengan nilai mendekati 1,00. Fluktuasi moderat pada nilai TSI Indonesia merefleksikan adanya penyesuaian impor bahan baku guna memenuhi kebutuhan industri pengolahan hilir domestik. Untuk menjaga kesinambungan ekspor, kebijakan strategis perlu difokuskan pada peremajaan tanaman karet, efisiensi rantai pasok, standardisasi mutu, dan percepatan hilirisasi produk.

latest.title: Knowledge Management Capabilities and Performance of Tier 1 Deposit-Taking SACCOs in Kenya
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
latest.abstract: The main objective of this study was to determine the influence of knowledge management capabilities on the performance of Tier 1 Deposit-Taking SACCOs (DT-SACCOs) in Kenya. Knowledge management capabilities were conceptualized as a second-order dynamic capability comprising knowledge acquisition, knowledge sharing and knowledge application. A mixed methods approach was applied, drawing data from finance, audit, credit, Front Office Service Activity (FOSA), marketing, and Information and Communication Technology (ICT) management staff across the 42 Tier 1 DT-SACCOs licensed by the Sacco Societies Regulatory Authority (SASRA) in Kenya. A census approach was adopted, and data were collected using structured questionnaires and analyzed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS), with descriptive statistics and simple linear regression guiding interpretation. The descriptive findings indicated moderate adoption of knowledge management practices, with item means ranging from 2.09 to 3.46. Knowledge management capabilities were found to enhance collaboration, information sharing and decision-making, although limited knowledge application and weak knowledge-tracking mechanisms restricted optimal performance gains. Simple linear regression established that knowledge management capabilities had a statistically significant and positive influence on performance, explaining 56.8% of the variance in performance (R² = .568, Adjusted R² = .566, F(1, 249) = 327.248, p < .001; B = .719, β = .754, t = 18.090, p < .001), leading to rejection of the null hypothesis. The study recommends strategic prioritisation of knowledge management systems, particularly knowledge application and knowledge-tracking mechanisms, to improve competitiveness, operational resilience and susta

latest.title: Stakeholder Patronage as Influencers Of Micro-Enterprise Growth At Kamukunji In Nairobi, Kenya
latest.abstract: Several studies show that significant relationship exists between stakeholder patronage and micro-enterprise growth. Although the roles of factors such as family, friends, debtors, employees, and partners have been widely studied, their influences on growth of sales, employees, departments, and divisions have been generally ignored. To bridge this gap, the paper investigates how stakeholder patronage of 354 micro-enterprises sampled from Kamukunji Jua Kali Association membership register impacts positively or negatively on vertical and horizontal growth. Data were collected using in a face-toface interview using a self-administered structured questionnaire and analysed by factor and multi-level analyses. Results indicate that stakeholder patronage model (65.33 percent variance explained), Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin measure of sampling adequacy (KMO = .87) and Bartlett s test of sphericity (.001) remain conceptually valid. Tests of 13 hypotheses indicates that stakeholder patronage of 76.92 percent acceptance moderately influence growth.

latest.title: Who Leads and Who Follows? Predicting Leadership Initiative and Success in Problem-Solving Groups
latest.abstract: Research on leadership emergence has long sought to identify the individual characteristics that predict who comes to occupy leadership roles in groups. However, most studies treat leadership emergence as a single outcome, making it difficult to determine whether predictors influence the propensity to attempt leadership, the likelihood of attracting followers, or both. We conceptualize leadership emergence as a two-stage process consisting of leadership initiative (i.e., attempts to influence the group) and leadership success (i.e., the extent to which those attempts attract follower endorsement). This distinction provides a framework for integrating diverse theoretical perspectives on leadership emergence, as different predictors may influence different stages of this process. Across two laboratory studies (total N = 754), we assessed both components on a behavioral level and examined a range of predictors, including intelligence, personality traits, motivational dispositions, status-based cues, and testosterone. Results showed that only a small subset of attributes was associated with either component of leadership emergence. In the pooled sample, intelligence was the only predictor of both leadership initiative and leadership success, with no significant difference between the two studies. Extraversion and subjective competence predicted leadership initiative but not leadership success, which was additionally predicted by the frequency of leadership initiative. Taken together, our findings demonstrate how distinguishing leadership initiative from leadership success can clarify which individual attributes shape each stage of the leadership emergence process.

latest.title: Exploring the role of nicotine and smoking in sleep behaviours: A multi‐variable Mendelian randomisation study
latest.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Increased nicotine exposure (resulting from greater cigarette consumption and/or slower nicotine metabolism) may directly affect sleep and could underlie relationships between smoking and sleep behaviours identified previously. We conducted a Mendelian randomisation (MR) study to explore whether nicotine metabolism has a causal effect on sleep behaviours. DESIGN: Our main analysis method was inverse-variance weighted (IVW) Multivariable MR, which was used to examine the independent effects of nicotine metabolism and smoking heaviness on sleep behaviours. The model was developed to provide insights into the potential role of nicotine exposure. SETTING AND PARTICIPANTS: The genome-wide association summary data for these analyses were sourced from published genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary-level data, or GWAS conducted within the UK Biobank. Primary analyses focused on current smokers of European descent (N = 5185 to 487 153). MEASUREMENTS: We used genetic proxies of the nicotine metabolite ratio (NMR), cigarettes per day (CPD), and sleep behaviours (chronotype [being an "evening" person versus a "morning" person], ease of getting up in the morning, insomnia symptoms, napping, daytime sleepiness and sleep duration). RESULTS: Higher NMR (consistent with lower circulating nicotine levels per cigarette smoked) decreased the likelihood of being an "evening" person when accounting for CPD in current smokers [beta coefficient (β) = -0.04, 95% confidence interval (CI) -0.06 to -0.02, p < 0.001]. A higher NMR also increased the ease of getting up (β = 0.02, 95%CI 0.01 to 0.04, p = 0.001) and likelihood of napping (β = 0.02, 95%CI 0.01 to 0.03, p < 0.001) in current smokers. There was no consistent evidence for effects of NMR or CPD on insomnia symp

latest.title: Shadows on the Crossroads: Childhood Exposure to Co-resident Parental Death in the United States Increases, 1999–2023
Scientific exploration outlasts industrial momentum and sustains innovation in genetic research: survey of 20 million papers and patents
latest.abstract: Long-term innovation depends not only on discovering new elements but also on facilitating new recombination at the time of their co-availability. This notion of combinatorial innovation raises the question about whether scientific exploration and industry research persist over similar time horizons to meet innovative opportunities. Here, we analyze about 20 million papers and US, Chinese, and European patents to compare the courses of scientific and industrial activities in genetic research, a domain of far-reaching societal importance. We observe that research on new genes has declined since the early 2000s, but the exploration of novel gene combinations remains active for biotechnology innovation. Yet, fields of highly practical or commercial focus are less likely to test novel gene combinations. Furthermore, industry R&D on each gene tends to decline earlier than scientific interest in that gene. After this decline of the industrial momentum, continuous scientific research still sustains exploratory and innovative opportunities, involving novel gene combinations, clinical trials, and technologically-impactful work. Based on a hypothetical scenario of over-aligned science and industry, we estimate that up to 42.2–74.4% of the combinational opportunities would be unexplored if scientific research becomes hindered due to industry’s retreat. This study suggests the potential complementary roles of scientific and industrial research with different temporal modes in innovation cycles, calling for balanced policies to foster innovation ecosystems.

latest.title: Noun-adjective collocations in L2 Portuguese: Exploring the effects of proficiency and native language in a large-scale learner corpus
latest.venue: International Journal of Learner Corpus Research
latest.abstract: Abstract In this study, we investigated the development of phraseological knowledge in Portuguese second language learners, focusing on noun–adjective combinations through the lenses of phrasal frequency, association strength, and accuracy. We analysed essays from 693 learners across five proficiency levels, representing 18 typologically diverse first languages (L1). Learners’ use of noun–adjective combinations was examined using four association measures — phrase frequency, mutual information, log dice, and delta P (ΔP) — as well as the accuracy of use. Findings reveal that phraseological development is not linear; advanced learners produced less frequent and less strongly-associated combinations, suggesting a shift toward more varied or creative expressions. L1 word order typology did not influence phrase frequency or association strength, but learners from noun–adjective dominant L1s produced collocations more accurately, indicating a dissociation between accuracy and idiomaticity. Accuracy followed a U-shaped developmental trajectory. Overall, the results highlight the complex interplay of learner and input-related variables in L2 phraseological development.

latest.title: A moderation examination of the effects of a mindfulness-based intervention on primary school students’ symptoms of inattention, depression, and anxiety
latest.abstract: Abstract The number of mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) has proliferated in the last decade, as accessible evidence-based practices, to improve children’s mental health in school settings. However, some studies suggest that MBIs do not offer distinct advantages over other mental health promotion interventions. These inconsistent findings may be explained, at least in part, by the lack of a clear definition of what constitutes a MBI, inconsistencies in intervention length and facilitator training, and importantly, the limited examination of moderating variables––particularly dispositional mindfulness, emotional regulation, and social competence––that may influence intervention effectiveness and mental health outcomes (inattention, anxiety, and depression). The present study was therefore interested in the potential benefits associated with a case of this type of intervention and aimed to explore whether dispositional (i.e., trait) mindfulness and mental health indicators evolved over time in primary school children. A secondary objective meant to evaluate whether receiving a MBI could moderate the relationship between changes in mindfulness and changes in mental health indicators. Contrary to our hypothesis, results showed that mindfulness levels were linked with indicators of mental health. Specifically, changes in mindfulness were associated with increases in inattention, anxiety and depression using structural equation modelling. Moreover, the association between changes in mindfulness and inattention differed by intervention group, with greater increases in mindfulness associated with greater increases in inattention in the control group but not in the intervention group. Results thus lend support to exercising caution when aiming to only foster mindfulness abi

latest.title: Residual Self-Guided Quantum Vision Adversarial Attention Network for Predicting AI-Driven Financial Performance in Automobile Industries
latest.abstract: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in the automobile banking industry and its impact on the business processes is very fast, the impact of AI techniques in financial performance is not fully understood. The challenge here is that banks involved in the automotive sector often have fragmented disclosures of AI and inconsistent metrics, making it challenging to come up with accurate predictions of the financial impact of AI. To address this gap, they propose a model known as “Residual Self-Guided Quantum Vision Adversarial Attention Network for Predicting AI-Driven Financial Performance in Automobile Industries. To fill this gap, they propose a model called “Residual Self-Guided Quantum Vision Adversarial Attention Network for Predicting AI-Driven Financial Performance in Automobile Industries.in the automobile banking industry has transformed business processes, yet how AI techniques influence financial performance is not yet fully understood. The difficulty here lies in scattered AI disclosures and disparate metrics that hinder effective forecasts of financial results in car-related banks. In order to bridge this gap, the research introduces a model called “Residual Self-Guided Quantum Vision Adversarial Attention Network for Predicting AI-Driven Financial Performance in Automobile Industries.” The analysis relies on a dataset called “AI Techniques on Financial Performance of Automobile Industries,” which contains 131 annual report records for sixteen Indian-listed banks from 2015 to 2023. This dataset captures keyword-based AI disclosures, as well as institutional and financial indicators. Data pre-processing is done through the use of the Correlation Coefficient with Min–Max Weighted (CCMMW) method to normalize and fine-tune the input parameters, while

latest.title: The Role of Adverse Childhood Experiences in the Prospective Link Between Sleep-Affect Spillover and Anxiety Symptoms: A Daily Diary Study Combined With Panel Data
latest.abstract: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) carry enduring consequences, yet their role in shaping both real-time emotional reactivity and long-term vulnerability remains underexplored. We investigated how ACEs and their dimensions (threat, deprivation) influence sleep-affect spillover—individual differences in the coupling between prior-night sleep-onset difficulty and next-day negative affect (NA)—and whether spillover predicts later anxiety. Leveraging a rich multiple-time-scale data set (sample size: N = 420; diaries: N = 10,680), we employed multilevel modeling to capture individual-specific spillover effects. Nights of greater sleep-onset difficulty predicted higher next-day NA at within- and between-persons levels. Mediation analyses did not support spillover as a pathway from ACEs to anxiety. Instead, moderation analyses showed ACEs amplified the spillover-anxiety association: Stronger spillover predicted elevated anxiety among individuals experiencing more ACEs. Findings highlight that ACEs function less as direct antecedents and more as amplifiers of dynamic processes of emotional reactivity that consolidate into psychopathology.

latest.title: The incidence of disruptive behaviour disorders and comorbid ADHD diagnoses: a register‑based study of perinatal and psychosocial factors
latest.venue: Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Mental Health
latest.abstract: Abstract Background Disruptive behaviour disorders (DBDs) frequently occur alongside attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD); however, the current incidence and extent of this overlap remain unclear. We aimed to estimate the cumulative incidence of DBD diagnoses and their comorbidity with ADHD and the trends in the incidences over time. Methods We used register data of live-born children from 2001–2005 (N = 282,773). The cumulative incidence of DBD diagnoses up to age 12 was studied. DBDs were defined by conduct disorder (CD, F91.x) and mixed disorders of conduct and emotions (F92.x), based on the 10th International Classification of Diseases. Concomitant ADHD (F90.x, F98.8) diagnoses were examined, and analyses were adjusted for perinatal and psychosocial factors. Results The cumulative incidence of CD and mixed disorder of conduct and emotions diagnoses were 0.8% (2,208) and 1.5% (4,128) respectively in 269,490 study children followed up to 12 years. The cumulative incidence of DBDs varied by cohort and was higher in later-born cohorts. In boys, incidence increased from 2.8% in the 2001 cohort to 3.3% in the 2005 cohort, and in girls from 0.8% to 1.1% (p < 0.0001 and p = 0.0007, respectively). Among 5,573 children with a DBD diagnosis (763 with both F91.x and F92.x diagnoses), 40.6% (n = 2,260) had comorbid ADHD. The DBD–ADHD comorbidity was more likely (adjusted odds ratio [95% Confidence Intervals]) among children whose mothers smoked during pregnancy (2.6 [2.4–2.9]), were single (1.8 [1.6–2.1]), were unemployed (1.2 [1.1–1.3]) or had a psychiatric disorder between pregnancy and the child’s first four years (2.5 [2.2–2.8]), as well as among boys (6.8 [6.0–7.8]). Over the cohorts, ADHD diagnosis increased in boys with DBDs diagnosis (p<0.05), but not in girls

latest.title: Potentially modifiable mediators of the association between child abuse and dementia
latest.abstract: Background: Literature investigating mediation of the association between child abuse and dementia has largely considered composite adverse childhood experience scores rather than individual adverse experiences, despite evidence that different experiences have different impacts on dementia risk. Additionally, prior studies consider mediators in isolation, despite known associations between mediators which may impact indirect pathways from child abuse to dementia. Objectives: To investigate whether potentially modifiable health and lifestyle factors mediate the association between child abuse and dementia. Methods: We used data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing to investigate associations between child abuse and dementia (N:5,448). Indirect pathways through four mediator categories (education, health behaviours, mental health and cardiovascular health) were examined. We used regression modelling to estimate associations between child abuse, mediators and dementia, and causal mediation analysis using the g-formula to estimate the joint indirect effect through the mediators. Results: Individuals who experienced child abuse had, on average, an 80% higher hazard of dementia, compared to those who did not (RTE HR:1.80, 95% CI:1.21-2.39). Mental health mediators showed strong associations with both child abuse and dementia. Evidence for other mediators was weaker. Education, health behaviours, mental health and cardiovascular health mediated approximately 18% of the association. Sensitivity analysis revealed that almost all this mediation occurred through mental health. Conclusions: Child abuse was associated with higher risk of dementia. Joint mediation analysis suggested that education, health behaviours, cardiovascular health, and mental health accounted for a r

latest.title: The social cure effects of United Voices: a randomized waitlist-controlled pilot trial of an online group-singing intervention for older adults with HIV
latest.abstract: Introduction Older adults with HIV experience increasing loneliness and social isolation as they age with the stigma of HIV. Group singing is a promising social identity approach but remains largely understudied among people with stigmatizing health conditions. Based on our conceptual model, we developed United Voices (UV), a group-singing intervention for older adults with HIV to mitigate the impacts of stigma on loneliness and social isolation. Methods We conducted a randomized, waitlist-controlled pilot trial of UV to evaluate its feasibility and acceptability. A total of 23 people with HIV ages 50 years and older were randomized into immediate- (n=13) or delayed-start (n=10) group of 12 weekly 90-minute group-singing sessions via Zoom during COVID-19. Psychosocial and behavioral measures were administered at baseline, 6- and 12-weeks, and semi-structured exit interviews were conducted. Results Of four a priori feasibility thresholds, only enrollment was met (6.8 per week vs. 6). Of 27 enrolled participants, 23 (85%) were randomized (threshold 100%). Of 13 randomized to the immediate-start arm, 9 (69.2%) completed baseline (threshold 80%); of these, 7 (77.8%) attended at least 10 of 12 rehearsals and 7 (77.8%) completed both follow-up assessments (thresholds 80%). Among the 7 participants who completed the acceptability survey, the 80% benchmark was met for staff support (100%), information provided, the study website, rehearsal structure, and confidence in ability to participate (86% each), but not for overall satisfaction with the choir (71%) or the research study (57%). Exit interviews from 4 of the 13 participants randomized to the immediate-start arm indicated that while participants were at first skeptical regarding online group-singing, the experience was enjo

latest.title: Haematological alterations associated with panic disorder among Sri Lankan university students: a preliminary case-control study
latest.abstract: Panic disorder (PD) is a significant mental health concern in Sri Lanka, with a prevalence of 14% exceeding global averages. However, its pathophysiology remains unexplored locally. This preliminary case-control study aimed to assess the hematological alterations and panic severity associated with PD among university students. We evaluated 60 university students (30 PD patients and 30 healthy controls). PD patients scored significantly higher across all panic measures (* p < 0.001). RBC (* p = 0.002) and platelet (* p = 0.003) counts were significantly higher in the PD group and differential WBC profiles also differed between groups. Despite remaining within physiological reference ranges, the neutrophil-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) was significantly elevated in the PD group (* p = 0.002), potentially reflecting stress-induced leukocyte redistribution and neuroendocrine activity associated with HPA-axis dysregulation. However, since NLR does not constitute direct evidence of systemic inflammation, future studies evaluating direct inflammatory biomarkers such as CRP and IL-6 are warranted. These findings remained significant after adjusting for age and sex via Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) and controlling for multiple testing via Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction ( q < 0.05). These preliminary findings contribute to understanding the complex pathophysiology of PD, highlighting potential stress-mediated physiological alterations within South Asian cohorts, offering a foundation for prospective research. Not applicable.

latest.title: Interpersonal distress mediates and self-efficacy moderates the association between family functioning and anxiety in college students in China
latest.abstract: Abstract Family functioning has been consistently associated with anxiety symptoms in college students, yet the underlying associations remain incompletely understood. This cross-sectional study examined whether interpersonal distress mediates the association between family functioning and anxiety, and whether self-efficacy moderates this indirect association. A convenience sample of 1,120 Chinese college students (82.1% female; mean age = 20.30 years) completed self-report measures of family functioning, interpersonal distress, self-efficacy, and anxiety. A latent moderated structural equations (LMS) approach was employed in Mplus 8.3 to estimate the latent interaction between family functioning and self-efficacy while accounting for measurement error, with gender and family economic status included as covariates. Results indicated that poorer family functioning was associated with higher interpersonal distress and anxiety, although the direct association with anxiety was not robust to controlling for common method variance. Interpersonal distress partially accounted for the family functioning–anxiety association (unstandardized conditional indirect association at the mean level of self-efficacy = -0.114, 95% CI [-0.160, -0.068]). Self-efficacy moderated the first-stage association between family functioning and interpersonal distress, with the association weakening as self-efficacy increased (unstandardized simple slopes = − 0.255, − 0.164, and − 0.074 at low, mean, and high self-efficacy, respectively; the slope at high self-efficacy was not significant); however, the direct family functioning–anxiety association was not significantly moderated ( β = 0.042, p = 0.113). These findings highlight interpersonal distress as a key correlate and self-efficacy as a moderatin

latest.title: A scoping review of self-silencing and mental health outcomes in women across three decades
latest.abstract: Silencing the Self-theory proposes that women who inhibit self-expression to preserve close relationships are at greater risk of depression. This scoping review maps the empirical literature on self-silencing and women’s mental health published since 1996. Following PRISMA-ScR, we searched Scopus, Web of Science and ProQuest (1,761 records) and an AI-assisted search engine (Consensus; 108 records). After deduplication, single-reviewer title/abstract screening and quality-control checks, 184 records (1996–2026) were charted: 154 primary studies, 11 reviews and 19 non-empirical records. Two raters appraised the quantitative studies with the MMAT (κ = 0.98). Depressive symptoms were the most frequently examined outcome (111 of 184 records; 60.3%), followed by anxiety (29; 15.8%), disordered eating (27; 14.7%), self-esteem (19; 10.3%), relationship functioning (18; 9.8%), intimate partner violence (18; 9.8%), trauma/PTSD (9; 4.9%) and suicidality (2; 1.1%). Most studies were cross-sectional, and cultural context, racial identity and partner dynamics are increasingly examined as moderators. Screening and charting were done by one reviewer from abstracts, and effect directions and sizes were not charted, so counts show where research effort has gone, not the strength or consistency of associations. The review maps three decades of research across outcomes, populations, designs and theoretical frameworks, and identifies which outcome areas now have enough primary studies to justify full systematic reviews. Many women learn to quiet their own thoughts, feelings and needs to keep the peace in close relationships. This review looks at “self-silencing” and how it connects to women’s mental health. We searched three academic databases and a supplementary citation-search tool, then

latest.title: Group Counseling Using Cognitive Restructuring Techniques to Improve Self-Confidence in Students Experiencing Body Image Dissatisfaction
latest.venue: Urwatul Wutsqo Jurnal Studi Kependidikan dan Keislaman
latest.abstract: This study aims to systematically examine the implementation of cognitive restructuring techniques in group counseling to enhance secondary school students’ self-confidence, investigate the relationship between body image dissatisfaction and self-confidence, and identify factors influencing counseling outcomes. A qualitative Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted using the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and SPIDER framework. Relevant publications from 2017 to 2026 were retrieved through Google Scholar and GARUDA. Ten primary studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising seven intervention studies and three correlational studies. Methodological quality was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute critical appraisal tools, followed by thematic synthesis. The findings indicate that cognitive restructuring generally involves identifying negative thoughts, developing rational alternatives, practicing positive self-statements, and evaluating behavioral changes. Intervention studies consistently reported improvements in students’ self-confidence, although methodological limitations restrict causal conclusions. Student participation and supportive environments facilitated implementation, whereas embarrassment, hesitation, and fear of criticism constituted barriers. Correlational studies demonstrated significant positive relationships between body image and self-confidence without establishing causality. Importantly, none of the reviewed intervention studies specifically examined students experiencing body image dissatisfaction. This review contributes by integrating previously separate research findings and identifying an important evidence gap. Further controlled studies are recommended to evaluate cognitive restructuring interventions specifically among students experie

latest.title: The coping strategies used by university students with physical disabilities in managing psychological challenges in Tanzania
latest.venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Strategies for Education (RISE)
latest.abstract: University Students with Physical Disabilities (USPDs) often experience stress, anxiety, and depression arising from academic, social, and environmental barriers. This study examined the coping strategies USPDs use to manage psychological challenges in selected universities in Morogoro Region, Tanzania. A convergent parallel mixed-methods design was employed. Purposive and snowball sampling recruited 74 students. Quantitative data were collected through questionnaires, including an adapted Brief COPE inventory, and analysed in SPSS using descriptive statistics, paired-samples t-tests, and hierarchical multiple regression. Qualitative data were gathered through semi-structured interviews and analysed thematically. USPDs used emotion-focused coping significantly more than problem-focused coping (M = 19.43, SD = 3.95 vs. M = 13.97, SD = 3.85), t(73) = 7.67, p < .001, d = 0.89. Registration with disability support services was the only significant predictor of problem-focused coping, explaining an additional 11.2% of variance after controlling for demographic characteristics and disability severity. Residence was the only significant predictor of emotion-focused coping, with off-campus students scoring lower; interviews did not explain this association, and its cause cannot be established in a cross-sectional design. Common emotion-focused strategies included breathing exercises, sharing with peers, entertainment, and spiritual practices. Problem-focused strategies, such as task management and seeking academic support, were less frequent because many stressors were perceived as beyond students’ control. Limited institutional support encouraged temporary avoidance responses, such as ignoring, to regulate emotions. The study concludes that strengthening disability support ser

latest.title: From Price to Value: How Procurement Practices Reshape Competition in Medical Device Markets
latest.abstract: Procurement affects both the prices paid for medical devices and the conditions under which suppliers compete. Broader value-based assessment may reward clinical performance and life-cycle savings but may also raise bidding costs and favor incumbents. This conceptual study examines that tension through a focused, non-systematic review of economic theory, peer-reviewed studies, and public procurement documents. It develops four conditional propositions on aggregation, verifiable quality, contractual governance, and evidence-related entry barriers. The framework separates static purchasing efficiency from dynamic market contestability, including supplier entry, switching, and innovation. Evidence from U.S. group purchasing, Canadian tenders, Dutch purchaser interviews, UK experiments, and European procurement frameworks is compared according to the claims each design can support. Available evidence identifies specific expenditure and decision-process effects but does not establish a universal causal impact of value-based procurement on long-run competition. The paper argues for independently verifiable criteria, proportionate evidence requirements, workable contract exit, and continuing opportunities for qualified suppliers. Price-based awards may remain suitable where products are genuinely comparable and downstream differences are small.

latest.title: Social inequalities and nurturing care determinants of early language developmental delay among Ecuadorian children aged 12–42 months
latest.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Early language development is a key indicator of child well-being and is influenced by social, environmental, and biological factors. The study aimed to estimate the prevalence of language developmental delay and identify associated factors among Ecuadorian children aged 12-42 months. STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional analytical study using nationally representative survey data. METHODS: Cross-sectional analytical study using data from the 2018 Ecuadorian National Health and Nutrition Survey (ENSANUT). We included a nationally representative sample of 8446 children aged 12-42 months. Language delay was defined as scores below the 10th percentile on the MacArthur-Bates Communicative Development Inventories using age- and sex-specific national reference curves. Survey-weighted logistic regression models assessed associations according to the UNICEF early childhood development framework. RESULTS: The prevalence of language developmental delay was 14.5%. Delay was associated with male sex (aOR 1.46, 95% CI 1.18-1.81), increasing age (aOR 1.03 per month, 95% CI 1.02-1.05), prematurity (aOR 1.38, 95% CI 1.04-1.84), and greater daily screen exposure (aOR 1.07 per hour/day, 95% CI 1.01-1.15). Protective factors included higher HOME stimulation (aOR 0.61, 95% CI 0.48-0.79), playing with ≥3 toy types (aOR 0.75, 95% CI 0.57-0.98), and more children's books (aOR 0.90 per book, 95% CI 0.84-0.96). Structural socioeconomic factors were not significant. CONCLUSIONS: Approximately one in seven Ecuadorian children aged 12-42 months experienced language developmental delay. Lower home stimulation, fewer children's books, limited play opportunities, greater screen exposure, prematurity, male sex, and older age were independently associated with delay.

latest.title: Green Human Resource Management and Environmentally Friendly Behavior of Employees in Iraq's Ministry of Environment
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study examines how Green Human Resource Management (GHRM), expressed through green recruitment, green training, green performance appraisal, and green rewards, relates to and influences the environmentally friendly behavior of employees at the Ministry of Environment in Baghdad, Iraq. Methodology: A descriptive analytical design was used. A questionnaire built on a five point Likert scale was distributed electronically to a convenience sample of 110 employees, and 98 questionnaires were returned. Validity was checked with Pearson item correlations, reliability with Cronbach's alpha, and the hypotheses were tested with Pearson correlation and simple linear regression in SPSS version 27. Results: All four GHRM dimensions were rated highly, with green performance appraisal ranked first. GHRM correlated strongly and positively with environmentally friendly behavior (r=0.673) and had a significant effect on it (B=0.752, F=77.079, R²=0.453). Green training and green rewards were the strongest individual dimensions. Conclusions: Green HR practices, particularly training and rewards, give the ministry a practical way to steer employees toward greener behavior at work. Limitations: The study relied on a single public organization, a small convenience sample, cross sectional self reported data, and bivariate analysis. Contributions: The study adds evidence from an Iraqi public sector setting, where GHRM research is still scarce, and offers managers concrete steps such as environmentally oriented job descriptions and incentives for employees who propose ways to reduce waste.

latest.title: Foreign direct investment inflows, divestment and internationalisation: panel evidence from African economies, 2010–2023
latest.abstract: Abstract This study examines how foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows and foreign direct divestment (FDD) are associated with the internationalisation of African economies. Using an unbalanced panel of 47 African countries (618 country-year observations, 2010–2023), internationalisation is measured with the KOF trade and financial globalisation indices, while FDI inflows and FDD (the absolute value of negative net FDI inflows) are scaled by GDP and log-transformed. Two-way fixed-effects and two-step System GMM estimators are complemented by partial-sum asymmetry tests, Hansen panel-threshold models with institutional quality as the threshold variable, and income-group heterogeneity analysis based on the World Bank classification. FDI inflows are robustly and positively associated with trade globalisation in the fixed-effects models (β = 1.148, p = .006) and with financial globalisation in the dynamic and lagged specifications. Divestment is negatively associated with trade globalisation when estimated on its own and in the dynamic model, but the association is imprecise once FDI inflows are controlled for, is concentrated in lower-middle-income economies, and is driven largely by Angola and the Republic of Congo, which together account for 88% of divestment in the sample. Distributed-lag estimates show that the divestment association with trade globalisation materialises with a two-year lag (cumulative effect − 3.323, p = .026) and intensifies with natural-resource dependence. There is no statistically significant evidence that internationalisation responds asymmetrically to increases and decreases in investment. Threshold estimates indicate that the FDI–trade association is confined to economies with weaker institutional quality, contrary to the expectation that str

latest.title: How childhood motor skills, physical literacy, and social support shape young adult physical activity: a structural equation modelling approach
latest.abstract: Physical activity is influenced by a range of physical, psychological, and social factors. While motor competence has traditionally been considered a prime determinant of physical activity, the concept of physical literacy offers a broader framework that also incorporates motivational, cognitive, and affective factors. At present, limited research has examined how childhood experiences, motor competence, physical literacy, and social support jointly contribute to physical activity in young adulthood. A cross-sectional online survey was completed in 2341 young adults aged 16–30 years. Participants reported on their current physical activity, motor competence, physical literacy, and social support, as well as retrospective childhood experiences (grade 3/4) of physical activity, motor competence, and social support. Structural equation modelling (SEM) was used to examine the relationships among all variables. Childhood motor competence was strongly associated with motor competence in young adulthood. Both childhood and young adult motor competence were positively associated with physical literacy in young adulthood, while physical literacy, in turn, showed a strong positive association with young adult physical activity. Childhood social support was positively associated with childhood physical activity and young adult social support. The overall pattern of findings suggests that physical literacy, and its constituent factors, may provide a useful framework for understanding how childhood experiences link to physical activity in young adulthood. While motor competence remains important, physical literacy was found to be more strongly associated with physical activity in young adulthood and may help explain how early-life experiences connect to later physical activity behav

latest.title: How Does R&D Investment Influence Firm Innovation Quality? The Mediating Roles of Knowledge Absorption and Transformation Capabilities
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
latest.abstract: This study examines the impact of research and development (R&D) investment on firm innovation quality and further investigates the mediating roles of knowledge absorption capability and knowledge transformation capability. Although R&D investment is widely recognized as a key driver of technological progress and corporate innovation, the relationship between innovation input and innovation quality is not necessarily direct. The extent to which firms can identify, acquire, absorb, integrate, and transform external and internal knowledge may determine how effectively R&D resources are converted into high-quality innovation outcomes. Therefore, this study aims to clarify the underlying mechanisms through which R&D investment contributes to improvements in firm innovation quality and to identify whether these effects differ across firms with different ownership structures and industry characteristics. This study contributes to the existing literature by opening the black box between R&D input and innovation quality and highlighting the importance of knowledge-related capabilities as mechanisms connecting innovation investment with innovation outcomes also provides empirical evidence for understanding the conditions under which investment generates greater innovation value. Firms should not focus exclusively on increasing R&D expenditure but should also strengthen their knowledge absorption, integration, and transformation capabilities. The findings provide empirical support for promoting a transition from innovation quantity innovation quality improvement.

latest.title: Negative consequences of sleep disturbance in individuals with limb loss
latest.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To identify the association between sleep disturbance with physical function and psychological outcomes in individuals with limb loss. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 218 community ambulating individuals with at least one amputation, recruited from Military treatment facilities, community events, and prosthetic clinics. Participants' demographics were obtained from self-reported questionnaires. The Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS)-29 scores were used to assess sleep disturbance, physical function, anxiety, depression, fatigue, pain interference, and social participation. Sleep disturbance data were used to categorize the participants into three mutually exclusive groups: no sleep disturbance, mild sleep disturbance, and moderate to severe sleep disturbance. One-way analyses of variance (ANOVA) were used to determine if differences existed in PROMIS scores between the three sleep disturbance categories. RESULTS: Results showed that as compared to individuals with no sleep disturbance, those with moderate to severe sleep disturbance had worse physical function; higher levels of anxiety, depression, fatigue, and pain interference, and less social participation. In addition, a difference was noted between the mild and the moderate to severe groups indicating worse depression, fatigue, social participation, and pain interference. When compared to the no sleep disturbance group, the mild disturbance group demonstrated worse physical function and fatigue (all P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Results reflect that higher levels of sleep disturbance are associated with worse functional and psychological outcome measures in individuals with limb loss. Findings from this study also indicate that a higher threshold of sleep disturbanc

latest.title: Enlightened Egoism and Its Discontents: Mapping the Business Case for Doing Good
latest.abstract: Abstract Various voices in business ethics and wider discussions of ethical capitalism endorse instrumental or strategic reasons for being ethical. Yet this orientation has at times eluded sustained philosophical engagement by the business ethics discipline. This article addresses this gap by mapping and critiquing what I term "enlightened egoism"—approaches that draw upon instrumental reasoning to derive normative guidance without recourse to duties, rights, values, or questions of the good. Careful reconstruction reveals that enlightened egoist arguments combine descriptive claims about how business operates with normative conclusions about how businesses ought to behave. Variations in these descriptive claims yield three distinct subtypes—evidential egoism, ends-enclosed egoism, and evolutionary egoism—each prominent in contemporary business ethics discourse. Examples are drawn from stakeholder theory, ESG investing (including hedge fund Engine No. 1's engagement with ExxonMobil), and diversity hiring initiatives. Through immanent critique, I demonstrate that enlightened egoism exhibits fundamental instabilities, specifically around indeterminacy in criteria for action, failure to account for heterogeneity, and conceptual slippage into determinist accounts of behavior. These limitations suggest the need for more rigorous integration of instrumental reasoning within—rather than as replacement for—normative ethical frameworks.

latest.title: Promosi Melalui Implementasi Tiktok Ads untuk Meningkatkan Engagement Dasilva Batik Malang
latest.abstract: Dasilva Batik Malang is an MSME producing modern batik clothing whose TikTok engagement has declined due to inconsistent digital promotion and unused TikTok Ads potential. This research identifies TikTok Ads implementation as a digital promotion strategy, analyzes engagement differences among entertainment, storytelling, and promotional content, and determines the most effective content type, and identifies the obstacles encountered. The research applies the Kemmis and MeTaggart action research model through planning, action, observation, and reflection. The unit of analysis comprises 20 people: the business owner, marketing experts, computer experts, and prospective consumers selected purposively. The EPIC Model questionnaire was tested for validity using Pearson Product Moment correlation and reliability using Cronbach's Alpha via IBM SPSS Statistics 26. The EPIC Rate assessment showed all three contents were effective, with promotional content scoring highest (4.16). However, the actual engagement rate after publication via TikTok Ads showed entertainment content performed best (1.99%), followed by promotional (1.68%) and storytelling content (1.63%). Dasilva Batik Malang is advised to produce-more entertainment content without abandoning promotional and storytelling content, while future research should apply A/B Testing, add content variations, and increase the promotion budget for more representative results.

latest.title: Sistem Pendukung Keputusan Pemilihan Saham Terbaik Indonesia Dengan Menggunakan Metode Weighted Product dan ELECTRE
latest.venue: Jurnal Riset Informatika dan Teknologi Informasi
latest.abstract: This study develops a Decision Support System (DSS) for Selecting the Best Stocks using the ELECTRE and Weighted Product (WP) methods based on six financial criteria, namely Net Profit Margin (NPM), Return on Equity (ROE), Earnings per Share (EPS), Price-to-Earnings Ratio (PER), Debt-to-Equity Ratio (DER), and Price-to-Book Value (PBV), and develops a Python CLI-based application. The research subjects are companies listed on the main board of the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) that have published their financial reports for the last quarter of 2025 and have non-negative PER, EPS, and PBV values, resulting in a sample of 109 stocks. The accuracy and relevance of the method were tested by comparing the ranking results against actual stock returns for the first quarter of 2026 using Spearman’s correlation. The results show that WP method obtained a coefficient of 0.27777, while ELECTRE obtained 0.10994. Both methods showed a weak to very weak correlation with actual returns, but WP consistently produced a higher correlation. Thus, WP method is more suitable for a stock selection decision support system based on the research dataset and criteria than ELECTRE method.

latest.title: AI-Assisted Negotiation Training: A Quasi-Experimental Examination of Buyers’ and Sellers’ Perceived Negotiation Performance in a Used-Car Sales Simulation
latest.abstract: Background: Evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) as a preparatory learning aid for novice human negotiators remains limited in consumer negotiation simulations. Existing work emphasizes automated agents rather than students preparing to negotiate. Against this backdrop, the present study examined changes in students’ perceived negotiation performance, differences in those changes between buyer and seller roles, and the purposes for which students used AI during a simulated used-car sale. The outcome was perceived performance, not economic results. Methodology: A single-group, repeated-measures quasi-experiment involved 74 undergraduate business students enrolled in a negotiation course at a university in Bangkok, Thailand. Thirty-seven students served as buyers and 37 as sellers. Participants completed two negotiations outside regular class hours within a 24–48-hour period, retaining their assigned roles and using the same scenario. The first round was conducted without AI assistance. Before the second round, students spent approximately five minutes preparing with generative AI tools of their choice for information analysis, strategy planning, role-play, or feedback. Each negotiation lasted approximately five to seven minutes. Perceived negotiation performance was assessed using five-item self-report scales in each condition. Paired-samples t-tests and a mixed-design analysis of variance (ANOVA) examined differences between conditions and across roles. Reported purposes of AI use were summarized descriptively. Results: Students reported higher perceived negotiation performance after AI-assisted preparation (M = 4.45, SD = 0.42) than after the preceding non-AI round (M = 3.78, SD = 0.58). The mean difference was 0.67 points, t(73) = −9.23, p < .001, with a large sta

latest.title: Constraint-Native Globalization: Extending the Value-Yield Optimization (VYO) Framework to the Internationalization of Resource-Constrained SMEs
latest.abstract: International business scholarship has long documented that the benefits of globalization accrue unevenly: large multinational enterprises (MNEs) capture most cross-border value, while small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), which constitute the overwhelming majority of firms worldwide, remain largely excluded from global value chains. This exclusion is primarily a matter of constraint rather than ambition or product quality. The prevailing internationalization models-stage theories, the Uppsala model, and born-global paradigms-assume access to market intelligence, foreign-market capital, multilingual talent, and regulatory-compliance capacity that resource-constrained SMEs often cannot supply. The Value-Yield Optimization (VYO) Framework (Yevsiukova, 2026) addressed this problem domestically by ranking AI-driven optimization opportunities according to the return achievable within a firm's real capital, labor, and technical limits. This paper introduces the Global Value-Yield Optimization (G-VYO) Framework, which extends VYO to the cross-border domain. G-VYO differs from VYO in three respects: it adds three cross-border factors (market distance, currency and macroeconomic volatility, and regulatory friction) to the constraint-weighting function; it adds a sixth stage, a systemic resilience audit of the international portfolio; and it introduces a three-axis readiness-headroom-distance decision cube for entry-market planning. The framework specifies five foundational principles, a six-stage operating sequence, and a Global Constraint-Weighted Return on Investment (GCW-ROI) function with explicit measurement rules and a worked numerical example. Four country-entry archetypes are illustrated with five published empirical studies of SME internationalization from Eastern

latest.title: Beyond Apology: Corporate Moral Repair and the Limits of Organisational Entitlement
latest.abstract: An organisation can remedy wrongdoing without acquiring a right to demand forgiveness, renewed loyalty, or public endorsement from those harmed. This conceptual article asks which corporate claims remain justified after remedy and develops a non-conversion principle: fulfilment of an antecedent remedial duty does not, by itself, create an entitlement to the response an organisation prefers. Using theory adaptation, the analysis compares stakeholder, moral-repair, restorative, and dialogical scholarship with accounts of institutional repentance and African relational ethics. Explicit normative premises and five hypothetical claim episodes distinguish discharged duties, reasons for favourable reassessment, and independently justified reciprocal claims. Four propositions identify limits on conditional redress, requirements for maintaining outstanding commitments when endorsement is withheld, and the scope of legitimate completion claims. Repaired separation, qualified return, and voluntary reconciliation emerge as nonhierarchical possibilities. The contribution is a test of the source and scope of corporate demands and representations, extending existing protections of stakeholder agency. Boards should assess remedial provision, procedural authority, and authorised relational responses separately. For international business, this distinction constrains how local settlements and representative mandates support corporate-group reporting. A proposed coding protocol supports future empirical examination; the article does not establish prevalence or causal effectiveness.

latest.title: Pengaruh Employee Engagement dan Kepuasan Kerja terhadap Loyalitas Karyawan pada PT Pos Indonesia (Persero) Cabang Medan
latest.abstract: The logistics industry in Indonesia has undergone significant changes in line with the rise in e-commerce activity and the demand for fast and efficient delivery services, requiring logistics service providers to improve service quality through optimal human resource management. This quantitative study with a causal-associative approach aims to analyze the influence of employee engagement and job satisfaction on employee loyalty at PT Pos Indonesia (Persero) Medan Branch. The population consisted of 52 operational staff and field personnel, with total sampling employed so all members were included as research samples. Data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression, partial and simultaneous tests, and coefficient of determination. The results show that employee engagement and job satisfaction have both partial and simultaneous effects on employee loyalty. The R value of 0.801 indicates a strong relationship between the variables, and the Adjusted R-Square value of 0.627 reveals that employee engagement and job satisfaction contribute 62.7% to employee loyalty, while the remaining 37.3% is influenced by other variables not examined in this study

latest.title: From cutting to ear piercing: evolution of self-injurious behavior in an adolescent with treatment-resistant bipolar disorder: a case report
latest.abstract: Background Bipolar disorder is frequently associated with non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI), the manifestations of which vary across the illness course. Ear piercing may represent a covert alternative form of self-injury with an NSSI-like function that is commonly overlooked in clinical practice; consequently, reports documenting this phenomenon remain scarce. Case summary This report describes an 18-year-old female with treatment-resistant bipolar disorder whose self-injurious behavior evolved from wrist cutting to periungual skin picking and, ultimately, to 11 self-inflicted ear piercings within 48 hours, complicated by localized infection. The patient reported transient relief of agitation following these procedures, with no suicidal intent. Conclusion Repeated self-inflicted ear piercing within a short period, impaired behavioral control, disregard for infection risk, and use as an emotion-regulation strategy may be consistent with an NSSI-like pattern. Ear piercing may thus represent a covert NSSI-like substitute in some adolescents with bipolar disorder; however, such behavior should not be automatically classified as NSSI. Clinicians should maintain vigilance for this practice and carefully differentiate NSSI-like behavior from routine body adornment.

latest.title: Executives’ green cognition and biodiversity risk avoidance in international operations
latest.abstract: Purpose Biodiversity loss has become a material yet largely nonpriced risk in global investment decisions. However, little is known about how multinational enterprises (MNEs) internalize biodiversity risk in overseas subsidiary operations and whether managerial environmental orientation shapes such decisions. This study aims to examine whether executives’ green cognition influences MNEs’ exposure to biodiversity risk. Design/methodology/approach Using a sample of China A-share listed companies from 2009 to 2023, the authors investigate the relationship between executives’ green cognition and the biodiversity risk exposure of overseas subsidiaries. Findings Empirical results show that executives’ green cognition prompts firms to reduce the biodiversity risk exposure of their overseas subsidiaries. Boundary condition analyses indicate that the relationship between executives’ green cognition and biodiversity risk avoidance is significant among firms that have made climate commitments, disclosed climate risk information or attracted investor attention to climate risks, and this conclusion holds after a series of robustness tests. Extended analyses further reveal that the relationship remains significant under both short- and long-term climate commitments, while different types of investor climate attention exhibit distinct patterns, with the relationship being more evident for attention to pollution control and ecological protection. Originality/value This study connects executives’ green cognition with biodiversity risk management in MNE operations, demonstrating how managerial environmental orientation influences cross-border risk decisions. By developing an objective, species-occurrence-based measure of biodiversity risk and mapping it to firms’ overseas subsidiary loca

latest.title: Insider action research: staying close, remaining accountable
latest.abstract: BACKGROUND: Insider nurse researchers bring contextual knowledge, professional credibility, relationships and commitment to the issue under inquiry. These can strengthen action research, but may also shape assumptions, participation, interpretation and decisions about closure. AIM: To examine the practical and methodological challenges of undertaking a nurse-led appreciative inquiry study as a professional insider, and to propose 'responsible closeness' as a conceptual framework for navigating the complexities of insider research. DISCUSSION: This account was informed by reflective and documentary materials generated during the research process. Four tensions made responsible closeness visible: insider assumptions and collaborative challenge; professional identity and facilitative influence; advocacy and openness to inquiry; and responsible closure of the collaborative research phase. Across these tensions, responsible closeness involved using insider knowledge while keeping assumptions, interpretations and researcher influence open to reflexive and collaborative scrutiny. Reflexivity became methodologically significant when it changed subsequent questioning, facilitation, interpretation, action or plans for closure. CONCLUSION: Responsible closeness offers a conceptual framework for understanding how an insider position can be navigated in action research. It helps insider researchers draw on their professional knowledge, familiarity and relationships while remaining accountable for how these shape the inquiry, subsequent actions and the knowledge generated. IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Insider researchers should create explicit opportunities for participants to challenge emerging interpretations and approach closure as a collaborative phase that acknowledges what has be

latest.title: Moderating Factors of Digital Intimacy Interference and Marital Stability of Couple in Rivers State
latest.venue: WORLD JOURNAL OF INNOVATION AND MODERN TECHNOLOGY
latest.abstract: This study ascertained moderating factors on digital intimacy interference and marital stability of couple in Rivers State. The objectives of the study were among others: to identify the cultural/societal norms in Rivers State that moderate the relationship between digital intimacy interference and marital stability of couple. Theoretical framework of the study was drawn from the social penetration and social network interference theories. The research design adopted for this study was descriptive survey design. According to National Population Census, 2006 population census of Rivers State, the population of married male and female by age 18 and above was 1,404,855 (one million, four hundred and four thousand, eight hundred and fifty-five). According to a sample size table from Krejcie and Morgan’s sample table, a study population of 100,000, a sample of 384 is adequate. The sampling technique used by this study was multi-stage sampling technique. The research questions were analysed, using the weighted mean score and the criterion weighted mean score (CWMS) was established at 2.50. Findings revealed that, societal expectations of sharing personal information on digital platforms, cultural norms on perception of privacy, societal pressure to maintain traditional family values and relationship boundaries were the cultural and societal norms in Rivers State that moderated the relationship between digital intimacy interference and marital stability of couple. The study concluded that, individuals’ online behaviour and personal information sharing are greatly influenced by societal expectations, cultural norms and societal pressure to maintain traditional values. The study recommended that, couple should encourage a more open discourse about online behaviour and privacy, a

latest.title: Pengaruh Pengaruh SERVQUAL (Layanan Attendant Stateroom) dan Tarif Terhadap Kepuasan Tamu di Kapal Pesiar Icon of the Seas
latest.venue: Jurnal Akuntansi Ekonomi dan Manajemen Bisnis
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of service quality, particularly stateroom attendant services, and pricing on customer satisfaction aboard the Icon of the Seas cruise ship. A quantitative research approach with a survey method was employed. The study involved 68 respondents selected using purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, and multiple linear regression analysis with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics. The findings indicate that service quality has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction, with a regression coefficient of 0.364 and a significance value of 0.002. Pricing also has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction, with a regression coefficient of 0.472 and a significance value of 0.000. Simultaneously, service quality and pricing significantly influence customer satisfaction, as indicated by an F-value of 91.451 and a significance level of 0.000. The coefficient of determination (Adjusted R²) of 0.730 indicates that 73% of customer satisfaction is explained by service quality and pricing, while the remaining 27% is influenced by other factors. These findings suggest that improving stateroom attendant service quality and implementing appropriate pricing strategies are essential to enhancing customer satisfaction aboard the Icon of the Seas cruise ship.

hot.title: Trust in scientists and their role in society across 68 countries
hot.abstract: Science is crucial for evidence-based decision-making. Public trust in scientists can help decision makers act on the basis of the best available evidence, especially during crises. However, in recent years the epistemic authority of science has been challenged, causing concerns about low public trust in scientists. We interrogated these concerns with a preregistered 68-country survey of 71,922 respondents and found that in most countries, most people trust scientists and agree that scientists should engage more in society and policymaking. We found variations between and within countries, which we explain with individual- and country-level variables, including political orientation. While there is no widespread lack of trust in scientists, we cannot discount the concern that lack of trust in scientists by even a small minority may affect considerations of scientific evidence in policymaking. These findings have implications for scientists and policymakers seeking to maintain and increase trust in scientists.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: The evolving field of digital mental health: current evidence and implementation issues for smartphone apps, generative artificial intelligence, and virtual reality
hot.abstract: The expanding domain of digital mental health is transitioning beyond traditional telehealth to incorporate smartphone apps, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence, including large language models. While industry setbacks and methodological critiques have highlighted gaps in evidence and challenges in scaling these technologies, emerging solutions rooted in co-design, rigorous evaluation, and implementation science offer promising pathways forward. This paper underscores the dual necessity of advancing the scientific foundations of digital mental health and increasing its real-world applicability through five themes. First, we discuss recent technological advances in digital phenotyping, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence. Progress in this latter area, specifically designed to create new outputs such as conversations and images, holds unique potential for the mental health field. Given the spread of smartphone apps, we then evaluate the evidence supporting their utility across various mental health contexts, including well-being, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. This broad view of the field highlights the need for a new generation of more rigorous, placebo-controlled, and real-world studies. We subsequently explore engagement challenges that hamper all digital mental health tools, and propose solutions, including human support, digital navigators, just-in-time adaptive interventions, and personalized approaches. We then analyze implementation issues, emphasizing clinician engagement, service integration, and scalable delivery models. We finally consider the need to ensure that innovations work for all people and thus can bridge digital health disparities, reviewing the evidence on ta

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Shaping Organizational Work Practices and Culture
hot.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming organizational landscapes, significantly influencing work practices and triggering cultural shifts. This study explores the role of AI in reshaping organizational work practices and examines the resulting cultural transformation. Through a systematic literature review, this study synthesizes existing research to provide a comprehensive understanding of AI’s impact on organizational landscapes. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, books, and conference papers to identify key themes related to AI-driven changes in work practices, including automation, decision making, and employee roles. It also explores how these changes influence organizational culture, particularly shifts toward innovation, agility, and continuous learning, alongside challenges like resistance to change and ethical concerns. While AI adoption promises benefits such as enhanced efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also presents significant challenges related to cultural alignment, employee resistance, ethical concerns, and leadership communication. Effective leadership, transparent communication, and investments in skills development emerge as pivotal strategies for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring successful AI implementation. The findings offer insights into the complex interplay between AI adoption and cultural transformation, highlighting gaps in the current research and suggesting directions for future studies. This study serves as a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to understand the broader implications of AI on organizational structures and culture.

hot.title: Job demands-resources and conservation of resources theories: How do they help to explain employee well-being and future job design?
hot.abstract: This paper examines the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory to understand and predict employee well-being and performance. COR theory suggests that individuals aim to acquire, protect, and maximize resources to reduce psychological distress and prevent burnout. JD-R theory posits that balancing job demands and resources affects employee well-being, behaviors, and performance. By exploring these theories together, the paper offers insights into supporting the workforce amid challenges like remote work and technological advancements. It highlights shared features and differences between the theories, unresolved issues, and research opportunities, such as operationalizing and testing COR theory and differentiating job demands and resources in JD-R theory. The paper concludes with predictions about future job design, emphasizing the need to balance job demands and resources to support employee well-being and performance, contributing to the literature by challenging and refining these theories.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings.
