hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: AI and employee wellbeing in the workplace: An empirical study
hot.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in workplace settings significantly affects employees, particularly their wellbeing. Despite its growing relevance, the impact of AI on employee wellbeing remains underexplored. To address this gap, we conducted a survey and employed structural equation modeling to analyze data from Finnish and international companies headquartered in Finland (n = 207). We found that AI adoption does not directly impact employee wellbeing but indirectly influences it through work-related factors of task optimization and safety. This highlights the importance of strategically implementing AI to enhance aspects of work that are important to employees, thereby maximizing the wellbeing benefits of AI adoption. Practically, this study underscores the need for AI adoption to result in tangible improvements in organizational tasks and processes, data security, and occupational health. When these aspects are adequately addressed, AI adoption can enhance employee wellbeing and contribute to improved human-AI integration in the workplace.

hot.title: Greenwashing prevention in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosures: A bibliometric analysis
hot.venue: Research in International Business and Finance
hot.abstract: The accuracy and reliability of environmental, social, and governance (hereafter ESG) reporting are threatened by the presence of greenwashing which affects the quality of disclosure, complicates the decision-making process, adversely influences financial markets, and affects stakeholders’ trust in disclosed information. This study examines the academic literature on ESG disclosure and greenwashing prevention through a bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review. Our findings show that greenwashing is a complex phenomenon characterised by various forms, shapes, and levels, making it challenging to detect, measure, and develop prevention tools. The results show a growing trend in the academic literature on greenwashing with a strong focus on the establishment of greenwashing detection measures and the need for the creation of greenwashing prevention tools to ensure the reliability, comparability, and quality of corporate sustainability reporting. Understanding the challenges of greenwashing in ESG disclosures and the efforts toward greenwashing prevention carries significant implications for regulators and standard-setters, supervisory bodies, professional organizations, companies, researchers, and other stakeholders, especially in light of recent regulatory developments around the globe and the new forms and levels of greenwashing evolving in scientific research. • Greenwashing prevention in ESG disclosures analysed through a bibliometric analysis. • Performance, network, and systematic literature review analysis methods applied. • Greenwashing measurement is difficult as it has lots of levels, forms, and shades. • Greenwashing measurement methods at various greenwashing levels are systemized. • The creation of a credible greenwashing prevention tool in ESG d

hot.title: Technological folie à deux: feedback loops between AI chatbots and mental health
The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Abstract Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: Insights from the Job Demands–Resources Model: AI's dual impact on employees’ work and life well-being
hot.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly integrated into organizational workflows, sparking two debates: proponents argue that it increases productivity and decreases workloads, whereas opponents warn that it induces technostress (e.g., job replacement) and decreases employees' well-being. However, AI adoption by employees remains understudied, requiring both theoretical and empirical investigation to assess its positive and negative effects. This study employs the job demands–resources (JD–R) model as a guiding framework to examine the impact of AI demands (i.e., technostress) and resources (i.e., efficacy and generative AI) on employees' work and life domains (i.e., productivity, job satisfaction, and work–family conflict), with engagement and exhaustion as mediating factors. Data gathering through a three-wave survey involved 600 gender-balanced participants working with AI across diverse industries. Bayesian SEM results indicate that both AI efficacy and generative AI positively impact productivity, with AI efficacy also enhancing engagement and job satisfaction. In contrast, AI technostress increases exhaustion, exacerbates work–family conflict, and lowers job satisfaction, even though it may still contribute to productivity. These findings highlight the dual impact of AI on employees: AI technostress impairs well-being, while AI efficacy enhances it. Notably, generative AI mitigates the negative effects of technostress, a benefit not observed for AI efficacy as measured in this study. Overall, this study provides an empirical basis for understanding the resources and demands associated with AI adoption and its impact on employees' psychological processes, influencing both their work and life domains and leading to diverse outcomes. • This study explores how AI at

hot.title: AI-driven personalization: Unraveling consumer perceptions in social media engagement
Collaborative AI in the workplace: Enhancing organizational performance through resource-based and task-technology fit perspectives
hot.abstract: This research examines how artificial intelligence, human capabilities, and task types influence organizational outcomes. By leveraging the frameworks of the Resource-Based View and Task Technology Fit theories, we executed two distinct studies to assess the effectiveness of a generative AI tool in aiding task performance across a spectrum of task complexities and creative demands. The initial study tested the utility of generative AI across diverse tasks and the significance of AI-related skills enhancement. The subsequent study explored interactions between humans and AI, analyzing emotional tone, sentence structure, and word choice. Our results indicate that incorporating AI can significantly improve organizational task performance in areas such as automation, support, creative endeavors, and innovation processes. We also observed that generative AI generally presents more positive sentiment, utilizes simpler language, and has a narrower vocabulary than human counterparts. These insights contribute to a broader understanding of AI's strengths and weaknesses in organizational settings and guide the strategic implementation of AI systems. • Firms can utilize AI to gain competitive advantages. • Firms can deploy AI to automate routine tasks and enhance decision support tasks. • Firms should focus on AI and human collaboration to boost creative and innovative tasks. • Firms benefit when employees upskill to improve performance with AI. • Generative AI tool in our study had a more positive sentiment and used simpler language than humans.
hot.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Supply Chain Resilience: A Critical Review of Risk Mitigation, Robust Optimisation, and Technological Solutions and Future Research Directions
hot.venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management
hot.abstract: Abstract This study systematically evaluates the literature of supply chain resilience by integrating bibliometric and network analysis techniques. This analysis is conducted following the dynamic capability, as a theoretical lens, to understand and analyse supply chain resilience. We extracted and curated 294 peer‐reviewed articles from leading academic databases, Web of Science and Scopus, covering the period from January 2000 to 2024. We applied two complementary network analysis methods, a keyword co‐occurrence network (KCON) to analyse the frequency and interrelationships among key terms, and a research focus parallelship network (RFPN) to map the connectivity among research streams. These analytical approaches revealed three distinct research clusters, optimisation for supply chain resilience, technology adoption for supply chain resilience, and resilience strategies against disruptions and risk management. By linking emerging trends in digital transformation with traditional risk management practices, this study offers a new perspective for both academic inquiry and managerial practice. Practically, integrating digital technologies, especially digital twin and machine learning, into risk management processes offers a strategic roadmap for real-time monitoring and decision-making in supply chain resilience. Furthermore, this study identifies significant research gaps, including an exploration of micro‐level dynamics within organisations, and the development of advanced simulation techniques and robust approaches to manage uncertainties.

hot.title: Organizational culture, digital transformation, and product innovation
hot.abstract: This research fills a knowledge gap by introducing a new conceptualization of digital transformation through a multidimensional digital transforming capability. It further examines the influence of four cultural types on this capability and its subsequent impact on product innovation . Empirical findings reveal that adhocracy, followed in descending order of influence by clan, market, and hierarchy cultures, is positively related to digital transforming capability, which in turn is positively related to product innovation in terms of new product newness, meaningfulness, and performance. Additionally, new product newness and meaningfulness each positively mediate the effect of digital transforming capability on new product performance.

hot.title: Lower Artificial Intelligence Literacy Predicts Greater AI Receptivity
hot.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms society, understanding factors that influence AI receptivity is increasingly important. The current research investigates which types of consumers have greater AI receptivity. Contrary to expectations revealed in four surveys, cross-country data and six additional studies find that people with lower AI literacy are typically more receptive to AI. This lower literacy–greater receptivity link is not explained by differences in perceptions of AI's capability, ethicality, or feared impact on humanity. Instead, this link occurs because people with lower AI literacy are more likely to perceive AI as magical and experience feelings of awe in the face of AI's execution of tasks that seem to require uniquely human attributes. In line with this theorizing, the lower literacy–higher receptivity link is mediated by perceptions of AI as magical and is moderated among tasks not assumed to require distinctly human attributes. These findings suggest that companies may benefit from shifting their marketing efforts and product development toward consumers with lower AI literacy. In addition, efforts to demystify AI may inadvertently reduce its appeal.

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs : An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other. Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: Can Generative AI Chatbots Emulate Human Connection? A Relationship Science Perspective
hot.abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence capable of sustaining complex conversations has created a burgeoning market for companion chatbots promising social and emotional connection. The appeal of these products raises questions about whether chatbots can fulfill the functions of close relationships. Proponents argue that relationships with chatbots can be as meaningful as relationships between humans, whereas critics argue they are a dangerous distraction from genuine connections. This analysis applies theoretical tools from more than 50 years of research on close relationships to evaluate the extent to which human-chatbot interactions meet the definition of and fulfill the functions of close relationships. Interactions between humans and chatbots do possess some characteristic features of close relationships: Humans and chatbots can influence each other and engage in frequent and diverse conversations over time. Chatbots can be responsive in ways humans perceive as supportive, generating feelings of connection and opportunities for growth. Yet because chatbots make only superficial requests of their users, relationships with them cannot provide the benefits of negotiating with and sacrificing for a partner and may reinforce undesirable behaviors. Research that attends to the characteristics of users, chatbots, and their interactions will be crucial for identifying for whom these relationships will be beneficial or harmful.

hot.title: What you see is not what you get: ESG scores and greenwashing risk
hot.abstract: This paper shows that ESG scores capture a company’s greenwashing behavior. Greenwashing accusations are most prevalent among large companies with high ESG scores. We empirically employ a novel theoretical model that distinguishes between the communication of a company’s environmental efforts (apparent environmental performance) and its actual environmental impact (real environmental performance). The correlation of the apparent (real) environmental performance with ESG scores is significantly positive (negative). Therefore, ESG scores are unsuitable for measuring real environmental impact. Thus, investors focusing on high ESG-rated companies may unknowingly increase their greenwashing risk exposure, and academics may use misleading information to assess greenwashing risk. • ESG scores are positively correlated with greenwashing cases. • ESG scores mainly measure the apparent rather than the real environmental performance. • Higher analyst coverage limits the exaggeration of apparent environmental performance.

hot.title: Third-party evaluators perceive AI as more compassionate than expert humans
hot.abstract: Empathy connects us but strains under demanding settings. This study explored how third parties evaluated AI-generated empathetic responses versus human responses in terms of compassion, responsiveness, and overall preference across four preregistered experiments. Participants (N = 556) read empathy prompts describing valenced personal experiences and compared the AI responses to select non-expert or expert humans. Results revealed that AI responses were preferred and rated as more compassionate compared to select human responders (Study 1). This pattern of results remained when author identity was made transparent (Study 2), when AI was compared to expert crisis responders (Study 3), and when author identity was disclosed to all participants (Study 4). Third parties perceived AI as being more responsive-conveying understanding, validation, and care-which partially explained AI's higher compassion ratings in Study 4. These findings suggest that AI has robust utility in contexts requiring empathetic interaction, with the potential to address the increasing need for empathy in supportive communication contexts.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.

hot.title: Sustainability or Greenwashing: Evidence from the Asset Market for Industrial Pollution
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT We study the asset market for pollutive plants. Firms divest pollutive plants in response to environmental pressures. Buyers are firms facing weaker environmental pressures that have supply chain relationships or joint ventures with the sellers. While pollution levels do not decline following divestitures, sellers highlight their sustainable policies in subsequent conference calls, earn higher returns as they sell more pollutive plants, and benefit from higher Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) ratings and lower compliance costs. Overall, the asset market allows firms to redraw their boundaries in a manner perceived as environmentally friendly without real consequences for pollution but with substantial gains from trade.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: The past, present, and future of sustainability marketing: How did we get here and where might we go?
hot.abstract: The ever-increasing concerns about global sustainability have sparked intense debates and actions across various sectors, with marketing playing a pivotal role in influencing both the problem and potential solutions. This article maps the historical trajectory of sustainability marketing, analyzes current trends, and explores future directions to enhance sustainability within marketing practice. We show that sustainability marketing has historically centered on resource conservation and green marketing , but in recent years its scope has expanded to encompass a broader range of topics. These include the circular economy , anti-consumption, regulatory frameworks, innovation, carbon emissions , as well as the social and ethical considerations inherent in sustainability marketing. We propose three main areas within which sustainability marketing might expand in the future: system-driven changes, business-driven changes, and consumer-driven changes. Our analysis aims to deepen the understanding of sustainability marketing and inspire marketers to explore questions and solutions that will contribute to a sustainable future.

hot.title: Are lonely youngsters turning to chatbots for companionship? The relationship between chatbot usage and social connectedness in Danish high-school students
hot.abstract: • 2.44 % of Danish high-school students engage in mutual participative conversations or seek emotional support from chatbots. • Students who engage in such interactions with chatbots are lonelier than their peers. • Students seem to be using chatbots to cope with negative feelings. Are lonely youngsters turning to chatbots to fill their social needs? The present research contributes to the ongoing scientific endeavors to understand the adoption of chatbots as social companions. Specifically, we examined how many Danish high-school students engage in friend-like conversations with chatbots, why they engage in such conversations, and whether this trend is associated with the sense of social connectedness (operationalized as loneliness and perceived social support). In pursuing this goal, a preregistered mixed-methods cross-sectional survey study was carried out. A total sample of 1599 students from 15 Danish high schools was collected. In total, 234 students (14.6 %) responded that they engaged in friend-like conversations with chatbots. Qualitative thematic analyses of free-text responses revealed two dominant ways of engaging with chatbots: utilitarian conversations ( n = 174) and social-supportive conversations ( n = 39). A major finding was that social-supportive chatbot users reported significantly more loneliness than non-chatbot users ( d = 0.53) and utilitarian chatbot users ( d = 0.52). Furthermore, social-supportive chatbot users also reported significantly less perceived social support than non-chatbot users ( d = −0.46). Analyses also showed significant associations between higher loneliness and less perceived social support and various situational triggers for initiating conversations with chatbots, including bad mood, a need for self-disclosure, and a sense

latest.title: Pengaruh Kualitas Pelayanan dan Electronic Word of Mouth (eWOM) Terhadap Keputusan Pembelian pada Koka Ramen Express Sudirman
latest.venue: Jurnal Penelitian Ekonomi Manajemen dan Bisnis
latest.abstract: The increasingly competitive culinary industry requires businesses to improve service quality and manage their digital reputation to influence consumer purchasing decisions. This study aims to examine the effects of service quality and Electronic Word of Mouth (eWOM) on purchasing decisions among consumers of Koka Ramen Express Sudirman, both partially and simultaneously. This research employs a quantitative approach with a causal associative design. Data were collected through an online questionnaire using purposive sampling involving 120 respondents who had previously purchased and consumed products at Koka Ramen Express Sudirman. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with the assistance of IBM SPSS Statistics 29. The results indicate that service quality has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.207 and a significance level of less than 0.001. Electronic Word of Mouth also has a positive and significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a regression coefficient of 0.184 and a significance level of less than 0.001. Simultaneously, both variables have a significant effect on purchasing decisions, with a coefficient of determination of 63.6%. Service quality is the more dominant factor influencing purchasing decisions compared to eWOM. These findings imply that management should improve employee friendliness, service speed, and restaurant cleanliness while optimizing social media activities and responding professionally to customer reviews to strengthen consumer confidence in making purchasing decisions.

latest.title: Digital and social media marketing: a bibliometric mapping from 2020 to 2025
latest.abstract: Abstract Digital and social media marketing is reshaping how firms communicate with consumers, gather market intelligence, manage customer journeys, and build brand relationships. This study followed the PRISMA framework to select relevant Scopus-indexed articles between 2020 and 2025 under the business, management, and accounting subject area, using the search terms “digital marketing” and “social media marketing” in titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search, conducted on 20 February 2026 and restricted to open-access, English-language, final-stage journal articles, yielded 1,054 articles. Performance analysis, citation analysis, author-keyword co-occurrence mapping, an average-publication-year overlay, co-citation analysis, and bibliographic coupling were conducted using VOSviewer. Findings reveal publication growth, particularly during 2024 and 2025. Indonesia was the leading country by publications, whereas the UK was the most influential country by citations. Additionally, the “Journal of Business Research” is the most influential, while “Cogent Business & Management” is the most productive journal; the most-cited document is “Setting the future of digital and social media marketing research: Perspectives and research propositions,” with 1,806 citations, produced by “International Journal of Information Management.” Four of the ten prominent authors published six papers each, including Saura, J.R., and Huertas-Garcia, R., both affiliated with Spanish institutions. Keyword mapping identifies digital marketing, social media marketing, social media, consumer behavior, marketing, and purchase intention as central themes. This study clarifies the post-2020 knowledge structure of the open-access segment of this literature, proposes that digital and social media marketi

latest.title: Residual Self-Guided Quantum Vision Adversarial Attention Network for Predicting AI-Driven Financial Performance in Automobile Industries
latest.abstract: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in the automobile banking industry and its impact on the business processes is very fast, the impact of AI techniques in financial performance is not fully understood. The challenge here is that banks involved in the automotive sector often have fragmented disclosures of AI and inconsistent metrics, making it challenging to come up with accurate predictions of the financial impact of AI. To address this gap, they propose a model known as “Residual Self-Guided Quantum Vision Adversarial Attention Network for Predicting AI-Driven Financial Performance in Automobile Industries. To fill this gap, they propose a model called “Residual Self-Guided Quantum Vision Adversarial Attention Network for Predicting AI-Driven Financial Performance in Automobile Industries.in the automobile banking industry has transformed business processes, yet how AI techniques influence financial performance is not yet fully understood. The difficulty here lies in scattered AI disclosures and disparate metrics that hinder effective forecasts of financial results in car-related banks. In order to bridge this gap, the research introduces a model called “Residual Self-Guided Quantum Vision Adversarial Attention Network for Predicting AI-Driven Financial Performance in Automobile Industries.” The analysis relies on a dataset called “AI Techniques on Financial Performance of Automobile Industries,” which contains 131 annual report records for sixteen Indian-listed banks from 2015 to 2023. This dataset captures keyword-based AI disclosures, as well as institutional and financial indicators. Data pre-processing is done through the use of the Correlation Coefficient with Min–Max Weighted (CCMMW) method to normalize and fine-tune the input parameters, while

latest.title: Platforming musicians: Copyright capture, recursive commodification, and embedded generative AI in music platforms
latest.abstract: This article analyzes how music platforms in China recruit musicians and integrate them into systems of production, promotion, and circulation. It introduces three interrelated concepts to explain how this integration occurs. Copyright capture identifies the moment of recruitment and acquisition during which platforms bring musicians and their copyrighted works into platform infrastructures. Recursive commodification describes the processes through which copyright, visibility, promotion, data, and production become increasingly interconnected, with value generated at one stage becoming an input into the next. Embedded generative AI intensifies these dynamics by bringing technological mediation and music data into creative production. Drawing on interviews with musicians and industry practitioners, walkthrough analyses of platform interfaces, and documentary materials, we show how musicians become simultaneously producers of copyrighted works, generators of data, and consumers of platform services. We argue that musicians must negotiate new relations of dependence as creative production is progressively integrated into systems of evaluation, promotion, AI assistance, and monetization.

latest.title: From Price to Value: How Procurement Practices Reshape Competition in Medical Device Markets
latest.abstract: Procurement affects both the prices paid for medical devices and the conditions under which suppliers compete. Broader value-based assessment may reward clinical performance and life-cycle savings but may also raise bidding costs and favor incumbents. This conceptual study examines that tension through a focused, non-systematic review of economic theory, peer-reviewed studies, and public procurement documents. It develops four conditional propositions on aggregation, verifiable quality, contractual governance, and evidence-related entry barriers. The framework separates static purchasing efficiency from dynamic market contestability, including supplier entry, switching, and innovation. Evidence from U.S. group purchasing, Canadian tenders, Dutch purchaser interviews, UK experiments, and European procurement frameworks is compared according to the claims each design can support. Available evidence identifies specific expenditure and decision-process effects but does not establish a universal causal impact of value-based procurement on long-run competition. The paper argues for independently verifiable criteria, proportionate evidence requirements, workable contract exit, and continuing opportunities for qualified suppliers. Price-based awards may remain suitable where products are genuinely comparable and downstream differences are small.

latest.title: Foreign direct investment inflows, divestment and internationalisation: panel evidence from African economies, 2010–2023
latest.abstract: Abstract This study examines how foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows and foreign direct divestment (FDD) are associated with the internationalisation of African economies. Using an unbalanced panel of 47 African countries (618 country-year observations, 2010–2023), internationalisation is measured with the KOF trade and financial globalisation indices, while FDI inflows and FDD (the absolute value of negative net FDI inflows) are scaled by GDP and log-transformed. Two-way fixed-effects and two-step System GMM estimators are complemented by partial-sum asymmetry tests, Hansen panel-threshold models with institutional quality as the threshold variable, and income-group heterogeneity analysis based on the World Bank classification. FDI inflows are robustly and positively associated with trade globalisation in the fixed-effects models (β = 1.148, p = .006) and with financial globalisation in the dynamic and lagged specifications. Divestment is negatively associated with trade globalisation when estimated on its own and in the dynamic model, but the association is imprecise once FDI inflows are controlled for, is concentrated in lower-middle-income economies, and is driven largely by Angola and the Republic of Congo, which together account for 88% of divestment in the sample. Distributed-lag estimates show that the divestment association with trade globalisation materialises with a two-year lag (cumulative effect − 3.323, p = .026) and intensifies with natural-resource dependence. There is no statistically significant evidence that internationalisation responds asymmetrically to increases and decreases in investment. Threshold estimates indicate that the FDI–trade association is confined to economies with weaker institutional quality, contrary to the expectation that str

latest.title: Developing a Workplace Mental-Health Profiling Database System Integrated with Islamic Values
latest.venue: TAFHIM IKIM Journal of Islam and the Contemporary World
latest.abstract: Workplace mental-health profiling systems promise early intervention and psychosocial risk mitigation, yet in employment settings they introduce acute hazards of managerial surveillance, coercion, discrimination, and moral misclassification. This article develops a conceptual model for workplace mental-health profiling within Muslim-majority contexts by integrating Islamic ethical principles with Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory and privacy-by-design governance. It contends that Islamic ethics must function not as ornamental religious rhetoric, but as an institutional constraint on corporate power. Foundational concepts—specifically tawḥīd (divine unity), fiṭrah (primordial nature), iḥsān (moral excellence), amānah (fiduciary trust), sirr (confidentiality), and ʿadl (justice)—reorient profiling from individual risk categorisation toward structural psychosocial risk governance, employee dignity, confidentiality, and institutional accountability. Applying design-science conceptual modelling, this normative framework is operationalised into explicit system parameters: voluntary participation, enforceable non-retaliation guarantees, strict data minimisation, complete insulation from performance appraisals, aggregate-only reporting, and the absolute prohibition of spiritual data extraction.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Promosi Melalui Implementasi Tiktok Ads untuk Meningkatkan Engagement Dasilva Batik Malang
latest.abstract: Dasilva Batik Malang is an MSME producing modern batik clothing whose TikTok engagement has declined due to inconsistent digital promotion and unused TikTok Ads potential. This research identifies TikTok Ads implementation as a digital promotion strategy, analyzes engagement differences among entertainment, storytelling, and promotional content, and determines the most effective content type, and identifies the obstacles encountered. The research applies the Kemmis and MeTaggart action research model through planning, action, observation, and reflection. The unit of analysis comprises 20 people: the business owner, marketing experts, computer experts, and prospective consumers selected purposively. The EPIC Model questionnaire was tested for validity using Pearson Product Moment correlation and reliability using Cronbach's Alpha via IBM SPSS Statistics 26. The EPIC Rate assessment showed all three contents were effective, with promotional content scoring highest (4.16). However, the actual engagement rate after publication via TikTok Ads showed entertainment content performed best (1.99%), followed by promotional (1.68%) and storytelling content (1.63%). Dasilva Batik Malang is advised to produce-more entertainment content without abandoning promotional and storytelling content, while future research should apply A/B Testing, add content variations, and increase the promotion budget for more representative results.

latest.title: Between Play and Pressure: Pop Mart's 'Labubu' Craze, Blind-Box Consumption, and Emotional Socialization Among Primary School Students in Beijing
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This study investigated the psychological, consumerist, and educational intersections of Pop Mart’s ‘Labubu’ craze, analyzing how blind-box retail mechanisms impact peer dynamics and emotional socialization among primary school students in Beijing. Employing a comprehensive desk-based methodology that synthesized verified qualitative and quantitative secondary sources including municipal consumer protection reports, corporate market filings, and primary empirical school-district surveys the research examined the structural drivers of juvenile collectible consumption. Findings revealed that the algorithmic gamification of blind boxes intensifies status anxiety and peer-group stratification, compelling young learners to utilize scarce ‘secret edition’ figures as compensatory social currency. Concurrently, children internalize retail unboxing as a surrogate coping mechanism against rigorous academic pressures characteristic of Beijing’s primary education system. While informal peer trading networks fostered localized negotiation and community building, unmanaged commercial consumption precipitated compulsive spending habits and amplified classroom socio-economic divides. These insights illustrate the pressing necessity for cross-institutional regulatory oversight, school-based critical media literacy curricula, and parental financial guidance frameworks within contemporary urban educational ecosystems.

latest.title: AI-Assisted Negotiation Training: A Quasi-Experimental Examination of Buyers’ and Sellers’ Perceived Negotiation Performance in a Used-Car Sales Simulation
latest.abstract: Background: Evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) as a preparatory learning aid for novice human negotiators remains limited in consumer negotiation simulations. Existing work emphasizes automated agents rather than students preparing to negotiate. Against this backdrop, the present study examined changes in students’ perceived negotiation performance, differences in those changes between buyer and seller roles, and the purposes for which students used AI during a simulated used-car sale. The outcome was perceived performance, not economic results. Methodology: A single-group, repeated-measures quasi-experiment involved 74 undergraduate business students enrolled in a negotiation course at a university in Bangkok, Thailand. Thirty-seven students served as buyers and 37 as sellers. Participants completed two negotiations outside regular class hours within a 24–48-hour period, retaining their assigned roles and using the same scenario. The first round was conducted without AI assistance. Before the second round, students spent approximately five minutes preparing with generative AI tools of their choice for information analysis, strategy planning, role-play, or feedback. Each negotiation lasted approximately five to seven minutes. Perceived negotiation performance was assessed using five-item self-report scales in each condition. Paired-samples t-tests and a mixed-design analysis of variance (ANOVA) examined differences between conditions and across roles. Reported purposes of AI use were summarized descriptively. Results: Students reported higher perceived negotiation performance after AI-assisted preparation (M = 4.45, SD = 0.42) than after the preceding non-AI round (M = 3.78, SD = 0.58). The mean difference was 0.67 points, t(73) = −9.23, p < .001, with a large sta
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Factors associated with anxiety among college students: a combined analysis using regression and fsQCA
latest.abstract: Background This study explores the associations of information overload (IO), perceived involution (PI), psychological richness (PR), and meaning in life (MIL) with anxiety among college students. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 1,325 college students. A demographic questionnaire, the IO scale, the PI scale, the PR scale, and the MIL scale served as the measurement tools. Spearman correlation analysis was applied to examine the bivariate associations among variables. Linear mixed models and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) were adopted to investigate the interrelationships between IO, PI, PR, MIL, and anxiety. Results The linear mixed model results indicated that IO had positive indirect associations with anxiety via both MIL and PR. PI showed a positive direct association with anxiety but negative indirect associations through MIL and PR. The fsQCA results further revealed that no single antecedent condition was necessary for anxiety. One high-anxiety configuration was dominated by the core conditions of high IO and high PI, along with the absence of PR and MIL. Conclusion College students’ anxiety is associated with both external stressors and internal psychological resources. These preliminary findings may inform future longitudinal and intervention studies.

latest.title: Legal Challenges in Protecting the Rights of Digital Payment Instrument Users: The Case of Mongolia
latest.venue: Advances in Social Sciences Research Journal
latest.abstract: The rapid expansion of digital payment services has transformed financial transactions by making payments faster, more convenient, and accessible to a wider population. However, the increasing use of mobile banking, electronic money, digital wallets, QR-code payments, and other electronic payment instruments has created new challenges for consumer protection. These include unauthorized transactions, payment fraud, misuse of personal data, service interruptions, insufficient disclosure of information, and difficulties in recovering lost funds. Such developments raise concerns about whether existing legal frameworks provide adequate protection for users of digital payment services. This article examines the legal challenges associated with protecting the rights of digital payment users in Mongolia, drawing on selected regulatory approaches from Singapore, India, and China. The study adopts a doctrinal and comparative legal research approach, based on an analysis of relevant legislation, regulatory instruments, and scholarly literature. It examines Mongolia’s Law on the National Payment System, which establishes the legal foundations for protecting payment users, ensuring the security and reliability of payment systems, and supervising payment service providers. The analysis also considers the extent to which the existing framework addresses practical issues, particularly liability for unauthorized transactions, fraud reporting and investigation, complaint handling, personal data protection, and access to effective remedies. The comparative analysis highlights several regulatory approaches that may offer useful lessons for Mongolia. These include Singapore’s risk-based regulatory framework and consumer protection guidelines, India's rules governing customer liability for u

latest.title: EXPRESS: From Trends to Tweets: The Impact of Trendjacking on Consumer Engagement on Social Media
latest.abstract: Brands increasingly insert themselves into trending online cultural moments, a practice known as trendjacking, yet evidence on its effectiveness is mixed. Combining over 660,000 posts from 356 Fortune-listed companies (2018–2022) with trending topic data from X, we find that trendjacking increases social media engagement by 120.8%. We further find that trendjacking’s effectiveness varies by timing, trend type, and brand personality. Engagement is highest when brands post on the day following and on the day a trend first enters X’s top five trends. Effectiveness also varies by trend type, with pop culture trends generating the most engagement. Brand personality further shapes these effects, as exciting brands do best with pop culture trends, whereas rugged brands perform better with political trends. We further conduct two controlled experiments across different product categories, controlling for post and topic characteristics, and find consistent evidence that trendjacking increases engagement. These findings offer important implications for managers seeking to leverage trending topics in their social media strategy.

latest.title: From emotional comfort to relational investment in generative AI companionship: evidence from SEM and fsQCA
latest.abstract: With the rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence (AI), chatbots are evolving from instrumental assistants into emotionally responsive companions. This study develops a low-friction relational process model to examine the relationships linking generative AI companionship with emotional relief and positive social investment. AI emotional responsiveness, non-judgemental interaction, and memory-based continuity were conceptualized as interaction conditions, while perceived being understood, deep self-disclosure, and synthetic attachment were specified as psychological mechanisms. Structural equation modeling (SEM), bootstrap mediation analysis, moderation analysis, and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) were employed to analyse 765 valid responses from generative AI chatbot users. The SEM results show that non-judgemental interaction exhibits the most consistent pattern of associations with perceived being understood, deep self-disclosure, synthetic attachment, emotional relief, and positive social investment. Perceived being understood and synthetic attachment show relatively stable mediating patterns, whereas deep self-disclosure is significantly associated with emotional relief but shows a less consistent association with positive social investment. Perceived AI safety and self-disclosure habit play differentiated moderating roles. The fsQCA findings reveal three configurations for high emotional relief and four configurations for high positive social investment, complementing the SEM results. This study provides a systematic account of generative AI companionship and offers implications for safer and relationship-oriented AI design.

latest.title: A Quantitative Study on the Role of Government Incentives in Fostering Entrepreneurship in the Saudi SME Sector
latest.venue: Journal of Management Practices Humanities and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Despite being a major component of the Kingdom’s economic diversification strategy under Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030, creative entrepreneurs face recurring challenges such as limited access to small business funding, a lack of skills, and difficulties in administrative procedures. Based on institutional theory and incentive theory, this study analyzes the direct effects of three types of public support measures (direct financial support, tax exemptions, subsidy training) and the moderating effect of perceived bureaucratic burden on entrepreneurial orientation. Survey data were collected using a purposive sampling method and a cross-sectional design from 212 creative small- and medium-sized business managers and founders in Saudi Arabia and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The empirical results show that all three policy instruments have a positive impact on entrepreneurship, with targeted financial grants having the greatest direct impact, followed by tax breaks and subsidized training. In addition, perceived bureaucratic burden has a strong negative moderating effect on all three relationships, reducing the positive effect of grants, tax relief, and training programs. The model has an explanatory power of 66.6% in explaining fostering entrepreneurship. From these findings, it can be concluded that financial and capacity-building enablers are indispensable for the success of creative businesses; however, they can only be effective if institutional access is facilitated and procedures are streamlined. The study offers key insights for policymakers and cultural development institutions seeking to maximize public interventions in emerging creative ecosystems.

latest.title: Connect, Engage and Co-Create: The Role of Social Interactivity, Support and Identification in Driving Value Co-Creation in Live-Commerce
latest.abstract: Abstract Interactivity serves as a central element underpinning both live-commerce and value co-creation. An expanding number of studies have demonstrated their initiatives to validate the role of interactivity in live-commerce. However, there exists a void in current literature that translates interactivity to value co-creation behaviour. Addressing this gap, the study proposes a socially embedded process in which interactivity function as a primary driver of consumer-streamer value co-creation. Grounded in social support and social identification theory, the study provides a holistic model explaining how dual interactivity stimulates social support, which thereafter generates consumer-streamer identification, ultimately leading to value co-creation behaviour. Interestingly, the consumer involvement role couldn’t be established. As an additional analytical step, Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IPMA) was administrated on the data. In doing so, the current study helps strategic decision-makers to identify key performance indicators in the value co-creation mechanism and thus maintain a competitive edge within live-commerce.

latest.title: EXPRESS: Nation Brands and Firm Branding Strategy: Bibliometric, Conceptual, Econometric and Wavelet Analyses
latest.abstract: Nation brands and firm branding strategy are inextricably linked. However, the two streams of literature have evolved, and are often discussed, independently. This study provides a bibliometric analysis that examines the connection between these two research domains by drawing insights from 2,226 studies published between 1967 and 2025. This study provides a broad overview of how the field has developed over the past five decades. Building on social network theory and keyword co-occurrence map analysis, five interconnected thematic clusters are identified: (1) country-of-origin effects and consumer country dispositions, (2) digital engagement and customer relationships, (3) corporate social responsibility and trust, (4) brand equity and strategic brand management, and (5) marketing strategy and financial outcomes. By combining non-parametric, parametric, and wavelet analyses of the evolving knowledge structure with the identification of the longitudinal social network underlying the literature, this study clarifies the observed dynamics among the thematic clusters. Moreover, it supports a conceptual framework that differentiates foundational clusters from clusters acting as propelling mechanisms of knowledge diffusion, and emerging “rising star” clusters, contributing to the consolidation of new studies on nation brands and firm branding strategies. Scholarly and managerial implications, future research directions, and limitations are discussed.

latest.title: ASSESSMENT OF CONSUMER AWARENESS AND ADOPTION OF GREEN MARKETING AND WASTE MINIMIZATION PRACTICES IN SRINAGAR CITY, JAMMU & KASHMIR
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
authors: *1Mr. Sahil Bin Bashir, 2Dr. Asif Nazir, 3Ms. Ifshana Shafi, 3Dr. Murtaza, 3Dr. Aqib, 4Mr. Shaikh Anaitullah, 4Mr. Peerzada Mohammad Idrees, 4Ms. Saima Aijaz, 4Mr. Faisal Altaf Wani, 4Ms. Suraiya Mir, 4Ms. Fozia Subzar, 4Ms. Aabida Assadullah, 4Mr. Hilal Ahmad Bhat
latest.abstract: Background: Growing environmental concerns have increased the importance of sustainable consumption, green marketing, and waste minimization. Consumer awareness plays a critical role in encouraging the adoption of environmentally responsible products and practices. Srinagar City, Jammu and Kashmir, is experiencing increasing urbanization and waste-generation pressures, making consumer participation in sustainable practices particularly important. Objective: The present study aimed to assess consumer awareness regarding green marketing and waste minimization practices in Srinagar City and to examine the relationship between awareness, attitudes, and adoption of environmentally sustainable practices. Materials and Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional research design was adopted. Data were collected from 100 respondents comprising consumers, households, and small business owners in Srinagar City using a structured questionnaire. Stratified random sampling was used to obtain representation from different socioeconomic and demographic groups. The questionnaire assessed awareness of green marketing, perceptions of eco-friendly products, attitudes toward waste reduction, recycling and reuse, factors influencing sustainable purchasing decisions, and perceived barriers to adopting green practices. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistical methods, including percentages, mean scores, and cross-tabulations. Results: The findings demonstrated a generally high level of awareness and positive attitudes toward green marketing among respondents. The mean score for belief in the concept of green marketing was 4.59, while awareness of companies adopting green practices had a mean score of 4.51. Respondents also strongly recognized the advantages of green products (mean = 4.27) a

latest.title: Generative AI in Consumer Decision Making: How Algorithmic Recommendations Shape Brand Trust
latest.venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
latest.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly moving from the back end of recommendation engines to the consumer-facing interface, where conversational assistants, generated product descriptions and personalised feeds increasingly decide what shoppers see, compare and buy. While the literature on algorithm aversion and algorithm appreciation explains when consumers accept algorithmic advice, little is known about how such advice reshapes trust in the brand that deploys it. This paper develops and specifies a multi-level, testable framework in which four attributes of a GenAI recommendation (perceived personalisation, perceived accuracy and relevance, transparency and explainability, and disclosure of the AI source) influence brand trust through two opposing appraisal pathways: perceived algorithmic competence and fairness, which build trust, and perceived manipulation and privacy concern, which erode it. Brand trust in turn drives purchase intention and loyalty, with AI literacy and task type (utilitarian versus hedonic) as boundary conditions. Nine hypotheses are derived from trust theory, the persuasion knowledge model and the human–automation literature, and a dynamic trust-calibration loop is proposed in which each decision cycle updates the trust baseline used in the next. A two-study empirical design is specified, comprising a PLS-SEM survey and a 3 × 2 × 2 online experiment, and a Monte Carlo power analysis shows that a survey of about 300 respondents gives at least 95% power for the main hypothesised paths, while a 600-participant experiment gives about 92% power for medium-small effects of disclosure. The paper contributes a brand-level, trust-centred account of GenAI recommendations, identifies transparency as the lever that most plausibly converts alg

latest.title: The Effect Of Live Streaming, Brand Trust, And Electronic Word Of Mouth (E-WOM) On Purchase Decision For Sattka Basic On Tiktok E-Commerce (Survey of Sattka Basic Consumers in Tasikmalaya City): Dini Fauziah Amri, Budhi Wahyu Fitriadi, Dudu Risana
latest.venue: Journal of Law Social Science and Management Review
latest.abstract: This study aims to determine the influence of live streaming, brand trust, and electronic word-of-mouth (EWOM) on purchase decisions for Sattka Basic on the TikTok e-commerce platform (Survey of Sattka Basic Consumers in Tasikmalaya City). The method used in this study is descriptive quantitative research. The population for this study consists of consumers who purchase Sattka Basic products, with a total population that is unknown. The sample comprised 100 respondents selected through non-probability sampling using purposive sampling. The analysis tool used was multiple linear regression analysis using SPSS version 26. The results of this study indicate that, simultaneously, Live Streaming, Brand Trust, and Electronic Word of Mouth (EWOM) have a simultaneous effect on purchasing decisions. Partially, Live Streaming, Brand Trust, and Electronic Word of Mouth (EWOM) have a positive and significant effect on the decision to purchase Sattka Basic on the TikTok e-commerce platform.

latest.title: The Mediating Role of Digital Literacy Between Financial Literacy and Investment Scam Awareness
latest.venue: International Journal of Accounting and Business Finance
latest.abstract: This study analyses whether digital literacy mediates the relationship between financial literacy and investment scam awareness. Despite the rapid expansion of digital financial services, there remains limited knowledge of whether financial and digital literacy interact to shape resistance to online investment scams. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among undergraduates who were selected through stratified random sampling in Sri Lanka. Financial literacy is measured through budgeting skills, financial attitude, financial product literacy and risk awareness. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was applied to estimate the direct effects and mediating effects. Budgeting skills, product literacy and risk awareness enhance digital literacy, while financial attitude shows no meaningful effect. Digital literacy exhibits the strongest direct influence on investment scam awareness. Mediation analysis confirms that digital literacy transmits the effects of budgeting skills, product literacy and risk awareness to scam awareness, whereas financial attitude remains non-significant. The study conceptualizes digital literacy as a coping appraisal mechanism that enables individuals to operationalize financial knowledge in digital financial environments. Guided by Protection Motivation Theory, the study interprets financial literacy as supporting threat appraisal and digital literacy as supporting coping appraisal. The single institution, cross-sectional and self-reported design may restrict generalizability and causal inference. Future studies should use multi-site samples, longitudinal designs, fraud simulation experiments.

latest.title: PROMOTIONAL MARKETING STRATEGIES AND CUSTOMER RETENTION: THE ROLES OF CUSTOMER SATISFACTION AND TRUST IN MELCOM, ACCRA
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: This study examines the effect of promotion mix strategies on customer retention among Melcom customers in Accra, Ghana, with particular emphasis on the mediating roles of customer satisfaction and trust. The study is motivated by increasing competition in the retail industry and the need for organizations to adopt effective marketing communication strategies to attract and retain customers. It focuses on key elements of the promotion mix, including advertising, sales promotion, personal selling, public relations and direct marketing, and their influence on customer retention. Although previous studies have established relationships between promotional activities and customer retention, their findings remain mixed, suggesting the need to examine the mechanisms through which promotional strategies influence customer retention. Specifically, the study investigates whether customer satisfaction and trust mediate the relationship between promotion mix strategies and customer retention. Drawing on the marketing communication and customer relationship perspectives, the study seeks to provide insights into how effective promotional activities can strengthen customer relationships, enhance consumer confidence and encourage repeat patronage. The study is expected to contribute to the understanding of promotional effectiveness in Ghana's retail sector and provide practical guidance for improving customer retention strategies at Melcom. Its findings will also offer useful implications for retail managers seeking to develop customer-centred promotional strategies that promote long-term loyalty and sustainable competitive advantage.
