latest.abstract: Abstract Digital and social media marketing is reshaping how firms communicate with consumers, gather market intelligence, manage customer journeys, and build brand relationships. This study followed the PRISMA framework to select relevant Scopus-indexed articles between 2020 and 2025 under the business, management, and accounting subject area, using the search terms “digital marketing” and “social media marketing” in titles, abstracts, and keywords. The search, conducted on 20 February 2026 and restricted to open-access, English-language, final-stage journal articles, yielded 1,054 articles. Performance analysis, citation analysis, author-keyword co-occurrence mapping, an average-publication-year overlay, co-citation analysis, and bibliographic coupling were conducted using VOSviewer. Findings reveal publication growth, particularly during 2024 and 2025. Indonesia was the leading country by publications, whereas the UK was the most influential country by citations. Additionally, the “Journal of Business Research” is the most influential, while “Cogent Business & Management” is the most productive journal; the most-cited document is “Setting the future of digital and social media marketing research: Perspectives and research propositions,” with 1,806 citations, produced by “International Journal of Information Management.” Four of the ten prominent authors published six papers each, including Saura, J.R., and Huertas-Garcia, R., both affiliated with Spanish institutions. Keyword mapping identifies digital marketing, social media marketing, social media, consumer behavior, marketing, and purchase intention as central themes. This study clarifies the post-2020 knowledge structure of the open-access segment of this literature, proposes that digital and social media marketi

latest.title: Comfort, camaraderie, conflict, contamination: examining identity and boundary work in fan experiences during troubling times
latest.abstract: During troubling times, consumers may turn to their favourite fandom to help them through, and we posit that there are overlooked aspects of fandom that hold value during troubling times. Using the context of 2020 and the release of the Harry Potter at Home initiative, we explore how fans experience fandom during troubling times. We find that fans may experience their fandom as: (1) comfort, (2) camaraderie, (3) conflict, or (4) contamination. We extend marketing theory by (1) reconceptualising fandom as an inherently imaginative phenomenon, (2) identifying fandom as providing stability and creating instability in troubling times, (3) explaining how identity and boundary work helps fans navigate troubling times, and (4) providing a framework for how the same fandom can be both stabilising and destabilising, depending on whether trouble is internal or external to it.

latest.title: From experience to loyalty: A conceptual framework for building customer–brand relationships in retailing
latest.abstract: Brand loyalty has emerged as a critical factor amid intensifying competition in the retail sector. It serves as a key driver of brand equity, as loyal customers are more likely to engage in repeat purchase behaviour and promote the brand through positive word-of-mouth. Consequently, brand loyalty contributes significantly to customer retention and long-term business profitability. Sustaining brand loyalty has become increasingly challenging, as consumers are exposed to a growing number of competing brands and alternatives. Previous studies have examined the individual effects of retail brand experience (RBE), brand satisfaction, brand trust, and brand love on brand loyalty. However, limited research attention has been given to how these constructs interrelate and jointly influence brand loyalty within the retail context. This conceptual paper has thus developed an integrated framework comprising 11 formal propositions, grounded in the Stimulus–Organism–Response Theory and Expectancy-Disconfirmation Theory. The model conceptualises RBE as the stimulus; brand satisfaction, brand trust, and brand love as the cognitive, relational, and emotional states representing the organism; and brand loyalty as the consumer response, encompassing attitudinal and behavioural aspects. The proposed conceptual model will serve as a foundation for future empirical research and contribute to both academic knowledge and managerial understanding of brand management and consumer behaviour.

latest.title: Less Disclosed, More Minimal: How Soft Launches of Romantic Relationships Promote Minimalist Consumption
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Soft and hard launches of romantic relationships have become increasingly prevalent forms of relationship disclosure in digital environments, yet little is known about whether these forms of disclosure influence subsequent consumer behavior. Across four experiments, we show that soft (vs. hard) relationship disclosures increase consumers' preference for minimalist consumption. We identify preference for subtle self‐presentation as a potential explanatory mechanism underlying this effect: soft relationship disclosures increase preference for subtle self‐presentation, which subsequently enhances preference for minimalist consumption. Relationship privacy orientation moderates this process, such that the indirect effect of soft launch on minimalist consumption via preference for subtle self‐presentation strengthens as relation privacy increases. A marketplace urgency cue also moderates this process, such that the indirect effect holds when the cue is absent but diminishes when it is present. These findings demonstrate how romantic relationship disclosure types influence subsequent marketplace preferences.

latest.title: Balancing budgets and emotions: The dual influence of economic and psychological factors on furniture purchase decisions during relocation
latest.abstract: Furniture purchasing is a high-involvement consumer decision, particularly during relocation, when consumers must navigate both financial and psychological considerations. Despite extensive research on consumer behaviour, limited attention has been given to how these factors jointly shape furniture purchase decisions during relocation, particularly in the Malaysian context. This exploratory study employed a quantitative research design to examine the influence of economic and psychological factors on furniture purchase decisions before relocation. Data were collected from 218 adult consumers through a structured online questionnaire and analysed using descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, and multiple regression analysis. The findings show that both economic and psychological factors significantly influence consumer purchase decisions, with psychological factors emerging as the stronger predictor. This suggests that, alongside financial considerations, consumers place considerable importance on comfort, personal preferences, lifestyle compatibility, and adjustment to their new living environment. The findings extend the application of the Theory of Reasoned Action and the Theory of Planned Behaviour to relocation-related consumer behaviour and contribute to a better understanding of high-involvement purchasing during significant life transitions. Practically, the findings suggest that furniture retailers and marketers should combine affordability and flexible purchasing options with strategies that address consumers’ psychological and lifestyle needs.

latest.title: Examining the role of artificial intelligence and social media marketing activities through the brand resonance model
latest.abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractIn an era where digital technologies are rapidly transforming consumer behavior, e-commerce platforms have emerged as primary channels for purchasing goods. This shift has prompted organizations to adapt their marketing strategies to increasingly competitive digital environments, particularly by applying artificial intelligence and social media to build consumer relationships and strengthen customer-based brand equity. This study aims to examine the effects of Artificial Intelligence Marketing Activities (AIMA) and Social Media Marketing Activities (SMMA) on brand resonance, using Keller’s brand resonance model as the main theoretical framework. Data were collected through an online survey from 210 respondents in Thailand and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that both AIMA and SMMA have significant positive effects on brand salience, brand performance, and brand imagery. These constructs subsequently influence brand judgments and feelings, ultimately leading to brand resonance. The findings extend the application of the brand resonance model to the digital marketing context, contribute to a deeper understanding of how AI-driven and social media marketing can be effectively managed on digital platforms, and provide practical implications for developing marketing strategies aimed at strengthening brand equity.AcknowledgementsThe authors would like to thank all participants for their contribution to this study.

latest.title: Which review cues matter most? Perceived authenticity as the dominant predictor of purchase intention toward Indonesian local fashion brands
latest.abstract: In digital fashion markets, consumers navigate a complex landscape of online reviews, although the cues they prioritize when evaluating local brands remain poorly understood. Grounded in signalling theory and the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM), this study develops a multi-cue framework examining how review content quality, review source credibility, perceived review authenticity, and emotional tone collectively predict purchase intention toward local fashion brands. Drawing on survey data from Generation Z consumers in Indonesia analyzed through PLS-SEM, the findings reveal a signal hierarchy: perceived review authenticity consistently emerges as the dominant evaluative cue, outweighing informational and credibility-based signals alike. This pattern suggests that consumers in identity-driven consumption contexts prioritize legitimacy verification above argument evaluation, a finding that departs from prior ELM-based review research in which argument quality typically dominates. Theoretically, the study contributes to signalling theory by suggesting that signal effectiveness depends on imitation cost relative to the prevailing manipulation environment and identifies a scope condition for ELM in contexts where message authenticity cannot be presumed. Practically, local fashion brands are advised to cultivate authentic consumer narratives rather than optimizing review volume or aggregate ratings.

latest.title: Content Marketing and Fan Engagement at Major Sporting Events: A Multiple-Case Study of Adidas, Coca-Cola, and Samsung
latest.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
latest.abstract: Major sporting events provide brands opportunities to interact with fans, but audience attention might not necessarily create stronger relationships with brands. Most studies focus on describing the effects of individual cases and lack a multidimensional framework for comparing brands across different event types (such as the FIFA World Cup and the Olympic Games) and industries. This essay will examine Adidas's "Family Reunion" at the 2022 FIFA world cup, Coca-Cola's "believing is Magic" at the 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup, and Samsung's "Open Always Wins" at the Paris 2024 Olympics. A qualitative multiple-case study uses published campaign documents and academic literature to compare the brand's objective, content, intended engagement, brand-event connections, and reported outcomes. The analysis found three approaches. Adidas builds on football identity and togetherness, Coca-Cola focuses on connecting its brand with encouragement and inclusion, and Samsung shows product usefulness within sport experiences. This comparison suggests prioritizing players' stories and fan communities in football campaigns, and diversifying athlete‑related experiences and practical services. These recommendations might remain provisional due to cases differing in brand category, event, and available evidence. Managers should connect a clear brand message with voluntary participation and evaluate awareness, brand attitudes, and commercial outcomes separately.

latest.title: Green purchasing behavior in marketing research: Trends forward based on bibliometric analysis
latest.abstract: This study uses bibliometric analysis to map the evolution, intellectual framework, and research gaps in Green Purchasing Behavior (GPB) literature. 1,546 documents were found by searching article titles, abstracts, and author keywords in the Scopus database. A final dataset of 123 peer-reviewed journal articles was examined following the use of a PRISMA-style screening procedure based on publication era (1994–2025), subject areas, document type, publishing stage, keyword relevance, source type, and language. VOSviewer, Harzing's Publish or Perish, and Scopus analytical tools were used to apply bibliometric methodologies, such as co-authorship, co-citation, bibliographic coupling, and keyword co-occurrence analyses, for performance analysis and science mapping. The findings show a robust development trend in Green Purchasing Behavior (GPB) research, especially since 2018, indicating increasing scholarly consolidation and growing research maturity. The results indicate that intention-based behavioral models, particularly the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), remain among the most influential theoretical foundations in GPB research. All things considered, this study offers a methodical summary of the development of GPB research and points out important gaps in theoretical diversity, multidisciplinary integration, and cross-contextual cooperation. These findings have important ramifications for the advancement of sustainable marketing theory and practice.

latest.title: Spatial competition and patron retention: evaluating competitive zones in casino CRM models
latest.abstract: Spatial dependence influences casino demand in competitive regional markets. Patrons prefer casinos that offer greater value relative to their travel effort, making proximity an important consideration when choosing among alternatives. However, predictive CRM models for identifying shifts in casino patron behavior have generally overlooked the geographic distribution of competing properties. This study evaluates Competitive Zones, a measure identifying whether a focal casino is the geographically nearest property to a patron using distances calculated through the Spherical Law of Cosines, and tests whether embedding this measure improves casino CRM models. Using survey data from patrons in the New England casino market following the opening of Encore Boston Harbor, patrons residing within a focal casino’s Competitive Zone were less likely to report declines in visitation, gaming expenditure, and wallet share than those residing outside it. Monte Carlo cross-validated logistic models further show that adding Competitive Zones to traditional CRM predictors and distance to the focal casino improved validation AUC by 2.7% to 3.6%, with a 13.0% improvement in the top decile lift index for wallet-share decline. Findings suggest that Competitive Zones offer a simple, accessible tool for strengthening casino CRM modeling and identifying patrons at risk of reduced activity.

latest.title: Augmented reality and tourists’ purchase intention for intangible cultural heritage products: A two-study investigation of Shu embroidered fans
latest.abstract: As a form of Chinese intangible cultural heritage, Shu embroidery faces increasing challenges in balancing traditional aesthetic preservation with contemporary market commercialization. Augmented Reality (AR) technology, with its distinctive advantage of integrating virtual and real elements, can support the innovative visual presentation of traditional crafts. This study examines how AR-enhanced visual presentation influences tourists’ purchase intention for Shu embroidered fans. Two independent quantitative studies, including a field experiment (Study 1) and a questionnaire survey (Study 2), were conducted. The survey collected 452 valid responses through convenience sampling in Chengdu, Sichuan Province, an area with profound Shu embroidery cultural roots, for structural equation modeling (SEM) analysis; the experiment randomly assigned 386 tourists (198 in the AR display group and 188 in the conventional display group) at two Chengdu tourist sites for independent-samples t-tests. The findings show that AR-enhanced visual presentation is positively associated with tourists’ purchase intention; perceived aesthetic value and perceived authenticity exhibit bootstrap-supported indirect associations in this process; and cultural engagement moderates the relationship between AR-enhanced visual presentation and perceived aesthetic value. The experimental comparisons further indicated significantly higher perceived aesthetic value, perceived authenticity, and purchase intention in the AR display group than in the conventional display group, with large effect sizes (Cohen’s d ranging from 1.28 to 1.53). These findings offer theoretical and practical implications for the digital display of Shu embroidered fans and similar traditional cultural products.

latest.title: AI features and social influence affect Gen Z purchase intention and behavior through trust in an extended SOR model
latest.abstract: Driven by digital transformation in the global retail sector, this study investigates the psychological and behavioral mechanisms underlying Generation Z college students’ AI-assisted shopping experiences. It examines how four stimuli—AI algorithm transparency, user-friendliness, internet word of mouth (IWOM), and trust propensity—influence consumer trust and purchase intention, alongside the moderating effects of privacy concern and information collection behavior. Drawing on an extended Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, the research empirically validates the proposed framework using 979 valid online survey responses analyzed via SPSS 32. Results reveal that the four antecedents exert significantly positive effects on both consumer trust and purchase intention, with trust serving as a significant mediator between these antecedents and purchase intention. Additionally, information collection behavior positively moderates the relationship between IWOM and consumer trust, while privacy concern negatively moderates the relationship between AI algorithm transparency and consumer trust. This study offers novel theoretical insights into Gen Z’s AI shopping behaviors and provides practical implications: retailers should enhance AI algorithm transparency, optimize user interfaces, cultivate positive IWOM, and strengthen privacy protection to foster Gen Z’s trust and facilitate purchase conversion.

latest.title: Do inclusive retailers build stronger customer relationships? Evidence from a multi-wave repeated cross-sectional study
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: Retailers increasingly adopt diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility (DEIA) initiatives, yet limited evidence exists on whether and how consumers translate awareness of these initiatives into stronger customer relationships. Drawing on signaling theory, this study examines whether awareness of retailers' DEIA initiatives is associated with trust and loyalty, and whether this mechanism is consistent across annual samples and forms of diversity. Using a multi-wave repeated cross-sectional survey fielded across seven annual waves from 2019 to 2025, results show that awareness of DEIA initiatives is positively associated with trust, and trust is strongly associated with loyalty. The mechanism is consistent across all annual samples, while the magnitude varies to some extent. Although the results show variation across diversity forms, the trust-loyalty link remains consistently strong. These findings suggest that DEIA initiatives can operate as market signals for retailers’ broader customer base, with effects extending beyond the groups directly targeted by the initiatives. The study contributes to inclusive retailing research by connecting DEIA awareness with customer relationship outcomes and by showing that interventions should not be treated as interchangeable. For managers, the results highlight the importance of visible and context-sensitive DEIA initiatives embedded in the retail customer experience to support positive outcomes.

latest.title: Love to Fandom: Ethical Condition for Cosplayers Subjectivity
authors: André Luiz Maranhão de Souza Leão
latest.abstract: Abstract Cosplay is a fan production that allows its participants to express their subjective values through dressing up as characters from media products. Such phenomenon exemplifies the intricate dynamics of consumer relations since cosplay explores multiple aspects of consumer culture theory. Thus, drawing from fan studies and Foucauldian frameworks, the aim of the research is analyzing how cosplayer subjectivity is constituted. In this sense, the study performs an Ethnographic Foucauldian Genealogy, based on a corpora constituted of autoethnography, netnography, online ethnographic interviews and virtual ethnomethodology data. The results evidenced two subject-forms: Nailers, representing the position taken by cosplayers who take on the role of exemplary representing the cosplay phenomenon; and Guardians, highlighting how some cosplayers feel responsible for maintaining a community of practitioners that allows those interested in cosplay to feel comfortable. Both subjectivities share an ethic named as Love to fandom. Such ethic guide cosplayers to produce truths about the ways in which they interact or show solidarity between peers based on their own condition as fans, legitimizing autonomous and complementary subjectivities, and enhancing and ensuring experiences with cosplay practice. Thus, the study expands the possibilities of living love through consumption – here, inherent to fans. It is a love established and maintained by the consumers themselves both through the intense relationship with the products consumed and through interactions with their peers.

latest.title: Bridging Social Media Authenticity Gaps: Trust-Commitment Pathways to Brand Loyalty
latest.abstract: Indonesian K-12 private Islamic schools depend primarily on parental enrollment to remain viable. In cities where schools compete to attract and retain students, schools' ability to build strong relationships with parents has become increasingly important. Nevertheless, many schools still struggle to use social media to convey their educational and religious values. This study investigates how social media marketing actions affect parents' brand loyalty to Islamic schools by considering brand authenticity, customer-based brand equity, and brand trust through the lens of Trust-Commitment Theory. The study employs a quantitative explanatory methodology. This study examined parents of children attending private Islamic K-12 schools in Greater Jakarta. This study collected 280 valid responses through an online survey and used purposive sampling. The data were analyzed using structural equation modeling with the Partial Least Squares method. The results show that social media marketing makes parents see the brand as more authentic. This authenticity builds brand trust and customer-based brand equity, leading to greater parental loyalty to Islamic schools. The paper also draws on the Trust-Commitment Theory to examine Islamic K-12 education and highlights how honest digital communication helps build lasting relationships between schools and parents.

latest.title: The double-edged sword of virtual influencer anthropomorphism: a paradoxical framework of social presence and identity threat
latest.venue: Journal of Humanities and Applied Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how the perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers shape consumers’ attitude toward virtual influencers through the competing psychological pathways of social presence and identity threat. Design/methodology/approach Through a cross-sectional survey, a sample of 448 Instagram users in Egypt was collected and analyzed using CB-SEM through AMOS v.23. Findings Both perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers have a positive influence on both social presence and identity threat. Importantly, both social presence and identity threat concurrently mediate the relationships between both dimensions of anthropomorphism and attitudes toward virtual influencers. Therefore, both dimensions of anthropomorphism influence consumers’ attitudes toward virtual influencers through the positive mediating role of social presence and the negative mediating role of identity threat. Research limitations/implications The study expands anthropomorphism research to the virtual influencer context by showing that anthropomorphism is not unequivocally superior. Therefore, grounding in social presence and social identity theory, we suggest that anthropomorphism is a double-edged sword in shaping attitudes toward virtual influencers. Practical implications Both designers and marketers employing virtual influencers should consider the multi-dimensionality anthropomorphism. Moreover, they should aim to maximize social presence while reducing identity threat when utilizing virtual influencers. Originality/value This study conceptualizes anthropomorphism as a multifaceted construct composed of physical and psychological dimensions and it can work through two opposing positive and negative pathways.

latest.title: A Multi-layered identity-consumption model: integrating identity constructs, Guochao influence, and consumer willingness to purchase domestic fashion brands in China
latest.abstract: Guochao has transformed domestic fashion consumption in China into a symbolic, identity-driven practice. This study develops a multi-layered identity-consumption model linking national identity, cultural identity, consumer ethnocentrism, perceived quality, consumer trust, and purchase willingness, with Guochao influence as a moderator. Survey data were collected from 500 Chinese consumers aged 18 or older in Beijing, Sichuan, and Guangdong who had engaged with Guochao-related domestic fashion brands but had never purchased from them. Covariance-based structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis examined net associations and configurational pathways. National and cultural identities are positively associated with consumer ethnocentrism, which is subsequently associated with perceived quality, consumer trust, and purchase willingness. Guochao influence strengthens associations between identity-related and evaluative factors and purchase willingness. Configurational findings indicate multiple pathways associated with high purchase willingness, suggesting possible equifinality and asymmetry, although limited solution consistency warrants caution. The study extends identity-based consumption research by integrating identity formation, consumer evaluation, and symbolic-cultural amplification. Managers should combine culturally meaningful narratives with credible product quality and brand performance to strengthen purchase willingness among brand-aware non-purchasers.

latest.title: L'identité numérique au service de la personnalisation de l'expérience client : un levier de compétitivité pour les entreprises
latest.abstract: Résumé À l’ère du digital, l’identité des consommateurs se construit à travers les données qu’ils génèrent en ligne : profils, historiques d’achats, interactions et comportements numériques. Ces informations constituent une ressource stratégique pour les entreprises, qui les exploitent grâce au Big Data, à l’intelligence artificielle et aux outils CRM afin de proposer des expériences personnalisées. La personnalisation des offres, de la communication et des parcours clients renforce la satisfaction, la fidélisation et la proximité avec la marque. Elle devient ainsi un véritable levier de compétitivité, permettant aux entreprises de se différencier, d’améliorer leur performance marketing et d’optimiser leur productivité. Toutefois, cette dynamique soulève des défis liés à la vie privée, à la confiance numérique et à la régulation des données. Cet article s’attache à comprendre comment l’identité numérique des consommateurs, constituée par l’ensemble des données qu’ils laissent en ligne, peut être utilisée par les entreprises pour concevoir des expériences personnalisées. Il met en évidence les mécanismes par lesquels ces données favorisent l’adaptation des offres, la fidélisation des clients et l’optimisation des stratégies marketing. Il interroge également les retombées de cette personnalisation sur la compétitivité des entreprises, en soulignant à la fois les opportunités d’innovation et les défis liés à la confiance, à la régulation et à l’éthique à l’ère du digital.Mots clés : Identité numérique, Expérience personnalisée, Données clients, Compétitivité des entreprises. Abstract In the digital age, consumer identity is built through the data they generate online: profiles, purchase histories, interactions, and digital behaviors. This information is a strategic resourc

latest.title: From Consumption to Creation: Social Media Engagement and Visit Intention in Vietnamese Restaurants
latest.abstract: Customer engagement with brand-related content on social media is increasingly recognised as a multidimensional phenomenon. Drawing on the Consumers’ Online Brand-Related Activities (COBRA) framework, this study examines how content consumption, contribution, and creation influence consumers’ attitudes toward online reviews and ratings and their purchase/visit intentions in the restaurant industry. Existing research has largely focused on highly visible engagement behaviors, leaving fewer observable forms of engagement underexplored, particularly in emerging markets. A quantitative, cross-sectional design was employed using survey data from 509 social media users engaging with Golden Gate Restaurant Group brands in Vietnam. Measurement scales were adapted from established studies, and the proposed model was tested using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) with AMOS. The findings show that all three engagement dimensions have significant positive effects on attitudes toward online reviews and ratings and on purchase/visit intention. Content consumption, often considered a passive behavior, produced stronger effects on both attitudinal and behavioral outcomes than content contribution and creation. These results demonstrate the importance of low-visibility engagement behaviors in shaping consumer perceptions and decision-making processes. The study contributes to the literature by extending the COBRA framework to the restaurant context and providing evidence from an emerging market. From a managerial perspective, the findings suggest that restaurant marketers should develop social media strategies that encourage engagement across all behavioral levels rather than concentrating solely on content creation. Overall, the study highlights the strategic value of customer engage

latest.title: Brand Experience, Engagement, and Loyalty in Iraqi Retail
latest.venue: Central Asian Journal of Innovations on Tourism Management and Finance
latest.abstract: In Iraqi cities the shopper can buy the same product category from a neighbourhood shop, from a regional chain or from an international brand store, so the question why a customer returns to one brand is a practical one for the retailers there. In this study, the mediating role of customer engagement in the association between brand experience and customer loyalty has been examined in Iraqi urban retail markets, together with the moderating role of perceived value on the association between engagement and loyalty. A cross-sectional survey was carried out with a convenience sample of consumers, mainly in Baghdad, Mosul and Tikrit, where each respondent rated a brand bought in the previous three months. From 300 returns, 263 usable responses remained after the screening for missing data, straight-lining and multivariate outliers. The conditional process model (PROCESS Model 14) was estimated with 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples. It can be noted from the results that brand experience was positively associated with customer engagement (b = 0.533, p < .001) and with loyalty (total effect b = 0.506, p < .001), and engagement was related also positively to loyalty (b = 0.453, p < .001). The indirect effect of brand experience on loyalty through engagement was 0.242 (95% CI [0.162, 0.334]) and the direct path stayed significant, so the mediation is partial. The engagement × perceived value interaction was positive (b = 0.170, p = .032), and the index of moderated mediation was 0.092 (95% CI [0.008, 0.189]). This means that engagement carries a part of the link between experience and loyalty, and this part becomes larger when the customer judges that the brand gives more for its price. The reliability was acceptable, but the CR and AVE values derived from PCA were low,

latest.title: ИДЕАЛЬНЫЙ ИЛИ ЖИВОЙ: ПОЧЕМУ НЕИДЕАЛЬНЫЙ КОНТЕНТ ИНОГДА ВЫЗЫВАЕТ БОЛЬШЕ ДОВЕРИЯ?
latest.abstract: в статье рассматривается, почему профессиональная реклама не всегда воспринимается как искренняя и способна создавать дистанцию между брендом и потребителем, тогда как естественные публикации в социальных сетях зачастую вызывают у аудитории больше доверия. На основе российских и зарубежных научных исследований анализируется влияние блогеров, отзывов покупателей и пользовательского контента на отношение аудитории к брендам. Рассматриваются причины, по которым обычные фотографии, видео без сложного монтажа и честные отзывы могут казаться людям более убедительными. Также объясняется, почему естественная подача не всегда помогает вызвать доверие и почему важно открыто сообщать о рекламе.

latest.title: Analyzing Consumer Loyalty to Ultra‐Fast Fashion: An Integrative Analysis Based on the Stimulus‐Organism‐Response Model
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The ultra‐fast fashion industry generates massive online sales, partly because of its ability to attract the custom of Generation Z (Gen Z). Given that this generational cohort typically has low brand loyalty, this paper examines how the dimensions of the stimulus‐organism‐response (S‐O‐R) model explain Gen Z's loyalty to the ultra‐fast fashion industry. For this purpose, the analysis presented in this paper relies on both a linear and an evolutionary view of the S‐O‐R model. Based on data from 208 questionnaires completed by consumers of ultra‐fast fashion, two analytical phases were conducted: (1) partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) and (2) qualitative comparative analysis (QCA). The results of the first phase suggest that consumer sustainability consciousness is associated with brand loyalty directly and under mediation, whereas social media peer communication is associated with brand loyalty only under mediation by brand equity. The second phase shows the relevance of brand equity in explaining both high and low brand loyalty. The configurations explaining high brand loyalty or low brand loyalty show that the relationship of each outcome with consumer sustainability consciousness and social media peer communications reflects psychological mechanisms that allow consumers to overcome the cognitive dissonance between their attitudes and behavior.

latest.title: Strategic Hotel Location and Customer Repurchase Intention: Insights from Hotel sector
latest.venue: Global Journal of Management and Business Research
latest.abstract: The study intends to examine the impact of various customer engagement practices identified with respect to the Hotel location on repurchase intention. The perception of hotel customers towards these practices while assessing and organizing the decisions for repatronizing a hotel. It has been predominantly acknowledged that hotel locations play a significant role in repurchase intention. The study was conducted using a survey method, a structured, closed-ended questionnaire to collect responses from 375 hotel guests, and the calculation of descriptive statistics guided the exploration of the perception of customers towards these practices. Further, a study was carried out with regression analysis to examine the impact of various customer engagement practices on re-purchase intention. The study resulted a strong customer perception towards both natural and non-natural attribute of hotel location based engagement practices, with highest mean value (M=4.49), followed by camp/bonfire practices with vale of (M=3,39), and centralized location with the mean of (M=3.89), study also indicates significant impact of primary customer engagement practices in connection to their overall influence on repurchase intention. So it becomes a guiding tool for hotel owners and industry players to involve and focus on such practices while choosing a site or location for a hotel. The findings are applicable for hotel owners and new industry players to distinguish and focus on available sources of engagement and manage their access and reach to everyone.

latest.title: THEORETICAL FOUNDATIONS OF CORPORATE BRANDING: BRAND EQUITY, REPUTATIONAL SPILLOVERS, AND SHARED-BRAND RISKS
latest.abstract: This article examines the distribution of corporate brand equity, reputational spillovers, and their relationship with revenue using 4,816 quarterly observations from 40 corporate groups and 301 service units. Variance decomposition attributes 42.0% of brand-equity variation to corporate-level differences, 34.8% to unit-level differences, and 23.3% to changes over time. Fixed-effects estimates show that adverse incidents reduce brand equity by 5.83 points in affected units and 1.00 point in sister units, while awards increase equity by 2.39 and 0.43 points, respectively. Negative spillovers are strongest in branded houses (−1.77 points) and weakest in houses of brands (−0.13 points). A one-point increase in a unit’s own brand equity is associated with a 0.565-point increase in its revenue index, whereas sister-unit equity has no statistically significant additional association. The findings emphasize balancing shared-brand advantages against reputational risks and monitoring brand equity at the unit level.

latest.title: The Effect of Customer Relationship on Customer Loyalty Moderated by Customer Satisfaction at Dazzle Outfit Palembang
latest.venue: Equivalent Journal Of Economic Accounting and Management
latest.abstract: The increasingly competitive fashion retail industry requires companies not only to offer high-quality products but also to build long-term relationships with customers in order to maintain loyalty. Dazzle Outfit Palembang still faces several challenges, including suboptimal customer interaction, limited loyalty programs, and customer loyalty that has not been fully established despite relatively good levels of customer satisfaction. This study aims to analyze the effect of customer relationship on customer loyalty, the effect of customer satisfaction on customer loyalty, and the role of customer satisfaction in moderating the relationship between customer relationship and customer loyalty at Dazzle Outfit Palembang. This study employed a quantitative approach with a descriptive and causal-associative research design. The sample consisted of 100 customers selected using purposive sampling, with the criteria of being at least 17 years old and having made at least two purchases. Data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) with the assistance of SPSS. The results showed that customer relationship had a positive and significant effect on customer loyalty, with a significance value of 0.017. In contrast, customer satisfaction did not have a significant effect on customer loyalty, with a significant value of 0.099. The interaction between customer relationship and customer satisfaction was also not significant, with a significant value of 0.359, indicating that customer satisfaction did not moderate the relationship between customer relationship and customer loyalty. The Adjusted R Square value of 0.518 indicates that the model explains 51.8% of the variation in customer loyalty. This study confirms that stre

latest.title: Brand Image and Membership on Direct Booking Intention through Perceived Value in Resort Hotels
latest.abstract: This study examines the effects of brand image and membership on direct booking intention, with perceived value as a mediating variable at Jayakarta Hotels & Resorts. A quantitative approach was applied to 180 respondents across three Jayakarta properties, using purposive and proportionate stratified sampling and analyzed through SEM-PLS with SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that brand image has no significant direct effect on direct booking intention, while membership has a positive and significant effect. Both brand image and membership significantly influence perceived value, which subsequently affects direct booking intention. Perceived value fully mediates the effect of brand image and partially mediates the effect of membership. These findings highlight the importance of translating brand strength and membership benefits into perceived customer value to encourage direct bookings and reduce hotel dependence on Online Travel Agents (OTAs).

latest.title: The effects of visual cues on sustainable consumer behavior and their underlying mechanisms
latest.abstract: 摘要： 视觉元素是消费者感知环境刺激、加工产品信息的重要输入, 对可持续消费决策具有重要影响。针对现有关于视觉元素影响可持续消费的研究较为碎片化、结论零散甚至矛盾等问题, 本文基于视觉元素所传递的象征意义与物理功能差异, 将色彩、图像、字体、标识、立体形态与材质等元素归类为图形线索与结构线索, 并系统梳理其对绿色购买、可持续使用与循环处置等行为的影响。为推进视觉线索作用机制的结构化研究, 本文借鉴可持续消费决策中的合意性与可行性考量, 从意义价值评估与执行可能性判断两个维度, 构建视觉线索影响可持续消费的解释框架。具体而言, 图形线索主要通过合意性路径发挥作用, 概念隐喻与认知图式等机制具有较强解释力; 结构线索主要通过可行性路径发挥作用, 可供性与自动分类等机制具有较强解释力。此外, 为丰富视觉线索作用效果的边界研究, 本文从个体层、产品层与环境层挖掘影响视觉线索效应的调节因素。未来可进一步比较两类线索的相对效应, 拓展视觉线索的分类维度, 深入探讨可持续消费行为的多样化表现, 并在数字化场景与互动媒介中推进多感官整合研究。

latest.title: Prior brand cognition and behavioral intention: omnichannel experience and consumer trust as complementary psychological pathways
latest.abstract: Restaurant consumers increasingly encounter brands across interconnected online and offline touchpoints, yet less is known about how prior brand knowledge relates to the interpretation of these encounters and subsequent decision making. Drawing on customer-based brand equity, schema-based information processing, customer-journey research, and trust theory, this study examines a cognition–experience–trust–behavior model. Survey data were collected from 510 restaurant consumers in three Chinese cities who had used at least two channels of a focal restaurant brand. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling were conducted in R/lavaan, and indirect effects were assessed using 10,000 bootstrap resamples. Cognitive brand equity was positively associated with omnichannel experience and consumer trust. Omnichannel experience was positively associated with trust and behavioral intention, while trust showed the strongest proximal association with behavioral intention. All three specific indirect effects were significant, including the sequential pathway through omnichannel experience and trust, and the model explained 52.2% of the variance in behavioral intention. The findings are consistent with two complementary psychological routes: a practical route related to reduced interactional friction and a diagnostic route in which coherent cross-channel experiences provide cues associated with trust. Given the cross-sectional design, these pathways are interpreted as theory-guided associations rather than established causal processes.

latest.title: Self-identity and cool destinations: An interpretative phenomenological analysis of Chinese youth travellers
latest.venue: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Management
latest.abstract: This research investigates the relationship between cool destinations and self-identity in the Chinese context and the role of the “coolness” phenomenon in tourism destination marketing. In doing so, this study explores how Chinese youth travellers construct their identity through their lived experiences in cool destinations. Interpretative phenomenological analysis is employed to investigate young travellers’ narratives of visiting destinations they perceived as “cool”. Findings reveal that cool destinations serve as spaces for self-discovery and as a self-reflective mirror, where encounters with divergent social realities prompted participants to reassess their identity in everyday life. How travellers negotiate between individual self-identity and their social identity is evident, and the role of travel in challenging social norms is also revealed. The study advances understanding of the connection between personal and social identity and destination coolness. Implications for understanding youth travel motivations and the symbolic role of cool destinations in identity are presented.

latest.title: CLO 3D VISUALIZATION AND INFLUENCER MARKETING IMPACT ON CONSUMER BUYING BEHAVIOR IN THE FASHION INDUSTRY: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF TRUST, ENGAGEMENT, AND PERSONALIZATION
latest.abstract: This study compares the effects of influencer marketing and CLO 3D-based garment visualization on consumers’ purchase intention in the fashion industry. The paper investigates trust and involvement as mechanisms by which both strategies function and estimates the two strategies on six consumer outcomes including personalization. A cross-sectional study involving 250 online fashion shoppers with a prior experience of influencer-marketing and CLO 3D and virtual try-on technology was conducted through purposive and snowball sampling methods. Hypotheses were evaluated by means of hierarchical multiple regression, parallel mediation analysis with Monte Carlo confidence intervals, and Steiger’s tests of difference of dependent correlations. Influence marketing predicted purchase intention (β = .49), as did CLO 3D visualization (β = .56) when both were introduced more than once (β = .31 and β = .43; R² = .39). Trust and engagement were partial mediators of both influences; together, they carried about 58% of influencer marketing influence and about 31% of CLO visualization influence. The connection of the CLO 3D visualization with understanding of the product, personalization, and purchase confidence was considerably stronger than that of influencer marketing with brand attachment and awareness of trends. However, there were no significant differences in the strategies’ overall connections to purchase intention. The cross-sectional self-reported non-probability design does not allow for causal conclusions and generalizability of the findings and the use of experimental and longitudinal approaches is recommended. Fashion brands need to consider both strategies as complementary, mostly by employing influencers in the discovery phase and using CLO 3D visualization in the evaluati

latest.title: The psychology of prestige: how identity, social comparison, and brand attachment shape apple consumer behavior
Organisational ethics and stakeholder loyalty: the role of trust, experience, and engagement in the Colombian food industry
latest.abstract: Purpose Organisational ethics has become increasingly important in shaping stakeholder relationships, particularly in markets where consumers expect firms to demonstrate transparency and social responsibility. While prior research has examined ethical perceptions in branding contexts, less attention has been given to how individual characteristics shape these relationships. This study aims to examine how perceived organisational ethics influences engagement and loyalty in the food industry, using Alpina® as the empirical context, while exploring whether these relationships vary across educational levels. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey was conducted with Colombian consumers of Alpina products. From 472 questionnaires collected, 281 valid responses were retained after screening procedures. The proposed model was tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Bootstrapping and multigroup analysis (MGA) were used to examine differences across educational groups (secondary, university and postgraduate). Measurement reliability and validity were assessed through confirmatory factor analysis. Findings Perceived organisational ethics significantly influences brand engagement and perceived value, which in turn predict loyalty. Customer experience and trust also shape how consumers interpret the organisation’s positioning. MGA reveals significant differences across educational segments, suggesting that educational background influences the cognitive mechanisms through which relational drivers translate into loyalty. Originality/value By introducing educational background as a source of heterogeneity, this study extends research on ethics-driven relationship building and highlights how individual characteristics shape stakeholder

latest.title: INFLUENCE OF BRAND IDENTITY ON CUSTOMER LOYALTY IN SELECTED FAST-FOOD RESTAURANTS IN NAIROBI COUNTY, KENYA
latest.abstract: Purpose of the Study: The purpose of this study was to determine the relationship between brand identity and customer loyalty in selected fast-food restaurants in Nairobi County, Kenya. Methodology: A pragmatist convergent parallel mixed-methods design was used. Five Nairobi sub-counties formed study clusters, with twelve franchised or chained fast-food restaurants randomly selected from each cluster. Data comprised 387 usable customer questionnaires and 31 supervisor interviews. Quantitative data were analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and regression, while interviews were analysed thematically and triangulated with survey findings. Findings: Brand identity recorded an overall mean of 3.71 (SD = 1.141). Brand uniqueness (M = 4.06), distinctiveness (M = 3.96) and trust in consistent quality (M = 3.92) were strongest, while emotional brand connection was weakest (M = 3.15). Brand identity was positively associated with customer loyalty (r = 0.617, p < 0.001) and remained significant in regression (B = 0.275, β = 0.268, t = 7.184, p < 0.001); H₀₄ was rejected. Supervisor interviews highlighted brand trust and promise delivery, halal certification credibility, social-media reputation and loyalty recognition as mechanisms supporting customer commitment. Conclusion: Brand identity has a statistically significant positive correlation with customer loyalty. The level of trust, reputation, distinctiveness, and uniqueness is relatively high, while the depth of emotional connection is less developed. When actual restaurant experiences consistently verify the brand promise, brand credibility is enhanced. Recommendation: Fast-food operators should align brand promises with actual experience, strengthen emotional brand connection, communicate credible halal c

latest.title: Lipstick Effect Gen Z: Hubungan Tiktok Exposure Dan Ewom Terhadap Konsumsi
latest.abstract: Penelitian ini mengkaji lipstick effect pada perempuan Generasi Z di Kabupaten Sikka dengan membedakan dimensi emosional dan konsumsi serta menganalisis keterkaitannya dengan electronic word of mouth (e-WOM) dan TikTok exposure. Penelitian kuantitatif dilakukan terhadap 130 responden dengan purposive sampling. Data dianalisis menggunakan statistik deskriptif, korelasi Pearson, dan regresi berganda. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa self-reward motivation (4,08) dan emotional gratification (4,02) merupakan dimensi paling dominan, sedangkan consumption prioritization terendah (2,98). TikTok exposure berhubungan signifikan dengan seluruh dimensi lipstick effect, sementara e-WOM hanya signifikan pada emotional gratification dan self-reward motivation. Secara keseluruhan, TikTok exposure memiliki hubungan lebih kuat dengan lipstick effect (r=0,676) dibandingkan e-WOM (r=0,567). Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa lipstick effect lebih menonjol sebagai fungsi emosional konsumsi daripada perilaku konsumtif. Temuan ini memberikan implikasi strategis bagi pelaku industri kecantikan untuk memformulasikan strategi pemasaran digital berbasis pendekatan psikologis dan nilai pemenuhan emosional

latest.title: Peran Pengalaman Merek dan Keterikatan Merek terhadap Niat Beli Ulang Minuman Cokelat Malt Merek Ovaltine di Kota Ambon
latest.venue: Jurnal Bisnis dan Manajemen West Science
latest.abstract: Penelitian bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran pengalaman merek dan keterikatan merek terhadap niat beli ulang produk susu dalam kemasan merek ovaltine di kota Ambon, Populasi adalah masyarakat kota Ambon dengan jumlah 143 responden dengan teknik penarikan sampel purposive sampling. Teknik analisis data menggunakan regresi berganda dengan hasil yang didapat adalah Berdasarkan hasil pengujian, variabel Pengalaman Merek memperoleh nilai koefisien regresi sebesar 0,170, nilai t hitung sebesar 1,668, dan nilai signifikansi sebesar 0,098. Nilai signifikansi 0,098 lebih besar dari 0,05artinya pengalaman merek berpengaruh positif tetapi tidak signifikan terhadap niat beli ulang produk susu dalam kemasan merek Ovaltine di Kota Ambon. Keterikatan merek memperoleh nilai koefisien regresi sebesar 0,481, nilai t hitung sebesar 6,849, dan nilai signifikansi sebesar 0,000 lebih kecil dari 0,05. Dengan demikian, dapat disimpulkan bahwa keterikatan merek berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap niat beli ulang produk susu dalam kemasan merek Ovaltine di Kota Ambon.

latest.title: Made by humans? Human-AI co-creation, the human-origin premium and brand authenticity in the age of generative AI
latest.abstract: This conceptual paper asks when and why perceived human involvement in AI-assisted brand creation adds relational value, and when co-creation outperforms human-only or AI-only creation. Drawing on research on brand authenticity, human-AI collaboration, creative authorship, effort and presence, signalling and consumer-brand relationships, it develops a dual-pathway framework and seven propositions. The central argument is that consumers judge AI use by inferring who retained consequential judgement over the output, not by asking whether a machine was involved. Distinguishing augmentation from substitution therefore explains why the same level of AI involvement can produce opposite outcomes. A human pathway running through intentionality, effort and presence supports authenticity, while an AI pathway running through competence and consistency supports functional evaluation. Which pathway carries more weight depends on brand type, emotional consequence, transparency and category norms. Because generative assistance makes origin divisible, consumers must allocate credit within a single artefact, and the paper specifies the human-origin premium as a conditional and falsifiable effect of that allocation. It separates what assistance does to the work from what disclosure does to the credit, and distinguishes generic AI labels from role-specific disclosure that reveals consequential human decision rights. For managers, the framework indicates when to preserve and signal human control, when to foreground machine competence and why ceremonial involvement is a liability. The propositions call for experimental and longitudinal testing across categories, cultures and levels of AI involvement.

latest.title: Applications of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Marketing: A Research Review and Future Prospects
latest.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is turning marketing content into an abundant resource with near-zero marginal cost, but related research is highly fragmented. This paper thematically integrates Chinese- and English-language literature published from 2019 to 2026. The findings show that gains from GenAI marketing are “stratified along the funnel”: evidence of improvements at the attention and interaction stages is sufficient, whereas the effect on final conversion is weak; consumers’ evaluations of content are decoupled from evaluations of the “artificial intelligence (AI) source” label, and disclosure of the AI source significantly suppresses transactions; only 13% of the literature examines moderating variables. Accordingly, this paper proposes a five-stage integrated framework of “technical characteristics → marketing applications → psychological mechanisms → consumer responses → moderating boundaries” and a future research agenda.

latest.title: Modeling the moral account: a system dynamics framework for brand-induced moral licensing and behavioral rebound in sustainable consumption
latest.abstract: Introduction Quantitative models of sustainable consumption typically treat consumption as exogenous, assuming that every green purchase improves environmental outcomes. Behavioral research on moral licensing, however, suggests that purchases perceived as virtuous can license compensatory indulgence that erodes some of the benefit. Recent formal work treats licensing as an environmental rebound mechanism in static consumer models; this study contributes the first dynamic stock-and-flow formalization, developed from a recent conceptual framework of brand-induced moral licensing. Methods Four communication pathways (virtue attribution, identity conferral, effort signaling, and absolution framing) feed two moral accounts with opposite mechanics: credits, which deplete when spent, and credentials, which license behavior without being consumed. The model yields closed-form steady states and a licensing-resistance condition on the rebound ratio ρ> (backfire at ρ> 1). Communication parameters were calibrated through a preregistered content analysis of 120 verbatim-archived units from eight sustainable brands, with perfect dual-coder agreement on the reliability subsample; identity internalization was calibrated from a two-country survey of 3,293 adults. The behavioral conversion parameters are literature-anchored or illustrative, so all rebound magnitudes are model-derived, order-of-magnitude results rather than empirical estimates. Results Rebound stays far below backfire: steady-state values span 0.01 to 0.19 across archetypes, preserving 81 to 99% of gross benefit, across 8,000 uncertainty samples and under structural variants allowing credential depletion, sign reversal, and alternative licensing functions. Calibration inverts the theorized risk ordering: identity-position

latest.title: Managing consumer behavior through digital marketing strategies: a comprehensive review
latest.venue: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
latest.abstract: Digital marketing has fundamentally transformed how businesses influence consumer behavior by leveraging tools such as social media, search engine optimization, content marketing, email marketing, and data analytics. This paper provides a comprehensive review of how digital marketing strategies manage consumer behavior, focusing on their impact on consumer engagement, decision-making, and brand loyalty. The purpose of the article is to conduct a comprehensive study of the theoretical and methodological foundations of consumer behavior management in the context of the digitalization of marketing activities, to systematize contemporary digital marketing strategies, and to identify the mechanisms through which they influence the processes of forming, transforming, and forecasting consumer needs, motivations, and behavioral patterns. The methodological foundation of this study consists of a set of general scientific and specialized methods, the application of which ensures a systematic and comprehensive approach to the study of consumer behavior management in the context of the digitalization of marketing activities (in particular, methods of analysis and synthesis, induction and deduction, systematization, comparative analysis, etc.). By synthesizing insights from literature and empirical studies, the study identifies and systematizes the key digital marketing tools, their applications, and their influence on consumer behavior across diverse contexts. The analysis highlights the role of personalization, social media engagement, and data-driven decision-making in fostering consumer trust and brand loyalty. It establishes the correspondence between the stages of the consumer decision-making process – awareness, information search, evaluation, purchase, and post-purchase – an

latest.title: Unequal Brand Outcomes Across Social Media Communication Routes: Evidence from Generation Z

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: Impact of digital transformation on SME’s marketing performance: role of social media and market turbulence
hot.abstract: Despite the rising relevance of digital transformation, there is still a knowledge vacuum due to limited literature available on digital transformation. This study aims to examine the impact of digital transformation on the marketing performance of small and medium enterprises. This research seeks to fill this void by adopting the technology adoption model in order to explore how in a fast-changing technological environment, digital transformation plays its role in firm specific capabilities that are imperative for a firm to adopt, and how they impact firm’s marketing performance. Combination of convenience sampling as well as snowball sampling was used to collect the data. Utilizing survey data from 316 small to medium-sized enterprises in the twin cities (Islamabad & Rawalpindi), Pakistan the results indicate that digital transformation has a positive influence on small and medium enterprises’ marketing performance. This encourages businesses to take advantage of the opportunity presented by new digital technologies and industry-wide digitalization trends by adopting new technologies and improving their digital capabilities in order to increase their productivity, efficiency, and innovation as well as their marketing performance. Hence this study is a practical demonstration of how developing digital transformation may be used to develop novel digital products and services and thereby improve marketing performance that leads to the overall corporate performance. Finally, the study contributes to the literature by evaluating the proposed model that describes the relationships between digital transformation, social media marketing, market turbulence and marketing performance concurrently.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: Understanding Customer Responses to AI-Driven Personalized Journeys: Impacts on the Customer Experience
hot.abstract: Within advertising, the customer journey concept helps explain how customer perceptions and behaviors evolve through seller–customer interactions. The concept has developed to reflect omni-channel marketing but neglects the emergence of algorithmically personalized advertisements. This study therefore explores impacts upon customer experiences of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven recommendations and personalized advertisements by analyzing customer perceptions of tensions between the personalization and customer empowerment inherent within AI-driven advertising. By combining semi-structured phenomenological interviews with Customer Journey Mapping, we capture experiences and behaviors across multiple touchpoints. Our findings show how technological limitations of AI mediate brand–customer relationships and influence customer behaviors. The study contributes theoretically by critically contextualizing AI-driven advertising within broader ethical debates, emphasizing practitioners’ responsibilities to combine technological advancements with consumer autonomy.

hot.title: The Impact of Visual Elements of Packaging Design on Purchase Intention: Brand Experience as a Mediator in the Tea Bag Product Category
hot.abstract: While packaging design plays a vital role in experience-oriented markets, how multiple visual elements influence purchase intention through brand experience remains unclear. This study addresses this gap by employing innovative orthogonal experiments to examine the complex relationship between the visual elements of packaging design and purchase intention for low-involvement products, integrating both design and marketing perspectives. Through orthogonal experimental design, we developed 14 packaging prototypes as stimuli by systematically manipulating five visual elements (Colour, Graphics, Logo, Typography, and Layout). The framework and prototypes were validated through expert evaluation. Data were collected via a cross-sectional survey from 490 tea bag consumers and analysed using SPSS (version 29.0) for preliminary data processing and Mplus (version 8.3) for structural equation modelling. Our results reveal the direct effects of visual packaging elements on consumer purchase intention. Notably, Colour, Graphics, Logo, and Layout significantly influence purchase intention through brand experience mediation. Importantly, our multi-level analysis of visual elements unveils distinct patterns in how different design levels (e.g., colour harmony, graphic types) affect consumer responses. This study provides novel theoretical insights into how consumers make purchase decisions based on packaging design visual elements, addressing a significant gap in existing research. Unlike previous studies focusing on isolated design elements, our systematic classification and multi-level analysis offer both theoretical insights into packaging design mechanisms and practical guidelines for designers and practitioners.

hot.title: The Impact of Green Perceived Value Through Green New Products on Purchase Intention: Brand Attitudes, Brand Trust, and Digital Customer Engagement
hot.abstract: This study examines how the introduction of green new products (GNPs) by luxury brands contributes to building brand equity (i.e., brand attitude and trust) through green perceived value (GPV) and empirically assesses its impact on consumers’ purchase intentions. Furthermore, it explores the moderating role of digital customer engagement (DCE) in the relationship between GPV and building brand equity. To verify the hypothesis, we performed the partial least squares structural equation model (PLS-SEM) as an analytical technique using 572 datasets from luxury consumers in China. The results revealed that GPV through GNPs significantly influences both brand attitude and brand trust. In addition, brand attitude and brand trust were found to have a significantly positive effect on purchase intention. Moreover, DCE was observed to positively moderate the relationship between GPV and brand trust. To enhance the purchase intentions for luxury brands, it is essential to foster brand attitude and brand trust by developing a multidimensional GPV through GNPs. Furthermore, DCE plays a crucial role in strengthening the brand trust component of GPV.

hot.title: Impact of Influencer Marketing on Consumer Behavior and Online Shopping Preferences
hot.venue: Journal of theoretical and applied electronic commerce research
hot.abstract: Influencer marketing has emerged as a crucial element in digital marketing, significantly shaping consumer behavior and online shopping preferences. This study examined the multidimensional impact of influencer marketing by analyzing engagement metrics, marketing effectiveness, and consumer decision-making processes, based on consumers in the Greek sector. Through a structured methodological framework, the research employed a questionnaire-based survey, statistical modeling, and Fuzzy Cognitive Mapping (FCM) scenarios to assess consumer interactions with influencer-driven content. Findings highlight that while influencer marketing enhances brand engagement and sales, its effectiveness varies based on content authenticity, transparency, and user trust. Additionally, consumer purchasing decisions are influenced by social media visibility, personalized marketing strategies, and digital platform usability. This study underscores the need for strategic influencer selection and information-driven marketing optimization to sustain long-term consumer engagement. These insights provide practical implications for businesses aiming to enhance digital marketing strategies and contribute to the ongoing discourse on social commerce and consumer-centric marketing models.

hot.title: Influence of short video content on consumers purchase intentions on social media platforms with trust as a mediator
hot.abstract: Short videos on social media platforms have boomed with the rapid growth of the video consumption industry and have become an important marketing tool for businesses. With the rise of platforms such as TikTok or Douyin, short videos have profoundly impacted consumer behavior, making it crucial to understand their role in shaping consumer purchase intention. However, there is still a need for further research on how short video content promotes consumer purchase intent. Based on the Stimulus-Organism-Response (SOR) model, this study constructs a structural model to explore the impact of short video content on consumer purchase intention, focusing on the mediating role of consumer trust. The model incorporates usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment as external stimuli, consumer trust as internal psychological responses, and purchase intention as the final behavioral outcome. This study collected 372 valid data from Chinese consumers through an online questionnaire and empirically analyzed it using structural equation modeling. The study results show that short-form video content's usefulness, ease of use, and entertainment significantly affect consumers' trust and purchase intention. Moreover, consumer trust positively affects purchase intention and mediates the relationship between short video content and purchase behavior. This research extends the application of the SOR model to the context of social media short videos, highlighting the crucial role of consumer trust in shaping consumer purchase decisions. Based on these findings, we propose actionable strategies for businesses to optimize short video content and build consumer trust, ultimately enhancing marketing effectiveness and driving consumer purchases.

hot.title: Guidelines for Theory Selection: The IMPACT Framework
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT Though the role of adopting an appropriate theory in shaping the publishability and impact of research has long been recognized, psychology and marketing researchers lack specific guidance on how to choose a theory to frame their work. Addressing this gap in the literature, this article proposes a set of guidelines for the selection of relevant macro‐foundational theory to guide research projects addressing specific meso‐ or micro‐foundational theoretical entities (e.g., constructs or individual decision‐making) for research impact. Specifically, we develop a set of six guidelines to select an appropriate macro‐foundational theory for research impact, including Interestingness , Matching , Parsimony , Applicability , Conceptual rigor , and Testability (collectively abbreviated as the “IMPACT” guidelines). We next depict the proposed guidelines in an organizing framework that specifies Matching , the theoretical co ‐infusion of the studied micro‐ or meso‐foundational theoretical entity and the chosen macro‐foundational theory, as the central action item for researchers to shape the impact of their work. Researchers are then advised to use the five remaining guidelines to assess the quality of their proposed Matching for research impact. We conclude by discussing pertinent implications that arise from our analyses (e.g., to ensure Interestingness , we recommend researchers to select a macro‐foundational theory that refutes (vs. affirms) prior findings).

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Marketing Within the Framework of Sustainable Management
hot.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not only revolutionizing digital marketing through personalized customer experiences and optimized advertising strategies, but it is also contributing to sustainability initiatives. As AI reshapes digital marketing, its impact on sustainability is becoming increasingly significant. This dynamic highlights the necessity of exploring how AI can be utilized to foster more sustainable marketing practices.
